msp objects.name: mc.stash~
msp objects.digest: Store and Recall Audio Signal Values (multichannel)
msp objects.description: Use the stash~ object to store and recall a buffer of signal values. In one mode, stash~ can perform sample-and-hold operations on an input signal but unlike the sah~, stash~ reads from a buffer rather than holds a single sample. stash~ can be a simple interpolating lookup table or audio-rate step sequencer.

inletlist.description: Values from a signal are captured when store~ triggers a write. Float values are written to the object's buffer at the current write index.
In the second inlet, a signal can trigger a sample capture. A float sets the threshold level for signal capture.

In the third inlet, a signal triggers advancing the playback to the next value in the buffer according to the current playback direction, or serves as an index into the buffer for table-based playback. A float sets the threshold level for advancing to the next value.
In the right inlet, both a signal and float set the position (write index) where the next input value will be stored.

outletlist.description: The left outlet produces a signal of stepped or interpolated values from the buffer.
The right outlet outputs the buffer index for the current value of the left outlet.

arguments.name: sample-thresh
arguments.description: If present, a float sets the initial threshold value for writing a signal value into the buffer (samplelevel).

arguments.name: advance-thresh
arguments.description: If a second float argument is present, it sets the initial threshold value for advancing to the next value in the buffer (advancelevel).

methods.name: bang
methods.description: In left inlet: the bang message does nothing.In second inlet: if there is a signal connected to the left inlet and there is not a signal connected to the second inlet, a bang in the second inlet causes the first sample of the next signal vector to be captured according to the current writemode.In third inlet: if there is not a signal connected to the third inlet, a bang advances the output.In right inlet: advances the index used for writing samples either for a float in the left inlet or when there isn't a signal connected to the right inlet.

methods.name: int
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: float
methods.description: In left inlet: the value is written to the buffer at the current write index.In second inlet: sets the threshold value for capturing signals connected to the left inlet (samplelevel).In third inlet: sets the threshold value for a signal connected to the third inlet to advance the output (advancelevel).In right inlet: if a signal is not connected to this inlet, sets the current index for writing into the buffer for signal capture. A number in the right inlet also sets the index used to store a float sent to the left inlet.

methods.name: list
methods.digest: In left inlet: sets the buffer contents and size
methods.description: list received in the left inlet sets the contents of the buffer and sets its size to the length of the list. The maximum length of the list that will be used is set by the maxsize attribute.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: signal values are captured to the bufferIn second inlet: used to trigger capturing values from the signal connected to the left inletIn third inlet: depending on the setting of the mode attribute, a connected signal triggers advancing to the next item in the output buffer or is used as an index into the buffer to determine the output.In right inlet: sets the write index used when capturing signal values.

attributes.name: advancelevel
attributes.description: Sets the signal value that will trigger advancing the output to the next value in the buffer. The advancelevel value applies when the advancetriggermode attribute is set to Ascending, Descending, or Ascending or Descending).

attributes.name: advancetriggermode
attributes.description: Determines how a signal connected to the third inlet is interpreted for changing the signal output of stash~ when it is advancing to the next value in the buffer when mode is set to 0 (Next).

attributes.name: dir
attributes.description: Sets the direction in which stash advances through its buffer when mode is set to 0 (Next).

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: When the duration attribute is a non-zero value, the output signal remains at its new value for that number of samples, then resets to 0. Set duration to 1 to generate impulses. When duration is 0, the output value is held constant.

attributes.name: extend
attributes.description: The extend attribute controls how stash~ responds when an input index value (either signal or float) is less than zero or greater than the buffer size.

attributes.name: interp
attributes.description: Determines the interpretation of non-integer index values from signals or the index attribute.

attributes.name: maxsize
attributes.description: Sets the maximum buffer size. Note that maxsize can only be changed when the stash~ object is created as a typed-in argument. The default buffer size is 1000.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Sets how the signal connected to the third inlet determines the buffer index of the output value.

attributes.name: samplelevel
attributes.description: Sets the signal value that will trigger sampling the signal connected to the left input. The samplelevel value applies when the sampletriggermode attribute is set to Ascending, Descending, or Ascending or Descending).

attributes.name: sampletriggermode
attributes.description: Determines how a signal connected to the second inlet is interpreted for capturing the value of a signal connected to the left inlet. The sampletriggermode applies when the writemode is set to Next.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Sets the buffer size, which can range from 1 to the value of maxsize. Note: a list received in the left inlet sets the size to the size of the list.

attributes.name: writemode
attributes.description: The writemode attribute controls how the signal connected to the left inlet is captured (sampled). There are two aspects to capturing a signal: when it happens, and where the sample goes once it is captured. Logically, if you want to continue capturing to the same index, you need another signal that changes, because the index signal is not changing so it cannot provide triggering information.

msp objects.name: mc.sash~
msp objects.description: The sash~ object performs sample-and-hold operations on an input signal but unlike the sah~ includes a buffer (the extra "s" in sash~ is for "storage") that can holds samples of the input. Sample capture and sample output are triggered independently of each other, and sash~ includes a variety of methods for selecting the output sample from the memory buffer.

inletlist.description: The input signal to be sampled
Signal that triggers the sampling the input
Signal that advances to the next sample in the memory buffer

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: int
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Set sample trigger or advance level
methods.description: A float in the middle inlet sets the sample trigger level. A float in the right set the level for advancing to the next output value from the memory buffer.

methods.name: list
methods.description: A list of values is assigned to the memory buffer. This is useful when there is no signal connected to the sample trigger (middle) inlet. The size of the list can not be larger than the buffer size (maxsize attribute), and the new output size is set to the number of items in the list.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: A signal in the left inlet is sampled, triggered by the value of the signal in the middle inlet. The signal connected to the right inlet triggers sash~ to advance to the next output sample from the memory buffer. This happens when sample exceeds the  the advancelevel when the mode is set to Advance. When the mode is set to Index, the output sample changes when the integer value of the input changes. When the mode is set to Subdivision, the output sample changes when the input value, divided by the current size, reaches the next divisor.

attributes.name: advancelevel
attributes.description: Sets the level of the signal connected to the right inlet that will cause the next value in the memory buffer to be used. The next index into the buffer is chosen according to the dir attribute.

attributes.name: dir
attributes.description: Determines how the next memory buffer index is chosen when the advance trigger signal exceeds the advance level.

attributes.name: maxsize
attributes.description: Sets the maximum possible value of the size attribute. The default is 1000 samples. Note that maxsize can only be changed as a typed-in argument.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Determines the interpretation of the advance trigger signal

attributes.name: samplelevel
attributes.description: Sets the level of the signal connected to the middle inlet that will cause the next value in the left inlet to be sampled and recorded into the memory buffer.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Sets the current size of the memory buffer used for recording and output. The size must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to the maxsize attribute.

msp objects.description: Use the /~ object is to multiply a signal coming into the left inlet by the reciprocal of either the initial argument or an int or float received in the right inlet.

arguments.name: initial-divisor
arguments.description: Sets an initial value by which to divide the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is connected to the right inlet, the argument is ignored. If no argument is present, and no signal is connected to the right inlet, the initial value is 1 by default.

methods.name: int
methods.description: In left inlet: The number is divided by the signal coming into the right inlet. If a signal is connected to both left and right inlets, a float or int connected to either inlet will be ignored.In right inlet: A number by which to divide the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is connected to both left and right inlets, a float or int connected to either inlet will be ignored.

methods.name: float
methods.description: In left inlet: The number is divided by the signal coming into the right inlet. If a signal is connected to both left and right inlets, a float or int connected to either inlet will be ignored.In right inlet: A number by which to divide the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is connected to both left and right inlets, a float or int connected to either inlet will be ignored.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The signal is divided by a signal coming into the right inlet, or a constant value received in the right inlet. All signal inputs to a single inlet are summed. If a signal and number are both sent to the left inlet, the specified operation will be performed with those values.In right inlet: The signal is used as the divisor, to be divided into the signal coming into the left inlet, or the constant value received in the left inlet. All signal inputs to a single inlet are summed.

msp objects.name: stutter~
msp objects.digest: Signal capture buffer for granular playback
msp objects.description: The stutter~ object keeps a history of its signal input (left inlet). Upon receiving an int (left inlet), it copies that number of the most recently received samples to another playback buffer. This buffer may be cycled through by its phase, 0-1 (right inlet). On receiving a bang (left inlet) or a trigger signal (middle inlet), the last integer number of samples are copied to the playback buffer.

arguments.name: max-buffer-length
arguments.description: The maximum buffer length, in samples. This determines the memory size of the record buffer. Parts of the record buffer are copied to the playback buffer when the object is triggered.

arguments.name: initial-buffer-size
arguments.description: The initial buffer size, in samples, to copy from the record to the playback buffer upon receiving a trigger.

arguments.name: trigger-polarity
arguments.description: The polarity to use for accepting a trigger signal in the middle inlet. If the argument is greater than 0, stutter~ accepts a positive trigger; otherwise stutter~ accepts a negative trigger.

arguments.name: number-of-copied-samples
arguments.digest: Number of samples copied from record to playback
arguments.description: The number of samples which are copied from the record buffer to the playback buffer each iteration of the perform loop (the signal vector size). A larger value will decrease the stutter~ object's memory requirements and increase the CPU requirements.

arguments.name: number-of-outputs
arguments.description: An optional fifth argument allows you to specify multiple independent signal outputs the stutter~ object will use when playing back from the playback buffer. The default is 1, and the maximum is 30. The number of phase signal inputs to the stutter~ object is also determined by this argument.

methods.name: bang
methods.digest: Copy last buffer to the playback buffer
methods.description: In left inlet: A bang causes the last buffer of recorded samples to be copied to the playback buffer. You can use a bang instead of or in conjunction with the middle inlet trigger signal.

methods.name: int
methods.description: In left inlet: Specifies the size (in samples) of the playback buffer. This can be any number up to the maximum memory determined by the first argument to stutter~.

methods.name: ampvar
methods.digest: Set random amplitude variation in signal output
methods.description: The word ampvar, followed by a float, specifies a random amplitude variation in the output signal(s). The default is 0 (no variation).

methods.name: clear
methods.description: Clears the object's sample memory.

methods.name: dropout
methods.digest: Set the percentage chance of dropout on playback
methods.description: The word dropout, followed by a float, determines the percentage chance of a playback signal dropping out (i.e. 'gapping' or not playing). The default is 0 (no gapping).

methods.name: maxsize
methods.description: The word maxsize, followed by a number, sets the maximum buffer size, in samples.

methods.name: polarity
methods.description: The word polarity, followed by a zero or one, changes the trigger polarity of stutter~ to negative or positive, respectively.

methods.name: print
methods.digest: Print all parameter settings to the Max Console
methods.description: The word print will cause the object to print a detailed listing of all of its parameter settings within the Max Console.

methods.name: repeat
methods.digest: Set the percentage chance of repeat on playback
methods.description: The word repeat, followed by a float, determines the percentage change of the record buffer not being copied to the playback buffer so that the previous playback buffer is repeated. The default is 0 (no repeat).

methods.name: setbuf
methods.digest: Copy samples to a named buffer~ object
methods.description: The word setbuf, followed by arguments for a buffer name, a sample offset, and a channel, copies the specified samples to the named buffer~ object. Note: stutter~ always uses its internal buffer as the playback buffer; the copied samples can be sent to a named buffer~ object for use in some other way, if desired. The time required to move the specified amount of memory to the buffer is n/m, there n is the number of samples being copied and m is the fourth argument to the stutter~ object.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: Signals coming into the left inlet are stored in a record buffer, where they can be copied into a playback buffer and used as a playback source.In middle inlet: Accepts a trigger signal, which can be specified to be positive or negative. When the signal changes polarity in the correct direction, samples recorded from the left inlet are copied to the playback buffer.In right and successive inlets: A phase signal input in the range of 0-1 for each inlet controls the output speed of the playback buffer for that inlet. The number of phase inlets in a stutter~ object is set using the fifth argument; the default is a single inlet. Specifying multiple phase inlets allows you to specify multiple playback points in the sampled buffer.

msp objects.description: +=~ adds all the values it receives. The result can grow very large, very fast.

msp objects.name: mc.>~

msp objects.description: >~ outputs a 1 signal when the left input is greater-than the right input and a 0 when it is less-than or equal-to the right input. The right input can be a signal or a float.

arguments.name: initial-comparison-value
arguments.description: Sets an initial comparison value for the signal coming into the left inlet. 1 is sent out if the signal is greater than the argument; otherwise, 0 is sent out. If a signal is connected to the right inlet, the argument is ignored. If no argument is present, and no signal is connected to the right inlet, the initial value is 0 by default.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Compare value with left input signal
methods.description: In right inlet: A number to be used for comparison with the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is also connected to the right inlet, a float or int is ignored.

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Compare value with left input signal
methods.description: In right inlet: A number to be used for comparison with the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is also connected to the right inlet, a float or int is ignored.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The signal is compared to a signal coming into the right inlet, or a constant value received in the right inlet. If it is greater than the value in the right inlet, 1 is sent out; otherwise, 0 is sent out.In right inlet: The signal is used for comparison with the signal coming into the left inlet.

msp objects.name: minimum~
msp objects.digest: Compare two signals, output the minimum
msp objects.description: minimum~ outputs a signal which is the minimum of two input signals.

inletlist.digest: (signal) Signal to be compared with Right Inlet
(signal) Signal to be compared with Left Inlet

outletlist.digest: (signal) Minimum of Left and Right Signals

arguments.name: initial-comparison-value
arguments.description: Sets an initial comparison value for the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is connected to the right inlet, the argument is ignored.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Compare value with left input signal
methods.description: In right inlet: A number to be used for comparison with the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is also connected to the right inlet, a float or int is ignored.

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Compare value with left input signal
methods.description: In right inlet: A number to be used for comparison with the signal coming into the left inlet. If a signal is also connected to the right inlet, a float or int is ignored.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The signal is compared to a signal coming into the right inlet, or a constant value received in the right inlet. The lesser of the two values is sent out the outlet.In right inlet: The signal is used for comparison with the signal coming into the left inlet.

msp objects.name: mc.cell
msp objects.digest: Format messages from a jit.cellblock for use with MC objects
msp objects.description: The mc.cell objects takes a <column row value> message from the left outlet of the jit.cellblock object and produces a corresponding setvalue message for use with MC objects to set a value for a specific channel. Since jit.cellblock column numbers are 0-relative and MC channel numbers are 1-relative, mc.cell adds 1 to the incoming column number.

methods.name: list
methods.description: mc.cell accepts a list in the form <col-number row-number value> and outputs a message in the form setvalue<col-number+1 value>.

attributes.name: columns
attributes.description: Offsets the cell values for each row after the first by the specified number of columns. Typically this should be set to the same number of columns as the jit.cellblock feeding mc.cell. The default value for columns is 0, which causes no offset.

attributes.name: constant
attributes.description: When set, applies the specified channel to any incoming data, overriding the channel supplied by the input list.

attributes.name: message
attributes.description: Inserts any message after the column and before the value of all lists output by mc.cell. Useful for setting the value of an interal attribute of an MC object. Output lists are formatted as setvalue<olumn message value>.

attributes.name: numeric
attributes.description: Enable the numeric attribute to filter out non-numeric text (defaults to on). When off, cells will pass non-numeric values as well. Non-numeric text could be useful for entering the name of a buffer~ object or media file.

attributes.name: row
attributes.description: Use the row attribute to specify a row to read into the mc.cell object.

msp objects.name: mc.sah~
msp objects.description: Use sah~ to capture ("sample") and output ("hold") a value from an input signal whenever a trigger signal satisfies a threshold value according to one of several trigger conditions. The default trigger mode (Ascending) requires the signal to go from being at or below the threshold value to above it. At the moment the trigger condition is satisfied, the input signal is sampled and "held" until the trigger condition is satisfied again, at which point the input is sampled again. Generally this allows one signal to be synchronized to the behavior of another.

inletlist.digest: Values To Sample, double Sets Trigger Threshold

methods.name: float
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: A signal to be sampled. When the trigger signal (in the right inlet) satisfies the current trigger condition, the signal in the left inlet is sampled and its value is sent out as a constant signal value.In right inlet: The trigger signal.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: Normally the signal output of sah~ remains constant. With a non-zero value for duration any new non-zero value will remain constant for a specified number samples, after which it will be 0.

attributes.name: thresh
attributes.description: Sets the value of the trigger signal used to cause the input signal to be sampled and output.

attributes.name: triggermode
attributes.description: Determines how sah~ analyzes the trigger signal to cause the input to be sampled and output. The classic (and default) triggermode is 0 (Ascending).

msp objects.name: bitxor~
msp objects.digest: Bitwise exclusive-or-operation of floating point signals
msp objects.description: Use the bitxor~ object to perform a bitwise "exclusive or" operation on two incoming floating-point signals as either raw 32-bit data or as integer values. The bits of both incoming signals are compared, and the corresponding output bit will be set to 1 if the two bit values are different, and 0 if the two values are the same. The output is a floating-point signal composed of the resulting bit pattern.

arguments.name: bitmask
arguments.digest: Bitmask to be used by the bitxor~ object
arguments.description: Sets the bitmask to be used by the bitxor~ object. The default is 0. An integer value can be used as a bitmask regardless of the mode; the binary representation of this integer is the bitmask.

arguments.name: operational-mode
arguments.digest: Processing mode for floating signal/floating-point values
arguments.description: Specifies whether the floating-point signal or floating-point value will be processed as a raw 32-bit floating-point value or converted to an integer value for bit inversion. The modes of operation are listed below.0: Treat floating-point signal input as a raw 32-bit value (default).1: Convert the floating-point signal input to an integer value.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Use an integer value as a bitmask
methods.description: In right inlet: An integer value can be used as a bitmask when supplied to the right inlet of the bitxor~ object, provided that the proper mode is set.

methods.name: bits
methods.digest: In left inlet: The word bits, followed by a list containing 32 ones or zeros, specifies a bitmask to be used by bitxor~
methods.description: In left inlet: The word bits, followed by a list containing 32 ones or zeros, specifies a bitmask to be used by bitxor~. Alternately, a bitmask value can be set by using an int value in the right inlet.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The floating-point signal is compared, in binary form, with the floating-point signal in the right inlet. The signal can be treated as either a floating-point signal or as an integer.In right inlet: The floating-point signal to be compared with the signal in the left inlet. The signal can be treated as either a floating-point signal or as an integer.The raw floating-point signal bit values are expressed in the following form:<1 sign bit> <8 exponent bits> <23 mantissa bits>

attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Processing mode for floating signal/floating-point values
attributes.description: Specifies whether the floating-point signal or floating-point value will be processed as a raw 32-bit floating-point value or converted to an integer value for bit inversion. The modes of operation are listed below.0: Treat floating-point signal input as a raw 32-bit value (default).1: Convert the floating-point signal input to an integer value.

msp objects.name: mc.what~
msp objects.digest: Generate Impulses for a List of Audio Values (multichannel)
msp objects.description: The what~ object generates an impulse -- a signal value of 1 for one sample -- when its input signal crosses a value threshold. The object accepts a list of threshold values and will generate impulses for all of them. Connect a phasor~ to what~ to create a repeating rhythm. For example, when sending in a list of 0 0.25 0.5 and 0.75, what~ will output an impulse four times for each phasor~ ramp.

inletlist.description: A signal containing or ramping through values you want to detect

outletlist.description: what outputs 0 until it detects a matching value in its input, then it outputs 1 for one sample.

arguments.name: values
arguments.digest: One or more values to detect
arguments.description: If one or more values are arguments to what~ they define the initial list of values.

methods.name: int
methods.description: An int sets a single value to detect, replacing any existing values.

methods.name: float
methods.description: An float sets a single value to detect, replacing any existing values.

methods.name: list
methods.description: list sets the new values to detect, replacing any existing values. A list message is alternative to setting the matches attribute. If syncupdate is enabled, the new values are not used until the input phasor resets.

methods.name: clear
methods.description: The clear message removes all values that have been added to the what~ object. If syncupdate is enabled, the values are not cleared until the input phasor resets.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: The input signal used for theshold analysis, usually a phasor, though any signal can be used.

attributes.name: matches
attributes.description: Sets the values to detect

attributes.name: syncupdate
attributes.description: When syncupdate is enabled, messages to change the values to detect do not take effect until the input phasor resets. A reset is defined as a direction reversal in the signal.

attributes.name: triggermode
attributes.description: Determines how what~ matches values in the signal input.

msp objects.name: degrade~
msp objects.description: degrade~ takes any given signal and reduces the sampling rate and bit-depth as specified/desired.

arguments.name: resampling-frequency-ratio
arguments.description: The first argument sets the resampling frequency ratio, as described above. If this argument is not supplied, the default value is 1.0.

arguments.name: number-of-quantization-bits
arguments.description: The second argument sets the number of bits used to quantize the input signal. If this argument is not supplied, the default value is 24.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Set the number of quantization bits
methods.description: In right inlet: The number of bits used to quantize the input signal. This value must be in the range 1-52. Fewer bits mean lower signal quality.

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Set the frequency ratio at which the signal is resampled
methods.description: In middle inlet: The ratio of frequency at which the input signal is resampled, effectively reducing its sampling rate. This ratio is the resampling rate divided by the system sampling rate. For example, if MSP"s current sampling rate is 44100 Hz, and the ratio is 0.75, the effective sampling rate of the output signal will be 33075 Hz.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The signal to be degraded.

msp objects.name: mc.freqshift~

arguments.description: A numerical argument will be used as the frequency shift in Hertz. The default is zero.

arguments.name: frequency-shift
arguments.description: A numerical argument will be used as the frequency shift in Hertz. The default is zero. .

methods.name: float

methods.name: clear

methods.name: resetphase
