msp objects.name: mc.onepole~
msp objects.description: The onepole~ object implements the simplest of IIR filters, providing a 6dB per octave attenuation. This filter is very efficient and useful for gently rolling off harsh high end and for smoothing out control signals.

arguments.name: center-frequency
arguments.description: Sets the center frequency for the filter, as described above.

arguments.name: Hz/linear/radians
arguments.description: Using the symbols Hz, linear, or radians for an optional second argument sets the frequency input mode. The default mode is Hz (which is the same as providing no mode argument). Using the linear argument sets the frequency input mode to linear (0 - 1). Using the radians argument sets the frequency input mode to radians (0 - 1).

methods.name: int
methods.description: In right inlet: Sets the frequency for the filter (if no signal is connected). By default, frequency is expressed in Hz, where the allowable range is from 0 to one fourth of the current sampling rate. For convenience, onepole~ has two additional input modes that use the more conventional input range, 0 - 1 (see the linear and radians messages).

methods.name: float
methods.description: In right inlet: Sets the frequency for the filter (if no signal is connected). By default, frequency is expressed in Hz, where the allowable range is from 0 to one fourth of the current sampling rate. For convenience, onepole~ has two additional input modes that use the more conventional input range, 0 - 1 (see the linear and radians messages).

methods.name: Hz
methods.digest: Set the frequency input mode to Hz.
methods.description: In either inlet: Sets the frequency input mode to Hz (the default).

methods.name: clear
methods.description: In either inlet: Clears the internal state of onepole~. Since onepole~ does not have the inherent instability of other filter types, this should never be necessary.

methods.name: linear
methods.digest: Set the frequency input mode to linear
methods.description: In either inlet: Sets the frequency input mode to linear (0 - 1). Linear mode is simply a scaled version of the standard Hz mode, except that values in the 0-1 range traverses the full frequency range.

methods.name: radians
methods.digest: Set the frequency input mode to radians
methods.description: In either inlet: Sets the frequency input mode to radians (0 - 1). Radians mode lets you set the center frequency (f_c) of the equation directly, while the input has the same range (0-1), the output has a curved frequency response that is closer to the exponential pitch scale of the human ear.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: Signal to be filtered.In right inlet: A signal can be used to set the frequency for the filter, with the same effect as a float. If a signal is connected to this inlet, its value is sampled once every signal vector.

msp objects.name: mc.chord~
msp objects.digest: Store and Recall Signal Values Associated with an Index
msp objects.description: The mc.chord~ object is something like a version of the Max coll object that generates audio signals. You can store lists (which you can think of as chords) of numbers associated with a unique index, then recall your lists with messages or signals. When recalled, list values are assigned to channels in a multi-channel signal according to one of several allocation modes.

inletlist.description: A signal connected to mc.chord~ recalls stored lists according to the current inputmode. You can also store or recall values using messages.

outletlist.description: A multi-channel signal containing the values of the most recently recalled list. The assignment of list values to channels is set by the allocmode attribute. If offmode is set to zero, unused channels will be set to zero, otherwise they contain values from previously recalled lists.
If a channel in the left outlet is currently allocated to a list value, the corresponding channel in the second outlet will be 1, otherwise it will be 0.

When a stored list in mc.chord~ is recalled, it will be sent out the third outlet. The order of the list is the order the values were initially stored, which may not correpond to the order they appear in the channels of the left outlet depending on the current setting of allocmode.
When a list is recalled, its index is sent out the right outlet.

arguments.name: channels
arguments.description: An int supplied as an argument sets the initial output channel count.

methods.name: bang
methods.description: bang outputs the next stored list as a multi-channel signal out the left outlet; repeated bang messages will cycle through all stored lists.

methods.name: int
methods.description: An int outputs the list associated with the number as a multi-channel signal out the left outlet. If no list was stored at this number, zero signals are output.

methods.name: float
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: list
methods.description: list stores the items starting at the second value at an index specified by the first value. Example: 5 30 40 50 will store the list 30 40 50 at index 5.

methods.name: clear
methods.description: The clear message clears all lists stored in the object. To delete an individual list using its associated index, use delete.

methods.name: delete
methods.digest: Delete a list associated with an index
methods.description: The word delete followed by an index deletes a list of values associated with that index.

methods.name: dictionary
methods.description: When mc.chord~ receives a dictionary in the proper format, it will replace all stored lists with those in the dictionary. Data must be in the form of an array of dictionaries associated with the key data. Each dictionary has the key index with the index to associate with the list, followed by a list of values associated with the key values.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Output matching lists based on signal values
methods.description: When inputmode is set to Lookup (0), the signal value is truncated to an integer. When this integer value changes, mc.chord~ checks whether it matches an index for a stored list; if so, it outputs the associated list as a multi-channel signal.When inputmode is set to Increment Index (1), any change in the value of the input signal will cause the next stored list to be output in a cyclic fashion.

methods.name: store
methods.description: The word store followed by a list argument, stores the items in the list starting at the second value at an index specified by the first value. Example: store 5 30 40 50 will store the list 30 40 50 at index 5.

attributes.name: allocmode
attributes.description: Determine how list values are allocated to channels

attributes.name: busymapname
attributes.description: Sets the name of a busy map (within an mc.noteallocator~ or mc.voiceallocator~ object)to use in determining channel allocation. When there is an active busy map (usebusymap is enabled), items will be assigned to channels accoding to the current allocmode but only non-busy channels will be used. The value none resets the busy map to the default busy map for the patcher.

attributes.name: chans
attributes.description: Sets the number of channels in the two mc.chord~ multi-channel outputs. If the audio is on, the change will take place the next time the audio is restarted.

attributes.name: embed
attributes.description: When embed is enabled, list and index data currently stored inside mc.chord~ will be saved in its patcher and recalled when the patcher is reopened.

attributes.name: extendmode
attributes.description: Sets how non-existent indices are matched or ignored

attributes.name: inputmode
attributes.description: Determines how a signal value change is mapped to an output

attributes.name: offmode
attributes.description: Determines handling of output channels with inactive values

attributes.name: triggermode
attributes.description: Determines a signal change for increment index inputmode

attributes.name: usebusymap
attributes.description: When usebusymap is enabled, mc.chord~ will only allocate output values to non-busy channels of the current busy map.

msp objects.name: omx.comp~
msp objects.description: omx.comp~ is a fully-featured signal compressor with limiting, gating, sidechain, and dual-band options.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: agcEnabled
methods.digest: The word agcEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables the compressor
methods.description: The word agcEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables the compressor.

methods.name: agcThreshold
methods.digest: The word agcThreshold, followed by a number, sets the compressor threshold (in dB below full scale)
methods.description: The word agcThreshold, followed by a number, sets the compressor threshold (in dB below full scale). This is the main compression threshold. Any signal above the threshold will be reduced, and any signal below the threshold will be amplified, according to the range and ratio parameters.

methods.name: attack
methods.digest: The word attack, followed by a number, sets the rate at which the compressor is engaged when the signal level exceeds the agcThreshold
methods.description: The word attack, followed by a number, sets the rate at which the compressor is engaged when the signal level exceeds the agcThreshold. The value range is 0-150 on a logarithmic scale, with larger values indicating faster attack.

methods.name: bypass
methods.digest: The word bypass followed by a non-zero number will output the dry unchanged input signal straight out the outlet without any processing; followed by a 0, will output the signal effected by omx.comp~
methods.description: The word bypass followed by a non-zero number will output the dry unchanged input signal straight out the outlet without any processing; followed by a 0, will output the signal effected by omx.comp~.

methods.name: channelCoupling
methods.digest: The word channelCoupling, followed by a number, sets the gain control source as follows: 0 = stereo, 1 = left, 2 = right
methods.description: The word channelCoupling, followed by a number, sets the gain control source as follows: 0 = stereo, 1 = left, 2 = right. In stereo mode, the gain control signal is derived from whichever channel is loudest, unlike in left or right mode where the gain control signal will only be derived from the selected channel. This can be used for "keying" or "ducking" effects, where the energy of one sound modulates the level of another.

methods.name: choosePreset
methods.description: The word choosePreset, followed by a number in the range 0-4, selects a preset for the omx.comp~ object. These presets are to be considered "starting points" and should be tweaked for your particular purpose or desired sound. The preset options are:0: Guitar1: Bass2: Vocal3: Drums4: Program Material - An attempt at smooth "gain riding" of mixed program material as well as can be done with a non-multiband processor.

methods.name: delay
methods.description: The word delay, followed by a number, sets the sidechain delay time (in milliseconds). This emulates the attack characteristics of vintage "opto" compressors, and similar effects. The delay is applied to the control signal only, and hence may result in large peaks at transients.

methods.name: dualBandEnabled
methods.description: The word dualBandEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0, turns dual band mode on or off. In dual band, a crossover filter around 200hz splits the audio into two bands, which are compressed separately. This can reduce bass pumping and other artifacts of wide-band compression.

methods.name: freezeLevel
methods.digest: The word freezeLevel, followed by a number, sets the freeze threshold (in dB below full scale)
methods.description: The word freezeLevel, followed by a number, sets the freeze threshold (in dB below full scale). When the signal is below this threshold, the compressor release action will be suppressed, and the gain will remain constant. In normal operation, release action takes place when the signal is below the compression threshold, increasing the gain until the signal returns to its full-scale, uncompressed level. If there is no usable signal present, this can have the effect of simply amplifying the noise floor. Release gate and freeze can suppress gain recovery to avoid this condition.

methods.name: gatingLevel
methods.description: The word gatingLevel, followed by a number, sets the release gate threshold (in dB below full scale). When the signal is below this threshold, the release time of the compressor will be slowed by a factor of 3. See freezeLevel.

methods.name: limEnabled
methods.digest: The word limEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0 turns the peak-limiter on or off
methods.description: The word limEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0 turns the peak-limiter on or off.

methods.name: limMode
methods.description: The word limMode, followed by a number, sets the limiter response mode as follows: 0 = punchy, 1 = smooth. Punchy response yields extremely short attack and release times, useful for transparent limiting, or to create loudness. However, if over-used, intermodulation distortion may result. Smooth response uses longer attack and release times. The result is still a fast look-ahead limiter, but with less intermodulation distortion and less punch.

methods.name: meterData
methods.description: The word meterData will cause output (by instantaneous command as opposed to metering-interval described by the meterRate message) of values which describe the current state of various internal gain levels of the compressor, and can be used to drive GUI objects to provide visual feedback. omx.comp~ sends a list of six integers, describing compressor gain (left, right), noise gate gain (left, right), and limiter gain (left, right).

methods.name: meterRate
methods.description: The word meterRate, followed by a number, specifies the interval (in milliseconds) at which the meter data described above will be sent.

methods.name: meters
methods.description: The word meters, followed by a 1 or 0, turns the metering output on or off. When metering is on, a list of values will be sent from the rightmost outlet at a rate specified by the meterRate message. These values describe the current state of various internal gain levels of the compressor, and can be used to drive GUI objects to provide visual feedback. omx.comp~ sends a list of six integers, describing compressor gain (left, right), noise gate gain (left, right), and limiter gain (left, right).

methods.name: ngEnabled
methods.description: The word ngEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0, turns the noise gate on or off. A noise gate is effective for reducing background hiss when no other signal is present. Here, it's implemented as a downward expander with a ratio of 2:1.

methods.name: ngThreshold
methods.digest: Set the noise gate threshold level
methods.description: The word ngThreshold, followed by a number, sets the threshold level (in dB below full scale) at which the noise gate will be engaged.

methods.name: progressiveRelease
methods.description: The word ProgressiveRelease, followed by a number from 0-100, activates Progressive Release, which causes the compressor to release faster during heavy gain reduction. This means that the audio will sound more compressed when the input signal is louder. This can be used to create an illusion of dynamics. It is especially useful with the ratio set to Infinite:1, which could sound over-compressed without this option.

methods.name: range
methods.description: The word range, followed by a number, sets the maximum amount of gain amplification allowed in dB. This limits the gain that is applied when the signal is below the compression threshold. Note that this limiting takes place before the ratio is applied. For example, if the range is set to 24 dB, and the ratio is 2:1, the most gain amplification you can get (after the ratio is applied) is in fact 12 dB.

methods.name: ratio
methods.digest: Sets the numerator of the compressor gain reduction ratio
methods.description: The word ratio, followed by a number, sets the numerator of the compressor gain reduction ratio, from 1:1 to Infinite:1.

methods.name: release
methods.description: The word release, followed by a number, sets the rate at which the compressor releases its gain adjustment when the signal level no longer exceeds the agcThreshold. The value range is 0-150 on a logarithmic scale, with larger values indicating faster release. This rate can be modified by the release gate and freeze thresholds.

methods.name: saveSettings
methods.digest: Send all parameter values out the third outlet
methods.description: The word saveSettings causes all parameter values to be sent out the third outlet.

methods.name: sidechainFilterEnabled
methods.description: The word sidechainFilterEnabled, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables an attenuation filter in the upper midrange that makes the compressor less sensitive to vocal signals, and generally produces a more gentle response. This filter is only applied internally, to the control signal. Note that it may cause more output overshoots, where the signal output level exceeds 0dB.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: Audio input, the signal or pair of signals to be compressed.

methods.name: smoothGain
methods.description: The word smoothGain, followed by a number from 0-100, activates gain smoothing. This applies a low-pass filter to the control signal, and is useful both to prevent artifacts (gain fluttering) from high attack/release rates, and to intentionally make the compressor sluggish, adding extra "snap" to transients.

msp objects.name: mc.pink~
msp objects.description: pink~ generates pink noise, as distinguished from white noise (which the MSP object noise~ generates). White noise has constant spectral power per hertz of bandwidth, while pink noise has constant power per octave. Subjectively, pink noise sounds less hissy than white noise.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

msp objects.name: seq~
msp objects.description: The seq~ object is an event sequencer that is driven by a signal input. seq~ can be used to create looping sequences of control data that are synchronized to a phasor~.

inletlist.digest: phasor~ input, commands, messages to be sequenced

outletlist.digest: id on read, (bang) when done reading

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: bang
methods.digest: Causes information about the seq~ object's current sequence number, mode of operation (record, overdub, play)
methods.description: Causes information about the seq~ object's current sequence number, mode of operation (record, overdub, play) and total number of current events to be printed in the Max window.

methods.name: int
methods.description: Same as anything.

methods.name: float
methods.description: Same as anything.

methods.name: list
methods.description: Same as anything.

methods.name: anything
methods.digest: The seq~ object is used to record and play back messages.
methods.description: The seq~ object is used to record and play back messages. All events received in the inlet are stored according to the current value of the input signal. Any message can be sequenced except for commands to the seq~ object itself. The example shows a simple way to work around this limitation.Note: seq~ can be used to sequence MIDI data if the MIDI input stream is converted into lists of MIDI events. This conversion is necessary to avoid outputting a corrupted MIDI stream which would occur if only the raw int messages of a MIDI stream were sequenced individually and the seq~ object were not doing a simple forward linear playback.

methods.name: add
methods.digest: The word add, followed by an int, a float and a message, inserts a Max event specified by the message at the time specified by the float for the sequence number specified by the int. (e.g., add 2 0.5 honk will insert the message honk to be played at the halfway point of sequence 2.)
methods.description: The word add, followed by an int, a float and a message, inserts a Max event specified by the message at the time specified by the float for the sequence number specified by the int. (e.g., add 2 0.5 honk will insert the message honk to be played at the halfway point of sequence 2.)

methods.name: clear
methods.digest: The word clear, followed by the name of a sequence, erases the sequence.
methods.description: The word clear, followed by the name of a sequence, erases the sequence. The message clear all erases all current sequences.

methods.name: delete
methods.digest: The word delete, followed by an symbol that specifies a sequence name, a float and a message, deletes a Max event or events specified by the message at the time specified by the float for the sequence name specified by the symbol. An additional end time may also be specified. Here are some examples:delete mysequence 5.: delete all the events at time 5 in mysequence.delete mysequence 6.5 8.: delete all the events between time 6.5 and 8 in mysequence.delete mysequence -1. 99. explosion: delete only the event explosion wherever it occurs.
methods.description: The word delete, followed by an symbol that specifies a sequence name, a float and a message, deletes a Max event or events specified by the message at the time specified by the float for the sequence name specified by the symbol. An additional end time may also be specified. Here are some examples:delete mysequence 5.: delete all the events at time 5 in mysequence.delete mysequence 6.5 8.: delete all the events between time 6.5 and 8 in mysequence.delete mysequence -1. 99. explosion: delete only the event explosion wherever it occurs.

methods.name: dump
methods.digest: Causes the contents of the current stored event sequence to be sent out the middle outlet.
methods.description: Causes the contents of the current stored event sequence to be sent out the middle outlet. The word dump, followed by a number, outputs only the sequence designated by the number.

methods.name: erase
methods.description: Synonym for clear.

methods.name: offset
methods.digest: The word offset followed by a number will offset the numbering of sequences by the specified number.
methods.description: The word offset followed by a number will offset the numbering of sequences by the specified number.

methods.name: overdub
methods.digest: The word overdub, followed by 1, causes seq~ to begin Max event recording of the current sequence (set by the seqnum message)
methods.description: The word overdub, followed by 1, causes seq~ to begin Max event recording of the current sequence (set by the seqnum message) in "overdub" mode. Recording begins at the current point of the loop and wraps around at the point where the input signal reaches 1, continuing to record as the signal passes its original value. The message overdub 0 turns off overdub mode.

methods.name: play
methods.digest: The word play, followed by 1, causes seq~ to begin Max event playback of the current sequence (set by the seqnum message)
methods.description: The word play, followed by 1, causes seq~ to begin Max event playback of the current sequence (set by the seqnum message) at the point of the loop specified by the current value of the signal input. play 0 turns off playback. By default, playback is off.

methods.name: read
methods.digest: Reads a text file containing Max event sequences created using the seq~ object's write message into the memory of the.
methods.description: Reads a text file containing Max event sequences created using the seq~ object's write message into the memory of the. seq~ object. If no symbol argument appears after the word read, a standard open file dialog is opened showing available text files. The word read, followed by a symbol, reads the file whose filename corresponds to the symbol into the seq~ object's memory without opening the dialog box.

methods.name: record
methods.digest: The word record, followed by 1, causes seq~ to begin recording events into the current sequence (set by the seqnum message)
methods.description: The word record, followed by 1, causes seq~ to begin recording events into the current sequence (set by the seqnum message) at the point of the loop specified by the current value of the signal input. record 0 turns off recording. Recording is off by default.

methods.name: seq
methods.digest: Performs the same function as seqnum.
methods.description: Performs the same function as seqnum.

methods.name: seqnum
methods.digest: The word seqnum, followed by a number or symbol, sets the current Max event sequence being recorded or played back.
methods.description: The word seqnum, followed by a number or symbol, sets the current Max event sequence being recorded or played back.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: An input signal whose output is between 0.
methods.description: An input signal whose output is between 0. and 1.0 (usually the output of a phasor~) is used to drive the event sequencer.

methods.name: symbol
methods.description: Same as anything.

methods.name: write
methods.digest: Saves the contents of all current Max event sequences into a text file.
methods.description: Saves the contents of all current Max event sequences into a text file. A standard file dialog is opened for naming the file. The word write, followed by a symbol, saves the file, using the symbol as the filename, in the same folder as the patch containing the seq~ object. If the patch has not yet been saved, the seq~ file is saved in the same folder as the Max application.

msp objects.name: mc.abs~
msp objects.description: Use the abs~ object to take any given signal and output only the absolute (non-negative) translation of that signal (i.e. a rectified waveform). All negative values in the input signal are converted to positive values in the output.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: signal
methods.description: The abs~ object takes an input signal and output only the absolute (non-negative) translation of that signal - all negative values in the input signal are converted to positive values in the output.

msp objects.name: mc.count~
msp objects.description: Use the count~ object count samples elapsed and thus drive processes tightly synchronized to the sample rate. It outputs a signal increasing by 1 for each sample elapsed. It can be set to loop, and can be used to drive objects such as index~ with sample accuracy.

inletlist.digest: int, bang Start Count, stop Stops It

arguments.name: count-limit
arguments.description: Set a count limit for a looping counter, or 0 for no count limit. Note that the limit value is never reached.

arguments.name: enable
arguments.description: Specify whether the count~ object is off (0) or on (1) initially.

arguments.name: autoreset-state
arguments.description: When enabled, the internal counter is reset to the initial value whenever audio is turned on (see the autoreset message).

methods.name: bang
methods.digest: Reset to initial and begin counting

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Set initial value, reset, and begin counting

methods.name: float
methods.description: Left inlet: Set initial value without resetRight inlet: Set limit value without reset

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Set initial, limit, enable and autoreset state

methods.name: in1
methods.description: Set limit value. A value of 0 eliminates the counter limit.

attributes.name: autoreset
attributes.description: Reset the counter to the initial value when audio turns on

msp objects.name: mc.svf~
msp objects.description: The svf~ object is an implementation of a state-variable filter algorithm described in Hal Chamberlin's book, "Musical Applications of Microprocessors." A unique feature of this filter object is that it produces lowpass, highpass, bandpass, and bandreject (notch) output simultaneously - all four are available as outlets.

arguments.name: center-frequency
arguments.description: Sets the initial center frequency for the filter. The default value is 0.

arguments.name: resonance
arguments.description: Sets the initial resonance value for the filter. The default value is 0.01.

arguments.name: Hz
arguments.description: Sets the frequency input mode to Hz (the default mode - hence this is the same as providing no mode argument).

arguments.name: linear
arguments.description: Sets the frequency input mode to linear (0 -1).

arguments.name: radians
arguments.digest: Set frequency input mode in radians
arguments.description: Sets the frequency input mode to radians (0 -1).

methods.name: int
methods.description: In middle and right inlets: Integer values are converted to floats and can be sent in the two right inlets to change the center frequency and resonance of the filter. By default, the center frequency is expressed in Hz, where the allowable range is from 0 to one quarter of the current sampling rate. If a signal is connected to one of the inlets, a number received in that inlet is ignored. The values are sampled once every signal vector.

methods.name: float
methods.description: In middle and right inlets: A float can be sent in the two right inlets to change the center frequency and resonance of the filter. By default, the center frequency is expressed in Hz, where the allowable range is from 0 to one quarter of the current sampling rate. For convenience, svf~ has two additional input modes that use the more conventional input range, 0 - 1. (see the linear and radians messages). If a signal is connected to one of the inlets, a number received in that inlet is ignored. The values are sampled once every signal vector.

methods.name: Hz
methods.digest: Set the frequency input mode to Hz
methods.description: In either inlet: Sets the frequency input mode to Hz (the default).

methods.name: clear
methods.description: Clears the object's sample-memory in case of a blow-up.

methods.name: linear
methods.digest: Set the frequency input mode to linear
methods.description: In any inlet: Sets the frequency input mode to linear (0 - 1). Linear mode is simply a scaled version of the standard Hz mode, except that values in the 0-1 range traverse the full frequency range.

methods.name: radians
methods.digest: Set the frequency input mode to radians
methods.description: In any inlet: Sets the frequency input mode to radians (0 - 1). Radians mode lets you set the center frequency directly -- while the input has the same range (0-1), the output has a curved frequency response that is closer to the exponential pitch scale of the human ear.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: Signal to be filtered.In middle inlet: Sets the filter center frequency in Hz.In right inlet: Sets the bandpass filter "Q" - roughly, the sharpness of the filter - where Q is defined as the filter bandwidth divided by the center frequency. Useful Q values for svf~ are typically between 0.01 and 1.

msp objects.name: overdrive~
msp objects.description: The overdrive~ object uses a waveshaping function to distort audio signals. It amplifies signals, limiting the maximum value of the signal to +/- 1. Values outside of this range are removed using "soft clipping" somewhat like that of an overdriven tube-based circuit.

arguments.name: drive-factor
arguments.description: A single number can be provided to set the drive factor. If no argument is provided, the drive factor is set to 1.0.

arguments.name: drive-factor
arguments.description: Integer inputs are converted to float and set the drive factor.

methods.name: int
methods.description: Integer inputs are converted to float and set the drive factor. The drive factor should usually be in the range 1 - 10. Using a factor of 1 creates a linear response without distortion, and higher values increase the distortion. Values less than 1, including negative values, produce very heavily distorted signals. Use with caution.

methods.name: float
methods.description: In right inlet: The overdrive~ object accepts a floating-point "drive factor". The drive factor should usually be in the range 1.0-10.0. Using a factor of 1.0 creates a linear response without distortion, and higher values increase the distortion. Values less than 1, including negative values, produce very heavily distorted signals. Use with caution, this behavior was originally considered a bug until friends of the object's creator insisted that it should be considered a feature and left intact.)

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: the signal to be distorted.In right inlet: the drive factor as a signal value.

msp objects.name: line~
msp objects.description: Use the line~ object to generate a signal ramp or envelope. It uses the Max time format syntax; envelope times can be either single valued fixed or tempo-relative.

arguments.name: initial-value
arguments.description: Sets an initial value for the signal output. The default value is 0.

methods.name: int
methods.description: In left inlet: The number is the target value, to be arrived at in the time specified by the number in the right inlet. If no time has been specified since the last target value, the time is considered to be 0 and the output signal jumps immediately to the target value.In right inlet: The number is the time, in milliseconds, in which the output signal will arrive at the target value.

methods.name: float
methods.description: In left inlet: The number is the target value, to be arrived at in the time specified by the number in the right inlet. If no time has been specified since the last target value, the time is considered to be 0 and the output signal jumps immediately to the target value.In right inlet: The number is the time, in milliseconds, in which the output signal will arrive at the target value.

methods.name: list
methods.description: In left inlet: The first number specifies a target value and the second number specifies a total amount of time (in milliseconds) in which line~ should reach the target value. In the specified amount of time, line~ generates a ramp signal from its current value to the target value.line~ accepts up to 128 target-time pairs in a list, to generate compound ramps. (An example would be 0 1000 1 1000, which would go from the current value to 0 in a second, then to 1 in a second.) Once one of the ramps has reached its target value, the next one starts. A subsequent list, float, or int in the left inlet clears all ramps yet to be generated.A list consisting of a number, followed by a comma and up to 128 target-time pairs, will set an initial value for the ramp. An example would be 0, 1 1000 which would set an initial value of 0, a new value of 1, and a target time of 1000 ms.In right inlet: A list may be used to specify time in one of the Max time formats.

methods.name: anything
methods.description: In left inlet: The first number specifies a target value and the second number specifies a total amount of time (in milliseconds) in which line~ should reach the target value. In the specified amount of time, line~ generates a ramp signal from its current value to the target value.line~ accepts up to 128 target-time pairs in a list, to generate compound ramps. (An example would be 0 1000 1 1000, which would go from the current value to 0 in a second, then to 1 in a second.) Once one of the ramps has reached its target value, the next one starts. A subsequent list, float, or int in the left inlet clears all ramps yet to be generated.A list consisting of a number, followed by a comma and up to 128 target-time pairs, will set an initial value for the ramp. An example would be 0, 1 1000 which would set an initial value of 0, a new value of 1, and a target time of 1000 ms.In right inlet: A list may be used to specify time in one of the Max time formats.

methods.name: pause
methods.digest: Pause the internal ramp at its present location
methods.description: In left inlet: Pauses the internal ramp but does not change the target value nor clear pending target-time pairs. line~ will continue outputting whatever value was its current value when the pause message was received, until either it receives a resume message or until a new ramp is input.

methods.name: resume
methods.description: In left inlet: Resumes the internal ramp and subsequent pending target-time pairs if the line~ object was paused as a result of the pause message.

methods.name: stop
methods.digest: Stop the internal ramp and clear pending target-time pairs
methods.description: In left inlet: Stops the internal ramp and clears pending target-time pairs. line~ will continue outputting whatever value was its current value when the stop message was received, resetting its target value to that value.

attributes.name: maxpoints
attributes.description: Specify the maximum number of user defined points allowed in the line. The default is 129 points.

msp objects.name: log~
msp objects.description: Use the log~ object to output a signal composed of the logarithms of its input values. You can specify the logarithmic base.

arguments.name: logarithmic-base
arguments.description: Sets the base of the logarithm. The default value is 0.

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Set the base of the logarithm
methods.description: In right inlet: Sets the base of the logarithm. The default is 0, which is equivalent to the natural logarithm (log to the base e, or 2.71828182). log to the base of 1 is always 0.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: log~ sends out a signal that is the logarithm of the input signal, to the base specified by the typed-in argument or the value most recently received in the right inlet. If a value in the signal is less than or equal to 0, log~ sends out a value of 0.00000001.

msp objects.name: mc.retune~
msp objects.description: TEXT_HERE

outletlist.description: The deviation in cents from the closest note detected.

outletlist.digest: closest note and deviation in cents
outletlist.description: A list composed of the closest note and the deviation in cents from the closest note detected.

arguments.name: standard pitch
arguments.description: Reference tuning in Hz, the default is 440 Hz.

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Enable/disable notes in scale via MIDI notes
methods.description: MIDI notes as list e.g. “60 100” and “60 0” to enable/disable notes in the current notelist. If the default 12 tone chromatic scale is active, sending the note C3 (60) will enable note 0 (60 modulo 12), which is C.

methods.name: defaulttuning
methods.description: Go back to the default 12 note chromatic tuning.

methods.name: flush
methods.description: The flush message is used in conjunction with sending MIDI notes and will re-enable all notes in a scale.

methods.name: getlatency
methods.description: Report the latency in samples introduced by the retune~ object out the rightmost outlet.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: Signal values in the second or third inlets are used to lock the retuned signal to a specific pitch (Hz) (inlet 2) or to de fine detune modulation (inlet 3) values (Cents).

attributes.name: correction_ambience_threshold
attributes.description: Set the automatic bypass when the signal contains too much noise or background ambience (reverb). A value between 0.2 and 0.4 is usually a good starting point. Range: (-10...10).

attributes.name: correction_amount
attributes.description: Set the amount of pitch correction. 0 means no correction, 100 means full correction.

attributes.name: correction_bypass
attributes.description: Define the sibilance threshold at which the original signal is passed through unaffected. This bypass switch is required to make sure that sibilances in vocal recordings don’t sound too processed. A default setting of 100 is good.

attributes.name: correction_threshold
attributes.description: Define the threshold at which the correction takes effect. For most applications this should be set to 0 as this will correct notes that are more that 0 cent off, wrt their ideal pitch. A setting of 10 will allow a pitch deviation of 10 cents in either direction before the correction takes effect.

attributes.name: enablednotes
attributes.description: Either the keyword “all” or a list of notes in the range from 0 to the size of the current scale minus 1 (0 .. 11 in the case of a chromatic scale) determines which notes retune will quantize to. That list may also be sent in the form of a message (e.g. enablednotes 0 2 3 5 7 9 10 ).

attributes.name: notebase
attributes.digest: Base note for the currently used scale.
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: notelist
attributes.description: A list of note values or relations is used to specified the scale values used for retuning. The format follows the format used in the Scala definition standard.e.g.:Chromatic Scale: 100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800 900 1000 1100Major Scale: 200 400 500 700 900 1100Pythagorean Major Scale: 9/8 81/64 4/3 3/2 27/16 243/128

attributes.name: pitchdetection
attributes.description: Returns the average pitch of the segment that is currently being analyzed. This can be used as a pitch detector. A return value of 0.0 means that no coherent pitch could be estimated. You should expect an output fundamental frequency in the range of 50 Hz to 1000 Hz. Please note that this feature is experimental and might produce unpredictable results. In particular, it might introduce octave errors for the measured pitch depending on the input signal. Output as a signal from the second outlet.

attributes.name: quality
attributes.description: Sets the relative quality for retuning operations.

attributes.name: reportlatency
attributes.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) sending latency information out the right outlet of the retune~ object. Latency is reported in samples.

attributes.name: retune
attributes.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) retuning.

attributes.name: use_16bit
attributes.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) 16-bit processing. Better CPU performance can be obtained by using 16-bit processing, and it is reccomended if you are using the object for pitch detection and not retuning.

attributes.name: windowsize
attributes.description: Specifies the window size to be used for retuning calculations. The range is between 16 samples and the currently used signal vector size.

msp objects.name: mcs.vst~
msp objects.digest: Host VST, VST3 and Audio Unit plug-ins (multichannel I/O)
msp objects.description: Use the vst~ object to load a real-time VST, VST3 or Audio Unit plug-in and use its audio processing in MSP. When vst~ is instantiated as mcs.vst~, the plug-in's audio inputs are combined into a single multichannel inlet and its audio outputs are combined into a single multichannel outlet.

outletlist.digest: Parameter Index and Value When Changed

arguments.name: number-of-inputs/outputs
arguments.description: If the first or first and second arguments are numbers, they set the number of audio inputs and outputs. If there is only one number, it sets the number of outlets. If there are two numbers, the first one sets the number of inlets and the second sets the number of outlets.

arguments.name: VST-plugin-filename
arguments.description: Sets the name of a VST or Audio Unit plug-in file to load when the object is created. You can load a plug-in after the object is created (or replace the one currently in use) with the plug message.

arguments.name: preset-effects-name
arguments.description: After the plug-in name, a name containing preset effects for the plug-in can be specified. If found, it will be loaded after the plug-in has been loaded.

methods.name: int
methods.description: In left inlet: Changes the effect program of the currently loaded plug-in. The first program is number 1.

methods.name: float
methods.description: In left inlet: Floating point values are converted to int values and used to change the effect program of the currently loaded plug-in. The first program is number 1.

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Change a parameter value in the currently loaded plug-in
methods.description: In left inlet: Changes a parameter value in the currently loaded plug-in. The first list element is the parameter number (starting at 1) and the second element is the parameter value. The second number should be a float between 0 and 1, where 0 is the minimum value of the parameter and 1 is the maximum.

methods.name: anything
methods.digest: Set the value of a parameter
methods.description: A symbol that names a plug-in parameter followed by a float between 0 and 1 set the value of the parameter.

methods.name: (drag)
methods.digest: Click and drag to load a plug-in
methods.description: When a plug-in file is dragged from the file browser to a vst~ object, the plug-in will be loaded.

methods.name: (mouse)
methods.digest: Double-click to open the plug-in's edit window
methods.description: Double-clicking on a vst~ object opens the plug-in's edit window.

methods.name: disable
methods.digest: Stop plug-in processing and output a zero signal
methods.description: The word disable, followed by a non-zero argument, stops any further processing by the currently loaded plug-in and outputs a zero signal. disable 0 enables processing for the plug-in.

methods.name: get
methods.digest: Report parameter values and plug-in information
methods.description: The word get, followed by a number or symbol argument, reports parameter values and plug-in information. This is output from the fifth-from-right outlet of vst~ as a list with the query index (or plug-in info index) as the first element and the desired information as the second element.If a symbol argument is provided, and the symbol corresponds to the name of a parameter, the get message outputs the current parameter value (a float between 0 and 1) of the named parameter. Otherwise, nothing is output.If a number argument is provided, and the number argument is between 1 and the number of parameters of the currently loaded plug-in (inclusive), the get message outputs the current parameter value (a float between 0 and 1) of the numbered parameter. If the argument is 0 nothing is output.If a negative number argument is provided, the get message outputs a list with the first element specifying the number argument and the remaining elements specifying the following information:get -1 the plug-in's number of inputsget -2 the plug-in's number of outputsget -3 the plug-in's number of programs (VST) or factory presets (Audio Unit)get -4 the plug-in's number of parametersget -5 whether the plug-in's canMono flag is set. This indicates that the plug-in can be used in either a stereo or mono contextget -6 1 if the plug-in has its own edit window, 0 if it doesn'tget -7 1 if the plug-in is a synth plug-in, 0 if it isn'tget -8 the unique ID of the plug-in as an integer valueget -9 four integer values representing the left, top, right, and bottom coordinates of the desired rectangle of the plug-in UI edit windowget -10 an integer value representing the initial delay of the plug-in in samples to allow you to automatically compensate for the plugin's latency in your patchget -11 the plug-in's number of user preset files (Audio Unit only)

methods.name: getsubnames
methods.digest: Report a list of sub plug-in names when hosting a VST shell plug-in
methods.description: In left inlet: When using the vst~ object to host a VST shell plug-in (e.g., WaveShell) that is not instantiated with a specific plug-in name, the word getsubnames causes a list of sub plug-in names to be sent out the second-from-right outlet of the vst~ object.

methods.name: midievent
methods.digest: Send a MIDI event to the plug-in
methods.description: The word midievent, followed by two to four numbers, sends a MIDI event to the plug-in. The first three number arguments are the bytes of the MIDI message. The fourth, optional, argument is a detune parameter used for MIDI note messages. The value ranges from -63 to 64 cents, with 0 being the default.

methods.name: mpeevent
methods.description: Send MPE messages to the hosted VST, VST3, or Audio Unit plug-in.

methods.name: open
methods.description: The word open with no arguments opens the plug-in's edit window. If the window was previously opened then the edit window location will persist. The word open followed by two integer values specifying the left and top window coordinates respectively will open or move the plug-in's edit window to the given coordinates.

methods.name: params
methods.digest: Print a list of the plug-in's parameters
methods.description: The word params causes a list of the plug-in's parameters to be sent out the sixth-from-right outlet.

methods.name: pgmnames
methods.digest: Output a list of the plug-in's program names
methods.description: The word pgmnames causes a list of the plug-in's current program names to be sent out the right outlet.

methods.name: plug
methods.description: In left inlet: The word plug with no arguments opens a standard open file dialog allowing you to choose a new VST or Audio Unit plug-in to host. The word plug followed by a symbol argument searches for plug-in with the specified name in the Max search path. If a new plug-in is opened and found, the old plug-in (if any) is discarded and the new one loaded. An optional second argument to the plug message can be used to specify a plug-in name within a shell plug-in (e.g., WaveShell). This can either be a symbolic plug-in name or an associated ID value as displayed by the printids message).For mc.vst~, if the attribute @mcisolate is set to 1, sending a plug message will allow the user to load a VST for each instance individually. When @mcisolate is set to 0, any plug message received loads that plug-in to all instances.When the Max application starts up, the system VST folder will be added to the max search path. On the Macintosh this is generally /Library/Audio/Plug-ins/VST/ and on windows this is the folder specified in the VSTPluginsPath string value under the registry key HKLM\Software\VST. On Mac OS, Audio Unit plug-ins will be scanned and .auinfo files for Apple built-in and user-installed plug-ins will be added to the search path.

methods.name: plug_au
methods.description: Attempt to load an AudioUnit plug-in by name. Equivalent to plug C74_AU:/<plug-in name>.

methods.name: plug_vst
methods.description: Attempt to load a VST plug-in by name. Equivalent to plug C74_VST:/<plug-in name>.

methods.name: plug_vst3
methods.description: Attempt to load a VST3 plug-in by name. Equivalent to plug C74_VST3:/<plug-in name>.

methods.name: presetnames
methods.digest: Output a list of the plug-in's user preset filenames
methods.description: For Audio Unit plug-ins only, the word presetnames causes a list of the plug-in's user preset filenames to be sent out the right outlet.

methods.name: printids
methods.digest: Print a list of sub plug-in IDs for a VST shell plug-in to the Max Console
methods.description: In left inlet: When using the vst~ object to host a VST shell plug-in (e.g., WaveShell) that is not instantiated with a specific plug-in name, the word printids causes a list of sub plug-in IDs to be displayed in the Max Console.

methods.name: read
methods.digest: Read an effect program in bank or individual program format
methods.description: With no arguments, read opens a standard open file dialog prompting for a file of effect programs, either in bank or individual program format. read accepts an optional symbol argument where it looks for a VST plug-in bank or effect program file in the Max search path.

methods.name: scan
methods.description: Re-scan the system VST folders for new plug-ins. On the Macintosh this is generally /Library/Audio/Plug-ins/VST/ and on windows this is the folder specified in the VSTPluginsPath string value under the registry key HKLM\Software\VST. On Mac OS, Audio Unit plug-ins will be scanned and .auinfo files for Apple built-in and user-installed plug-ins will be added to the search path. The optional arguments 0, 1, 2, or 3, set the scan type to 0=default, 1=partial, 2=full, and 3=reset.

methods.name: set
methods.digest: Change the name of the current effect program
methods.description: In left inlet: The word set, followed by a symbol, changes the name of the current effect program to the symbol.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Input to be processed by the plug-in
methods.description: Input to be processed by the plug-in. If the plug-in is an instrument plug-in, the input will be ignored.

methods.name: subname
methods.description: In left inlet: The word subname, followed by a plug-in name or plug-in ID, will cause a shell VST plug-in (e.g., WaveShell) to be re-instantiated with the specified name/ID.

methods.name: wclose
methods.description: Closes the plug-in's edit window.

methods.name: write
methods.description: For VST plug-ins, with no arguments, write opens a standard Save As dialog box prompting you to choose the name and type of the effect program file (single program or bank). write accepts an optional symbol argument that specifies a full or partial destination pathname. An individual program file is written in this case. For Audio Unit plug-ins, the filename argument is required, and specifies the name of a user preset that will be written to a standard plug-in user preset location.

methods.name: writebank
methods.digest: Write an effect program bank file
methods.description: With no arguments, writebank opens a standard Save As dialog box prompting you to choose the name of the effect program bank file. writebank accepts an optional symbol argument that specifies a full or partial destination pathname. For Audio Unit plug-ins, the writebank message is the same as write and saves only the current settings to a named file.

methods.name: writepgm
methods.digest: Write an individual effect program file
methods.description: With no arguments, writepgm opens a standard Save As dialog box prompting you to choose the name of the individual effect program file. writepgm accepts an optional symbol argument that specifies a full or partial destination pathname. For Audio Unit plug-ins, the writepgm message is the same as write and saves the current settings to a named file.

attributes.name: annotation_name
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: autosave
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: bypass
attributes.description: Bypasses plug-in processing and passes all audio through the vst~ object.

attributes.name: enablehscroll
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: enablevscroll
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: genericeditor
attributes.description: Use a generic editor interface for a plug-in. Note that some Audio Unit plug-ins will not show generic interfaces.

attributes.name: mcisolate
attributes.description: Isolate parameter changes to a specified channel.

attributes.name: parameter_enable
attributes.description: Enables use of this object with Max for Live Parameters and allows for setting initial parameter values in the Max environment.

attributes.name: parameter_mappable
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: prefer
attributes.description: In the absence of other information, such as an absolute path to a plug-in file or an explicit typed plug-in path (e.g. C74_VST:/[pluginname], C74_VST3:/[pluginname], or C74_AU:/[pluginname] on OSX), the prefer attribute will be used to preferentially load one type of plug-in before other available formats when using the plug message. Note that the variations plug_vst, plug_vst3, and plug_au can also be used to override the specified preference.

attributes.name: valuemode
attributes.description: Determines the output at the vst~ object's fifth-from-right outlet. In Value mode (the default: 0), the object will send the parameter's index followed by a floating-point value between 0. and 1. (e.g. 2 0.25). In String mode (1), the object will send the parameter's index followed by a symbol value (e.g. 2 -6dB). In Both mode (2), the object will send the parameter's index followed by a floating-point value and a symbol value (e.g. 2 0.25 -6dB).

msp objects.name: vectral~
msp objects.description: Use the vectral~ object to filter frame-based signal data such as the output of the fft~ object.

arguments.name: vector-size
arguments.description: The argument is the vector size for the operation. It defaults to 512, but should be set appropriately for the size of the vectors you feed into the vectral~ object.

methods.name: clear
methods.description: Clears object's sample memory (in case of a blow-up).

methods.name: deltaclip
methods.digest: Limit the change in bins of successive vectors to a value range
methods.description: In left inlet: The word deltaclip, followed by two floats, limits the change in bins of successive vectors to the values given. This is equivalent to the time-domain deltaclip~ object.

methods.name: rampsmooth
methods.digest: Perform linear vector smoothing across successive frames
methods.description: In left inlet: The word rampsmooth, followed by two ints, causes the vector to be smoothed in a linear fashion across successive frames. The arguments specify the number of frames to use to interpolate values in both directions. This is equivalent to the time-domain filtering done by the rampsmooth~ object.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: A sync signal for the index of the output vector. This is typically in the range of 0 to n-1 (where n is the size of the vector).In middle inlet: A sync signal received in the middle inlet is used to synchronize the input index of the vector being processed. The sync signal will typically be in the range 0 to n-1 (where n is the size of the vector). If the left and middle inlets are "out-of-sync", the incoming vector's bins will shift by the difference between the two signals.In right inlet: Signal data to be filtered. This will usually be frequency-domain information such as the output of an fft~ or fftin~ object.

methods.name: size
methods.digest: Set the vector size for the operation
methods.description: In left inlet: The word size, followed by a number, sets the vector size for the operation. The default is 512.

methods.name: slide
methods.digest: Perform log vector interpolations across successive frames (like slide~)
methods.description: In left inlet: The word slide, followed by two floats, causes vectral~ to do logarithmic interpolation of successive vectors in a manner equivalent to the time-domain slide~ object. The two arguments determine the denominator coefficient for the amount of the slide.

msp objects.name: pow~
msp objects.description: pow~ raises the base value (set in the right inlet) to the power of the exponent (set in the left inlet). Either inlet can receive a signal, float or int.

arguments.name: base-value
arguments.description: Sets the base value. The default value is 0. If a signal is connected to the right inlet, the argument is ignored.

methods.name: int
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: float
methods.description: In left inlet: Sets the exponent. If there is a signal connected to the left inlet, a number received in the left inlet is ignored.In right inlet: Sets the base value. If there is a signal connected to the right inlet, a number received in the right inlet is ignored.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: Sets the exponent.In right inlet: Sets the base value.

msp objects.name: mc.in~
msp objects.digest: Signal inputs for a patcher loaded by poly~
msp objects.description: The mc.in~ object receives signals from multiple inlets to the poly~ object (or multiple channels within the input to mcs.poly~), and outputs those signals as one multichannel signal. The number of signal inlets is determined by the chans attribute.

arguments.name: starting-inlet-number
arguments.digest: Starting inlet number in a poly~ object
arguments.description: Specifies the starting inlet number in a poly~ object (default 1). If an argument of 2 is given, signal inlets will start with the second inlet and continue based on the number of input channels specified with the chans attribute.

methods.name: comment
methods.digest: Set a comment for display on poly~ object inlet mouseover
methods.description: Sets a comment for display on poly~ object inlet mouseover.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Receive signals sent to a loaded poly~ object
methods.description: Receives signals sent to a loaded poly~ object. The number of signal inputs is determined by the chans attribute.

attributes.name: attr_comment
attributes.description: Comment to be displayed on poly~ object inlet mouseover.

attributes.name: chans
attributes.description: Sets the number of input channels (default 1). If an argument of 4 is given (@chans 4), four signal inlets will be created in the containing poly~ object. The maximum number of channels for any single mc.in~ object is 128.

msp objects.name: snowfall~
msp objects.description: The snowfall~ object controls a multi-dimensional particle as one or more audio ramps whose lifetime is triggered and controlled by an input phasor ramp from 0 to 1. The object will typically be used within a larger system of quasi-independent particles using the MC Wrapper as mc.snowfall~.

inletlist.description: The start of a phasor ramp causes the particle to start its output signal ramps. Typically the particle output will end when the input ramp resets to zero.

outletlist.description: The particle's output ramp signals (up to 4, as determined by the value of the dimensions attribute) begin when an input phasor starts; their evolution is controlled by the various attributes of snowfall~.

arguments.name: dimenions
arguments.description: Sets the number of dimensions (1 - 4) which determines the number of signal outputs. The default value is 1.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: The start of a phasor ramp causes the particle to start its output signal ramps. Typically the particle output will end when the input ramp resets to zero.

attributes.name: boundarymode
attributes.description: The boundarymode attribute controls what happens when the particle output value reaches the current minimum or maximum. It is global for all dimensions.

attributes.name: dimensions
attributes.description: Sets the number of dimensions (1 - 4) which determines the number of signal outputs. The default value is 1. The dimensions attribute cannot be changed after the object is created. It can be set via an argument or typed-in attribute.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: direction contains up to four values, one for each dimension.When a particle starts, the direction attribute determines the velocity of movement. The value is expressed in units per second. For example, when direction is set to 5 means, the output value will increase by 5 over one second. If the direction attribute is negative, the output value is likely to decrease over time. If the direction attribute is positive, the output value is likely to increase over time.

attributes.name: directiondev
attributes.description: directiondev contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets a random deviation around the value of direction used in setting the particle velocity and direction.

attributes.name: endmode
attributes.description: Sets the behavior when the particle ends, either as a result of hitting a max or min boundary or when the input signal resets or goes to zero.

attributes.name: endvalue
attributes.description: endvalue contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets the value to output when a particle's life ends.

attributes.name: energyramp
attributes.description: energyramp contains up to four values, one for each dimension.The energyramp multiplies the incoming 0 - 1 ramp signal value as part of the particle calculation. If you do not want the particle to move faster as the input ramp value increases, set the energyramp to zero.

attributes.name: initial
attributes.description: initial contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets a starting output value for the particle.

attributes.name: initialdev
attributes.description: initialdev contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets a random deviation around the initial value used in choosing the starting output value.

attributes.name: interval
attributes.description: Set the time interval (in milliseconds) between new particle trajectory calculations.

attributes.name: intervaldev
attributes.description: Sets a random deviation around the value of interval used in choosing the  update interval.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: max contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Set's the particle's maximum boundary value. Once the particle reaches this value, its behavior is determined by the current setting of the boundarymode attribute.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: min contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Set's the particle's minimum boundary value. Once the particle reaches this value, its behavior is determined by the current setting of the boundarymode attribute.

attributes.name: scalemax
attributes.description: scalemin contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets a scale factor for the particle's output value. The particle's value will always range between the scaling minimum and the scaling maximum.

attributes.name: scalemin
attributes.description: scalemax contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets a scale factor for the particle's output value. The particle's value will always be bettern the scaling minimum and the scaling maximum.

attributes.name: squish
attributes.description: squish contains up to four values, one for each dimension.When the boundarymode attribute is set to Bounce, the squish attribute multiplies the force of the particle's direction reversal.

attributes.name: wanderprob
attributes.description: wanderprob contains up to four values, one for each dimension.Sets the probability that at any particular update, the direction will reverse. Note that as the interval becomes smaller, the effect of the wanderprob increases.

msp objects.name: mc.fft~
msp objects.description: fft~ performs a Fast Fourier transform on any incoming signal and outputs the real and imaginary parts of that transform as well as a synchronization signal.

outletlist.digest: (signal) Ramp from 0 to Number of Points - 1

arguments.name: number-of-FFT-samples
arguments.description: The first argument specifies the number of points (samples) in the FFT. It must be a power of two. The default number of points is 512.

arguments.name: spectral-frame-size
arguments.digest: Number of samples between successive FFs
arguments.description: The second argument specifies the number of samples between successive FFTs. This must be at least the number of points, and must also be a power of two. The default interval is 512.

arguments.name: phase
arguments.description: The third argument specifies the offset into the interval where the FFT will start. This must either be 0 or a multiple of the signal vector size. fft~ will correct bad arguments, but if you change the signal vector size after creating an fft~ and the offset is no longer a multiple of the vector size, the fft~ will not operate when signal processing is turned on.

methods.name: phase
methods.digest: Offset from the beginning of a period when the FFT is performed
methods.description: Offset from the beginning of a period when the FFT is performed.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The real part of a complex signal that will be transformed.In right inlet: The imaginary part of a complex signal that will be transformed.If signals are connected only to the left inlet and left outlet, a real FFT (fast Fourier transform) will be performed. Otherwise, a complex FFT will be performed.

msp objects.name: mc.list~
msp objects.digest: Create a multichannel signal from a list of values
msp objects.description: Use mc.list~ to create a multichannel signal from a list of values. The number of output channels is determined by the number of arguments provided to the object.

inletlist.description: A list of values sets output values in the multichannel signal.

arguments.name: initial values
arguments.description: Specifies the initial values of each output channel. The number of arguments determines the number of channels in the output multichannel signal.

methods.name: int
methods.description: Replaces the first value in the multichannel output.

methods.name: float
methods.description: Replaces the first value in the multichannel output.

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Replaces values in the multichannel output.
methods.description: A list replaces the values in the multichannel output. If the list is shorter than the number of output channels, it will leave remaining channels unchanged. If the list is longer than the number of output channels, the extra values will be ignored.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: chans
attributes.description: Sets the size of the multichannel output. If the chans value is changed after the mc.list~ object is created, the change takes effect the next time audio is started or restarted.

msp objects.name: mc.resize~
msp objects.description: The mc.resize~ object changes the number of channels in a connected single- or multichannel signal, producing an output multichannel signal with a number of channels specified by its argument.

inletlist.description: The input signal to be resized.

arguments.name: channels
arguments.description: The argument sets the number of channels in the output multichannel signal.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: Single- or multichannel signal to be resized.

attributes.name: chans
attributes.description: Sets the number of output channels in the multichannel output. If chans is sent to the object when audio is on, the number of output channels will not change until the audio is turned off and back on again.

attributes.name: replicate
attributes.description: When replicate is 0, any channels in the output signal not in the input signal will be set to zero. When replicate is 1, input channels will repeat, cyclically if necessary, in the output.

attributes.name: select
attributes.description: The select attribute contains a list of channels in the input to be assigned to successive channels of the output starting at the first output channel. For example, an mc.resize~ object of size 3 with its select attribute set to 5 7 9 will copy channel 5 of an input multichannel signal to output channel 1, channel 7 to output channel 2, and channel 9 to output channel 3. When select is 0, it has no effect and input channels are copied to the output in order.

msp objects.name: mc.deinterleave~
msp objects.description: The mc.deinterleave~ object separates a multichannel signal into two or more deinterleaved multichannel signals.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: A multichannel signal will be separated into two or more multichannel signals. Channels from the input will be assigned in turn to each of the output channels in left-to-right order. For example, given a 10 channel input and three outputs, the left output will contain channels 1, 4, 7, and 10 from the input; the middle output will contain channels 2, 5, and 8; and the right output will contain channels 3, 6, and 9.

msp objects.name: sync~
msp objects.digest: Synchronize MSP with an external source
msp objects.description: sync~ outputs a 0-1 ramp, like phasor~. The frequency of the ramp can be specified in beats per minute (BPM), or by sending sync~ a tempo reference via tap tempo, MIDI beat clock, or an audio signal containing a 'click track.' Also, sync~ generates MIDI beat clock to synchronize external devices.

inletlist.digest: synchronization input and messages to sync~

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: bang
methods.description: A sequence of bang messages is used to set the tap tempo. A bang message is interpreted as one tap. If the sync~ object receives three taps in a row with reasonably consistent timing, it changes the tempo to match them.

methods.name: int
methods.description: MIDI beat clock. Integer input is interpreted as MIDI data - you can directly connect the output of an rtin object. sync~ responds to MIDI beat clock start/stop (int 250 and 252), and tick (248). All other values are ignored.

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Set the BPM for the clock
methods.description: Sets the BPM for the clock.

methods.name: bpm
methods.digest: Set the output ramp to match a bpm rate
methods.description: The word bpm, followed by a number, sets the rate of the current output ramp to a frequency corresponding to the specified beats/minute.

methods.name: midioffset
methods.digest: Adjust the MIDI output "phase" of the output ramp
methods.description: The word offset, followed by a floating point number in the range 0.-1.0, adjusts the MIDI output "phase" of the current output ramp.

methods.name: offset
methods.digest: Adjust the output "phase" of the output ramp
methods.description: The word offset, followed by a floating point number in the range 0.-1.0, adjusts the "phase" of the current output ramp.

methods.name: ppq
methods.digest: Set the number of ticks output per quarter note
methods.description: The word ppq (parts per quarter), followed by a number, specifies the number of ticks output for each quarter note. By default, MIDI beat clock specifies a PPQ of 24. The ppq message is useful mainly for doubling or halving the tempo for an external device that is set to a different time signature. The ramp signal generated by the sync~ object can be scaled for output further by using the rate~ object.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Set the tempo to match an audio click track input
methods.description: The sync~ object will set its tempo to match an audio click track input. The click track should contain amplitude peaks at quarter-note intervals of the desired tempo. Signal input will affect the tempo only if sync~ detects peak values greater than 0.1 and within the tempo range of approximately 30-240 BPM.

methods.name: start
methods.digest: Stop current ramp output and reset to 0
methods.description: The word start causes the current output ramp to halt, and resets the ramp to 0. The start message has the same effect as receiving the MIDI beat clock start value (250). When the start message is received, sync~ outputs the number 250 from the MIDI beat clock output so that any external devices will also start.

methods.name: stop
methods.digest: Stop current ramp output and remain stationary
methods.description: The word stop causes the current output ramp to halt, and to remain stationary until a start message is received. It is equivalent to sending the MIDI beat clock stop value (252). When the stop message is received, the sync~ object sends the number 252 from its MIDI beat clock output. The sync~ object does not send MIDI beat clock ticks while it is stopped.

attributes.name: rtport
attributes.description: Optionally, the sync~ object can establish a direct connection to Max's MIDI system and receive MIDI Clock messages without patcher connections. This will ensure the best timing accuracy for MIDI Clock.By default, this attribute is set to None and is disabled. Choosing All will route all MIDI Clock messages from any and all ports to the sync~ object -- useful if you have a simple single-source MIDI clocking environment. For more complex usage, choose a specific MIDI Clock source from the menu to avoid conflicting MIDI Clock messages.

msp objects.name: tapin~
msp objects.description: tapin~ receives a signal in and copies into a delay line. Using tapout~ objects, you can read from the delay line at various delay times. You must connect the outlet of a tapin~ object to the tapout~ objects you want to use with the delay line. Note that this is not a signal connection, since no signal travels between the objects. It is merely a way to indicate that the objects share the same delay memory.

outletlist.digest: Connect To One Or More tapout~ Objects

arguments.name: maximum-delay
arguments.description: The maximum delay time in milliseconds. This determines the size of the delay line memory. If the sampling rate is increased after the object has been created, tapin~ will attempt to resize the delay line. If no argument is present, the default maximum delay time is 100 milliseconds.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: In left inlet: An int Resize and clear the delay line memory
methods.description: In left inlet: An int resizes the delay line memory with the new maximum delay time specified in milliseconds (this clears the memory of the delay line, which may produce a click in the output).

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Resize and clear the delay line memory
methods.description: In left inlet: A float resizes the delay line memory with the new maximum delay time specified in milliseconds (this clears the memory of the delay line, which may produce a click in the output).

methods.name: clear
methods.description: Clears the memory of the delay line (which may produce a click in the output).

methods.name: freeze
methods.description: The word freeze followed by a non-zero number will cause tapin~ to freeze its buffer memory. This means the object will keep echoing out of its output what has already been recorded into its memory at the point of freezing and no further input will be recorded. The word freeze followed by a 0 will reset the object to its default state of constantly recording and rerecording any given input into its memory buffer and outputting it after the specified delay time.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Write signal into a delay line
methods.description: The signal is written into a delay line that can be read by the tapout~ object.

msp objects.name: mc.poltocar~
msp objects.digest: Signal Polar to Cartesian coordinate conversion  (multichannel)
msp objects.description: poltocar~ will take any given signal as a polar coordinate and output the cartesian conversion of that signal.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: The magnitude (amplitude) of the frequency bin to be converted into a cartesian (real/imaginary) signal pair.In right inlet: The phase of the frequency bin to be converted into a cartesian (real/imaginary) signal pair.

msp objects.name: mc.targetlist
msp objects.digest: Format messages based on inlet number for controlling MC objects
msp objects.description: The mc.targetlist object simplifies creating the setvalue messages used to target specific instances within MC wrapper objects. The object maps the index of an inlet where a message was received to a voice index used in the resulting setvalue message.

inletlist.description: Each inlet of mc.targetlist is associated with a voice index. The index corresponding to the inlet will be used as the first argument to the setvalue message sent out the object's left outlet.

outletlist.description: Any message received any inlet of mc.targetlist will be repeated to the left outlet preceded by setvalue and a target channel index associated with the inlet where the message was originally received.

Prior to the setvalue message being sent out the left outlet, the current voice index is sent out the right outlet. This is handy for use with other MC message objects including mc.route, mc.makelist, or another mc.target.

arguments.name: prepend
