attributes.name: engine

attributes.name: fps

attributes.name: interp

attributes.name: planemap

attributes.name: realtime

(default = 0 0 (matrix width) (matrix height)) The proportions of the rectangle are expressed in the form left top right bottom. All values are relative to the top left corner of the viewing area of the input matrix.

attributes.name: time

attributes.name: usedstrect

attributes.name: usesrcrect

methods.name: list

jit objects.name: jit.displays
jit objects.description: Senses additional display hardware attached to your computer and allows you to use standard Jitter get* and set* messages to enumerate the number and coordinates of any and all monitors. The object remembers the original state of your system's display settings when the object is instantiated, which can be easily recalled, and you can also use the object to enable display mirroring.Typically, the jit.displays object is saved as a portion of a performance patch setup to automatically determine the exact position of your attached hardware and move your output window as needed.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: bang
methods.description: Equivalent to the count message. Sends a count of the attached displays out the object's outlet in the form count  number-of-displays.

methods.name: coords
methods.description: Sends the display screen coordinates for the display whose index is specified out the object's right outlet as a list in the form coords  display-index  left  top  bottom  right. Displays are counted from 0 (0 is the primary display).

methods.name: count
methods.description: Sends a count of the attached displays out the object's outlet in the form count  number-of-displays.

methods.name: currentstate
methods.description: Sends the current state of the display out the object's outlet as a list in the form currentstate  display-index  width  height  color-bit-depth  refresh-rate. Note that LCD displays report a refresh rate of 0.

methods.name: getmode
methods.description: Sends available display modes for display specified by display-index out the right outlet as a sequence of lists, one display per line. Each display is described by a list in the form mode  display-index  mode-index  width  height  color-bit-depth  refresh-rate. Note: LCD displays have a refresh rate of 0.

methods.name: manual
methods.description: Macintosh only Sets the display to a configuration which provides the closest match for the ideal configuration specified by the arguments.

methods.name: mirror
methods.description: Macintosh only Enables video mirroring of the display whose number is specified by src-display-index to the display whose number is specified by dst-display-index.

methods.name: move
methods.description: Changes the logical screen location of the display whose number is specified by src-display-index. Two additional arguments specify the new screen location. If a location is chosen which overlaps with the location of another display, a new non-overlapping location will be automatically assigned. The final position of the display after a move can be verified using the coords message.

methods.name: reset
methods.digest: Return displays to their snapshot state
methods.description: Return displays to their snapshot state (see the snapshot method). Note that reset does not have any affect on video mirroring settings, which must be maintained manually.

methods.name: setmode
methods.description: Change the display mode. The two arguments specify the display index, and the mode index (derived from the getmode message).

methods.name: snapshot

Multiple contexts can be managed by explicitly setting the name attribute of the jit.phys.world object and the worldname attribute of the child physics objects. Dynamics can be disabled, allowing the world to be used solely for collision detections. A 2D simulation is achieved with the remove_plane attribute.

The colliding objects name is reported out the right-hand (dumpout) outlet of the object, followed by the relative intersection position and world-space intersection. See raytest_mode for more info.

If a matrix is purged, the message purge 1 is sent out of the jit.scanwrap object's right outlet. If there is no matrix to purge, the message purge 0 is sent. purge does not reset the object like the reset message).

methods.name: reset
methods.digest: Sets the input/output scan back to the beginning and clears the output matrix
methods.description: Sets the input/output scan back to the beginning and clears the output matrix. (Note: In fill mode, the reset message will start filling the output matrix from the top, abandoning any partial fill data that had already accumulated.)

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Output mode (default = 0 (fill))0 = fill: The object will not output a matrix until it has received enough data to fill it. If the input matrix overflows the output, the excess data is truncated.1 = dump: The object will output one matrix regardless of the amount of data received. If the output matrix is not filled, the remaining cells are set to 0. If the input matrix overflows the output, the excess data is truncated.2 = spew: The object will output as many matrices as required to void itself of all data. If the output matrix is not filled, it waits until it has received enough data before it is output. If the input matrix overflows the output, the excess data is sent to new matrices, which will be output as soon as they are filled.3 = wrap: If the input underflows the output matrix, it is 'looped' until it fills it up. Excess data is truncated.

arguments.name: planecount

attributes.name: index

attributes.name: jump

attributes.name: offset

jit objects.name: jit.gl.text
jit objects.digest: Render text in a GL context
jit objects.description: Draws text in the named drawing context. The text is drawn as 2D, 3D, or outline, depending on the mode attribute. The text can be sent as a symbol, a list of symbols, or as a jit.matrix containing char data. When a jit.matrix is used, each row of the matrix is interpreted as one line of text.

methods.name: append
methods.description: Appends the specified symbol or list to the stored text string.

methods.name: face
methods.description: Specifies the face variant of the current font. One or more face variants may be specified. The Supported font faces are normal, bold, italic.

methods.name: font
methods.description: Specifies the font in which to draw.

methods.name: size
methods.digest: Set the font size in points
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: style
methods.description: Equivalent to face.

methods.name: text
methods.description: Replace the current text string with a symbol or list of symbols.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Text alignment mode (default = 0 (left))

attributes.name: depth
attributes.description: The depth (z extent) of the 3D geometry relative to the height of the font (default = 0.) If a depth of 0 is used, no extruded character sides are generated, which will draw much faster. Only valid if mode is 3d.

attributes.name: floatchomp
attributes.description: Toggles floating-point precision rounding.

attributes.name: floatplaces
attributes.description: When float point precision rounding is enabled set via the floatchomp attribute, this value sets the precision of the number.

attributes.name: fontname
attributes.description: Set the name of the font type used.

attributes.name: fontsize
attributes.digest: Set the font size in pixels
attributes.description: Set the font size in pixels (default = 9). Only valid if mode is 2d.

attributes.name: leadscale
attributes.description: The leading between multiple rows of text as a multiple of the standard leading. (default = 1.)

attributes.name: line_length
attributes.description: The line length specified in gl-units for mode 3d and outline, and in pixels for 2d. Lines of text extending beyond this value will wrap to the next line. The default value of -1 specifies no line length, and therefore no wrapping.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Defines how the rendered text is drawn (default = 2d).

attributes.name: plane
attributes.description: The plane of a multi-plane char input matrix which will be interpreted as text. (default = 0)

attributes.name: precision
attributes.description: Sets the precision of the quadratic curve calculation [0 ->inf], The default is 1.0

attributes.name: screenmode
attributes.description: If screenmode = 1, some 3D transformations are skipped so that pixel-accurate text can be drawn. The origin of the text on screen is determined by the usual projection of the object's position, but the text remains the same size. Rotation is only applied around the z axis. Screenmode is useful for making fixed-size labels which follow objects in space. With screenmode off, the text is transformed in space in the usual way for an OB3D-group object. (default = 1) Only valid if mode is 2d.

attributes.name: slant
attributes.description: Text slant (default = normal)

attributes.name: tracking
attributes.description: The tracking (intra-character spacing) as a multiple of the standard tracking for the face. (default = 1.)

attributes.name: weight
attributes.description: Text weight (default = normal)

jit objects.name: jit.matrix
jit objects.description: The jit.matrix object is a named matrix which may be used for data storage and retrieval, resampling, and matrix type and planecount conversion operations.

methods.name: bang
methods.description: Outputs the currently stored matrix.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
methods.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by value(s) and output the data. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (dimcount).

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
methods.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by value(s) and output the data. Value is specified as a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (dimcount).

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
methods.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by value(s) and output the data. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (dimcount).

methods.name: (drag)
methods.description: Drag and drop a compatible media file onto the object to load it.

methods.name: clear
methods.digest: Set all matrix values to zero
methods.description: Sets all matrix values to zero.

methods.name: exportimage
methods.digest: Export the current frame as an image file
methods.description: Export the current frame as an image file with the name specified by the first argument. The second argument sets the file type (default = png). Available file types are png, tiff, and jpeg.You can use the Max Preferences to specify a default image resolution for png image types.

methods.name: exportmovie
methods.digest: Export a matrix as a movie
methods.description: Exports a matrix as a movie. The exportmovie message takes an optional argument to specify a file name. If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file.See the jit.record object for information on the write arguments and their default values.

methods.name: exprfill
methods.digest: Evaluate an expression to fill the matrix
methods.description: Evaluates expression to fill the matrix. If a plane argument is provided, the expression is applied to a single plane. Otherwise, it is applied to all planes in the matrix. See jit.expr for more information on expressions. Unlike the jit.expr object, there is no support for providing multiple expressions to fill multiple planes at once with different expressions. Call this method multiple times once for each plane you wish to fill.

methods.name: fillplane
methods.digest: Fill a plane with a specified value
methods.description: The word fillplane, followed by an integer that specifies a plane number and a value, will fill the specified plane with the single value.

methods.name: getcell
methods.description: Sends the value(s) in the cell specified by position out the right outlet of the object as a list in the form cell  cell-position0... cell-positionN  val  plane0-value... planeN-value.

methods.name: importmovie
methods.digest: Import a movie into the matrix
methods.description: Imports a movie into the matrix. If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file. The time-offset argument may be used to set a time offset for the movie being imported (the default is 0).

methods.name: jit_gl_texture
methods.digest: Copy a texture to the matrix
methods.description: Copies the texture specified by texture-name to the matrix.

methods.name: op
methods.digest: Perform jit.op operations on the matrix
methods.description: The word op, followed by the name of a jit.op object operator and a set of values, is equivalent to including a jit.op object with the specified operator set as an attribute and this jit.matrix object specified as the output matrix. The additional value arguments may either be a matrix name or a constant. If only one value argument is provided, this matrix is considered both the output and the left operand. For example, "op + foo bar" is equivalent to the operation thismatrix = foo + bar, and "op * 0.5" is equivalent to the operation thismatrix = thismatrix * 0.5.

methods.name: read
methods.description: Reads Jitter binary data files (.jxf) into a matrix set. If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file.

methods.name: setall
methods.digest: Set all cells to a value
methods.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by value(s). Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (dimcount).

methods.name: setcell
methods.digest: Set a cell to a specified value
methods.description: Sets the cell specified by position to the value specified by value. Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (dimcount). The optional arguments plane  plane-number can be used to specify a plane. If a plane is specified, value should be a single number, otherwise it should be a list of numbers of size planecount - 1.

methods.name: setcell1d
methods.digest: Set a 1-dimensional cell to a specified value
methods.description: The word setcell1d, followed by a number specifying an x coordinate and a list of values, is similar to the setcell message but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (1) is fixed.

methods.name: setcell2d
methods.digest: Set a 2-dimensional cell to specified values
methods.description: The word setcell2d, followed by a pair of numbers specifying x and y coordinates and a list of values, is similar to the setcell message but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (2) is fixed.

methods.name: setcell3d
methods.digest: Set a 3-dimensional cell to specified values
methods.description: The word setcell3d, followed by three numbers specifying x, y, and z coordinates and a list of values, is similar to the setcell message but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (3) is fixed.

methods.name: setplane1d
methods.digest: Set a cell in a plane to a value (1d, no val token)
methods.description: The word setplane1d, followed by a number specifying an x coordinate, a number specifying a plane, and a value, is similar to the setcell message but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (1) is fixed, or use the "plane" token to specify which plane to set.

methods.name: setplane2d
methods.digest: Set a cell in a plane to a value (2d, no val token)
methods.description: The word setplane2d, followed by a pair of numbers specifying x and y coordinates, a number specifying a plane, and a value, is similar to the setcell message but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (2) is fixed, or use the "plane" token to specify which plane to set.

methods.name: setplane3d
methods.digest: Set a cell in a plane to a value (3d, no val token)
methods.description: The word setplane3d, followed by three numbers specifying x, y, and z coordinates, a number specifying a plane, and a value, is similar to the setcell message but without the need to use a "val" token to separate the coordinates from the value since the dimension count (1) is fixed, or use the "plane" token to specify which plane to set.

methods.name: val
methods.digest: Set all cells to a value and output the result
methods.description: Sets all cells to the value specified by value(s). Position is specified of a list whose length is equal to the number of dimensions (dimcount) and outputs the data.

methods.name: write
methods.digest: Write matrix set as a Jitter binary data file (.jxf)
methods.description: Writes matrix set as a Jitter binary data file (.jxf). If no filename is specified, a file dialog will open to let you choose a file.

attributes.name: adapt
attributes.description: Matrix adaptation flag (default = 0 if matrix arguments are present, otherwise 1) When the flag is set, the jit.matrix object will adapt to the incoming matrix planecount, type, and dimensions.

attributes.name: dim
attributes.description: The dimensions of matrix data (default = 1 1)

attributes.name: dimstride
attributes.description: The byte stride per dimension

attributes.name: dstdimend
attributes.description: The destination dimension end position (default = all dim values minus 1)

attributes.name: dstdimstart
attributes.description: The destination dimension start position (default = all 0)

attributes.name: interp
attributes.description: Matrix interpolation flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the input matrix will be interpolated when copied to the internal matrix.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The name of the matrix (default = UID)

attributes.name: planecount
attributes.digest: Number of planes in matrix data
attributes.description: The number of planes in matrix data (default = 4)

attributes.name: planemap
attributes.description: Maps input places to output planes (default = 0 1 2 3 ...)

attributes.name: thru
attributes.description: Thru mode flag (default = 1) When the flag is set, a matrix is output when another one is received.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Total byte size of matrix

attributes.name: srcdimend
attributes.description: The source dimension end position (default = all dim values minus 1)

attributes.name: srcdimstart
attributes.description: The source dimension start position (default = all 0)

attributes.name: usedstdim
attributes.description: Destdim use flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the destination dimension's attributes are used when copying an input matrix to an internal matrix.

attributes.name: usesrcdim
attributes.description: Srcdim use flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the source dimension's attributes are used when copying an input matrix to an internal matrix.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: The matrix data type (default = char)

jit objects.name: jit.robcross
jit objects.description: jit.robcross implements the Robert's Cross method of edge detection.

attributes.name: thresh
attributes.description: Edge detection threshold (default 0.). Cell values below this threshold are set to 0.

jit objects.name: jit.xfade
jit objects.description: Use the jit.xfade object to crossfade between two matrices. A crossfade value of 0. results in output values equivalent to the left input values, while a crossfade value of 1.0 results in output values equivalent to the right input matrix.

attributes.name: xfade
attributes.description: The crossfade amount. A crossfade value of 0. (the default) results in output values equivalent to the left input values, while a crossfade value of 1.0 results in output values equivalent to the right input matrix.

jit objects.name: jit.fastblur
jit objects.description: Performs several special-case convolution blur/sharpen operations on incoming matrices. Although it is less flexible than the jit.convolve object, the jit.fastblur object will be quicker and easier to set up for the equivalent convolution, in most cases.

attributes.name: center
attributes.description: The mathematical weighting of the center pixel when performing convolution (default = 1.)

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: The kernel shape (default = 0 (row))0 = row1 = column2 = cross3 = diagonal4 = square

attributes.name: range
attributes.description: The number of pixels from the center pixel of the convolution kernel to its edge (default = 1)

attributes.name: ring
attributes.description: The mathematical weighting of cells adjoining the center pixel when performing convolution (default = 1.)

attributes.name: ripple
attributes.description: The scaling applied to outer cells when performing convolution (default = 1.) The second ring of pixels is scaled by this factor in relation to the ring attribute when performing convolution, while the third ring is scaled in relation to the second.

jit objects.name: jit.expr
jit objects.digest: Evaluate an expression to fill a matrix
jit objects.description: Evaluates expressions to fill an output matrix. The expression can contain any operator available from within jit.op, any functor available from within jit.bfg, and many jitter MOPs. A variable number of inputs can be specified with an attribute argument setting the inputs attribute.

methods.name: int
methods.description: Sets all matrix cells corresponding with input to int.

methods.name: float
methods.description: Sets all matrix cells corresponding with input to float.

methods.name: list
methods.description: Sets all matrix cells corresponding with input to list, on a per plane basis.

attributes.name: cache
attributes.description: Toggles the cache intermediary values flag. The default is 1 (on). It may be desirable to turn off when using generator operators such as jit.noise in the expression, which should not be cached.

attributes.name: expr
attributes.description: The expression to evaluate. If one expression is specified, it is evaluated for all planes. If multiple expressions are specified, they are evaluated on a plane by plane basis.

attributes.name: inputs
attributes.description: Input count (default = 2). Please note, there is no inlet support for this attribute. Changing the input count via an attrui, message, or the inspector will not work. You can only change the input count by typing the attribute into the object box.

attributes.name: precision
attributes.description: Sets the internal precision. The options are:float32 (the default)float64

attributes.name: verbose
attributes.description: Toggles the printing of expression information to Max Console.

jit objects.name: jit.net.send
jit objects.digest: Send matrices to a jit.net.recv object via TCP/IP
jit objects.description: Use jit.net.send to send matrices and messages over a network connection to an instance of jit.net.recv.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Send numbers to a connected jit.net.recv object.
methods.description: Any number sent in the object's right inlet is output by the middle outlet of the connected jit.net.recv.

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Send numbers to a connected jit.net.recv object.
methods.description: Any number sent in the object's right inlet is output by the middle outlet of the connected jit.net.recv.

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Send data to a connected jit.net.recv object.
methods.description: Any message sent in the object's right inlet is output by the middle outlet of the connected jit.net.recv.

methods.name: anything
methods.digest: Send data to a connected jit.net.recv object.
methods.description: Any message sent in the object's right inlet is output by the middle outlet of the connected jit.net.recv.

attributes.name: connected
attributes.description: Whether or not the object is currently connected to a jit.net.recv server.

attributes.name: host
attributes.description: The domain name to form a connection with (default = localhost)

attributes.name: ip
attributes.description: The IP address to form a connection with (default = 127.0.0.1, the local loopback)

attributes.name: latency
attributes.description: An estimate of the time between a matrix being input to the jit.net.send object and being output from the corresponding jit.net.recv.

attributes.name: nagle
attributes.description: Toggles the use of Nagle's algorithm flag (default is 0/off). Improves network efficiency for small packet sizes, though at the possible expense of latency.

attributes.name: port
attributes.description: The port to use when creating the connection (default = 7474)

attributes.name: report
attributes.description: Toggles the report connected flag (default is 1/on). When enabled, the jit.net.recv object will report connection information out the dumpout outlet.

jit objects.name: jit.rubix
jit objects.description: jit.rubix segments a matrix into a grid of rectangular cells whose cells can be reordered, flipped both horizontally and vertically, frozen, and filled with a single color value derived from a cell in the grid area (monochromatic).

methods.name: colrot
methods.digest: Rotate a column by a number of cells
methods.description: Rotates the column specified by column the number of cells specified by rotate-cells.

methods.name: freeze
methods.description: Toggles the freeze flag for the cell specified by column row. If set, the cell's contents will be frozen.

methods.name: hflip
methods.description: Toggles the horizontal flip flag for the cell specified by column row. If set, the cell's contents will be flipped horizontally.

methods.name: mono
methods.digest: Fill the cell with the upper left corner cell's color
methods.description: Toggles the mono flag for the cell specified by column row. If set, the cell's contents will be all the same value as the upper left most value in cell.

methods.name: nomono
methods.digest: Disable mono mode for a cell
methods.description: Toggles the nomono flag for the cell specified by column row. If set, the cell's contents will not be monochromatic even if probmono has a non-zero value.

methods.name: reset
methods.description: Places all cells in their original position and orientation.

methods.name: rowrot
methods.digest: Rotate a row by a number of cells
methods.description: Rotates the row specified by row the number of cells specified by number-of-cells.

jit objects.name: jit.phys.conetwist

jit objects.name: jit.freeframe
jit objects.description: Provides support for using FreeFrame effects within Jitter. It supports both single and dual input effects, and 32-bit and 16-bit data sizes.

methods.name: anything
methods.description: If the message selector matches the name of a parameter, functions like the param message, taking a single float (or symbol, in the case of text parameters) argument.If the message selector matches the word get, followed by the name of a parameter (e.g. getbrightness, the message has the same effect as the getparam message, but requiring no further arguments.

methods.name: geteffectlist
methods.description: Sends a list out the object's right outlet comprising the names of all available FreeFrame effects, preceded by the word effectlist. On Macintosh, FreeFrame effects must be located either in the /Library/Application Support/FreeFrame/> folder, or in a directory called FreeFrame Plugins, within the Max search path. On Windows, FreeFrame effects must be located either in the C:\Program Files\Common Files\FreeFrame\ folder, or in a directory called FreeFrame Plugins, within the Max search path.

methods.name: getparam
methods.description: Sends a list out the object's right outlet containing the current value of the parameter specified by the param argument (either by name or by index into the list returned by getparamlist). The list is formatted as param  param  param-val  param-display. The param argument is the name of the parameters, the param-val the value, and param-display is an alternate display value, for parameters whose "real value", as understood by the parameter, lies outside of the range 0-1.

methods.name: getparamlist
methods.description: Sends lists out the object's right outlet describing the parameters for the currently selected effect, one list per parameter (see numparams). The list or lists are in the form paramlist  param-name  param-type.All parameters, regardless of type (with the exception of text), accept a single floating-point number between 0 and 1 as input.The parameter types are: boolean, event, red, green, blue, xpos, ypos, text, standard.After all parameters have been listed, the message paramlist done is output.

methods.name: loadeffect
methods.description: Selects an available FreeFrame effect for use. The effect must be specified by its name, as reported by the geteffectlist message.

methods.name: param
methods.description: Sets the value of the parameter specified by the param argument (either by name or by index into the list returned by getparamlist). All parameters, regardless of type (with the exception of text), accept a single floating-point number between 0 and 1 as input. See the getparamlist message for additional information on parameter types.

methods.name: reload
methods.description: Causes the object to rescan the FreeFrame plugins folders and add any new plugins to its list of effects. See the geteffectlist method for more details.

attributes.name: fx
attributes.description: The currently loaded effect

attributes.name: inmode
attributes.description: The matrix input mode (jitter/freeframe).The inmode and outmode attributes provide an optimization when building chains of jit.freeframe objects. Because Jitter and FreeFrame use different byte-padding, matrices generally have to be copied to a new buffer when the arrive at a jit.freeframe object, and copied back into a Jitter matrix after processing, before output. If several jit.freeframe objects will be used to sequentially process data, this copying step can be avoided.The first object in the chain should have inmode set to jitter, and outmode set to freeframe. All subsequent objects should have both attributes set to freeframe, except for the last one, which should have inmode set to freeframe, and outmode set to jitter.

attributes.name: numparams
attributes.description: The number of parameters for the currently loaded effect (default = -1)A value of -1 indicates that there is no loaded effect.

attributes.name: outmode
attributes.description: The matrix output mode (jitter/freeframe).The inmode and outmode attributes provide an optimization when building chains of jit.freeframe objects. Because Jitter and FreeFrame use different byte-padding, matrices generally have to be copied to a new buffer when the arrive at a jit.freeframe object, and copied back into a Jitter matrix after processing, before output. If several jit.freeframe objects will be used to sequentially process data, this copying step can be avoided.The first object in the chain should have inmode set to jitter, and outmode set to freeframe. All subsequent objects should have both attributes set to freeframe, except for the last one, which should have inmode set to freeframe, and outmode set to jitter.

jit objects.name: jit.qball

jit objects.description: The jit.qball object places all messages received at scheduler time in the low priority queue, even if overdrive is turned off.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME

methods.name: bang
methods.digest: Place a bang in the low priority queue.
methods.description: Any bang received at scheduler time will be placed in the low priority queue. When the low priority queue services this message, it will be sent out the left outlet. If the message received is being sent from the low priority queue it is immediately sent out the leftmost outlet.If mode= usurp, and the low priority queue has not yet serviced the last received message, it will be replaced by the most recently received message.If mode= defer, then the most recently received message will be placed in the low priority queue without affecting previously received messages.

jit objects.description: jit.la.mult calculates the matrix product of two input matrices (as opposed to multiplication performed by the jit.op object, which is pointwise multiplication). The input matrices must be 1-plane or 2-plane matrices of the type float32 or float64. If a 2-plane matrix is used, it is assumed that the data is from the set of complex numbers.

jit objects.description: Converts a 4-plane char ARGB (alpha, red, green, blue) matrix into a 4-plane char UYVY (signed chroma blue, luminance left, signed chroma red, luminance right) matrix. Alpha channel is lost and horizontal dimension is halved to support this half chroma, macro pixel output format. The UYVY format is typically useful for efficiently transferring chroma reduced codecs to the GPU without the expense of colorspace conversion, or bandwidth requirements of a full chroma format.

jit objects.name: jit.ayuv2argb
jit objects.description: Converts 4-plane char AYUV (alpha, luminance, signed chroma blue, signed chroma red) matrix into a 4-plane char ARGB (alpha, red, green, blue) matrix. Unlike UYVY data, AYUV data has an alpha channel and full resolution chroma data.

jit objects.name: jit.shade
jit objects.description: jit.shade performs a linear crossfade between corresponding cells in two input matrices at a rate determined by the values of the cells of a third "map" matrix. The crossfade rate is calculated in frames rather than units of time.

methods.name: reset
methods.digest: Start the fade over from the beginning
methods.description: Zeroes the fade counter, causing the fade to start over from the beginning. The fade counter is actually managed in the second plane of matrix 3. If initialization values were provided in that plane, they are lost after a reset message is received.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: Maximum rate (default = 255)

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: Minimum rate (default = 0)

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Crossfade mode (default = 0 (start to end))0 = start to end crossfade: Fades from start to end without looping and sends a done message out the right outlet on completion.1 = palindrome crossfade: Fades from start to end, then reverse direction.2 = looped cellwise start to end crossfade: Once any cell has finished its fade, it begins again.

jit objects.name: jit.bsort
jit objects.description: Performs a bubble sort on an incoming matrix, sorting the cells in ascending order.

attributes.name: dimmode
attributes.description: Sorts along the dimension specified the integer (0 or 1)

attributes.name: maxiter
attributes.description: The maximum number of search iterations (default = -1). A value of -1 sets the search iterations based on the matrix size.

attributes.name: planemode
attributes.description: Sorts cells based on the values contained in the plane specified by the planemode 0-(planecount-1)

attributes.name: summode
attributes.description: Summing flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, sorting is based on the sum of the planes.

jit objects.name: jit.playlist
jit objects.description: Use jit.playlist to organize sets of video files and play them back. Each video is given a visual representation in a clip where a selection from the entire video file may be choosen. Clips may be dragged within a jit.playlist to re-order them, or they maybe dragged to other jit.playlist objects by using the handle (dot) on the left side of the clip.

methods.name: int
methods.description: 0 stops video playback. A number greater than zero begins playback of the clip with that index. Indices begin counting at 1.

methods.name: append
methods.digest: Add a new video file to the list
methods.description: Add a new video file to the list. First argument specifies the video file. Second (optional) argument specifies the slot number for the clip (starting at 1). If no arguments are listed, clicking the append message in a locked patcher will open a dialog box where you can choose a file to append.

methods.name: clear
methods.description: Remove all clips from the playlist. To remove just one clip, right-click on the file you wish to remove in a locked patcher and choose "Remove" from the contextual menu.

methods.name: (drag)
methods.digest: Drag and drop compatible media files
methods.description: Create a new jit.playlist object by dragging and dropping a compatible media file into an unlocked patch. To load additional media files into a jit.playlist object, drag the new file onto the jit.playlist UI until a line appears above or below the currently loaded file. To rearrange tracks within jit.playlist, click and drag the handle (dot on the left side) up or down in a locked patch. To replace a currently loaded file, drag the new file over the old one until the entire track is highlighted.

methods.name: getclipattr
methods.digest: Retrieve attribute state for a specific clip
methods.description: The word getclipattr, followed by a clip number and attribute name, will send that attribute's value out the notification (middle) outlet of jit.playlist. This allows you to retrieve an attribute state for a specific clip. You can retrieve read-only attributes (e.g. duration, moviedim, etc.), along with most attributes supported by jit.movie.

methods.name: getcontent
methods.digest: Get the contents and behavior of all clips
methods.description: The word getcontent sends the contents and behavior of all clips out the last outlet of jit.playlist in dictionary format. Connect the last outlet to a dict.view object to see the contents. Please note that most content states will not print their default values. These will only be printed if you explicitly set a value. For the "absolutepath" entry, the full file path for each clip will only be displayed if the file is not in Max's search path. If the file is in Max's search path, only the file name will be displayed.

methods.name: (mouse)
methods.digest: Press play, loop, and make selections
methods.description: Use your mouse to play and stop a clip in jit.playlist. Also use it to select small parts of the sample for playback.

methods.name: next
methods.description: Plays the next clip loaded in jit.playlist.

methods.name: pause
methods.description: Pause playback of the current clip at the current position.

methods.name: remove
methods.description: The word remove, followed by a clip number starting at 1, removes that clip from the list.

methods.name: resume
methods.description: Resume playback from the current position if playback has been paused.

methods.name: selection
methods.digest: Select playback endpoints for a clip
methods.description: Select playback endpoints for a clip using a normalized range (0.0 is the beginning, 1.0 is the end). The first argument specifies which clip (starting at 1). The second argument is the start point for the clip, and the third argument is the end point. If only two arguments are given, they serve as the start and end points for all clips in jit.playlist. If only one argument is given, it serves as the clip number and clears any selection from that clip.

methods.name: selectionms
methods.digest: Select playback endpoints for a clip in milliseconds
methods.description: Select playback endpoints for a clip in milliseconds. The first argument specifies which clip (starting at 1). The second argument is the start point for the clip, and the third argument is the end point. If only two arguments are given, they serve as the start and end points for all clips in jit.playlist. If only one argument is given, it serves as the end point for all clips in jit.playlist.

methods.name: setclip
methods.digest: Set an attribute state for a specific clip
methods.description: jit.movie attributes are available in jit.playlist. To control a specific clip, use the "setclip" message followed by the clip number, attribute name, and value. The message "setclip 2 loop 1" will turn looping on for clip 2.

attributes.name: accentcolor
attributes.description: Sets the color of the loop icon when turned off.

attributes.name: allowreorder
attributes.description: Allow the re-ordering of clips in jit.playlist by dragging the handle (dot on the left side) for a clip above or below other clips.

attributes.name: bgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the background color of the object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: clipheight
attributes.digest: Height alloted for each clip to be displayed
attributes.description: Height alloted for each clip to be displayed. This value may be altered when dragging new clips into jit.playlist according to the expansion attribute.

attributes.name: color
attributes.description: Sets the controls color (when on) of the object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: drawto
attributes.description: A render context name, used when output_texture is enabled. If no value is specified the attribute is set implicitly. In this case use the getclipattr message to query the value.

attributes.name: elementcolor
attributes.description: Sets the clip divider color of the object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: expansion
attributes.digest: Style of accomodation for adding clips
attributes.description: Style of accomodation for adding clips to a jit.playlist with no empty space available.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Turn looping on/off.

attributes.name: loopreport
attributes.digest: Report when a video reaches the end of a loop
attributes.description: When loopreport is set to 1, the word "loopnotify", followed by the clip number and file name, will be sent out the second outlet of jit.playlist every time the selected video file reaches the end of a loop.

attributes.name: output_texture
attributes.description: When output_texture is set to 1, the video files in jit.playlist will be output as a texture. A valid GL context (e.g. a jit.world or jit.pworld) is required for texture output functionality.

attributes.name: parameter_enable
attributes.description: Enables use of this object with Max for Live Parameters and allows for setting initial parameter values in the Max environment.

attributes.name: parameter_mappable
attributes.description: When parameter_mappable is enabled, the object will be available for mapping to keyboard or MIDI input using the Mappings feature.

attributes.name: reportprogress
attributes.description: When reportprogress is set to 1, the current playback position will be sent out the second outlet of jit.playlist as a float from 0-1.

attributes.name: selectioncolor
attributes.description: Sets the selection color of the object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: showname
attributes.description: When showname is set to 1, the name of the video file is displayed in the jit.playlist UI.

attributes.name: style
attributes.description: Sets the style to be applied to the object. Styles can be set using the Format palette.

attributes.name: textcolor
attributes.description: Sets the color of the file name text in RGBA format.

jit objects.name: jit.path

jit objects.name: jit.vcr

jit objects.description: Use the jit.vcr object combine a sequence of Jitter matrices and MSP audio and save the sequence to disk as a synchronized movie. The two left inlets accept MSP audio signals (if only 1 inlet is used, the movie's audio will be monophonic). The right inlet accepts a Jitter matrix.

methods.name: stop

methods.name: write
methods.description: Writes the sequence of incoming Jitter matrices to a disk file as a movie. The default is to write a 30. fps raw codec max quality file with a timescale of 600.The following list of codecs is deprecated (retained for reference). See codeclist for the preferred method to list valid system codecs.The available codec types are raw, cinepak, graphics, animation, video, componentvideo, jpeg, mjpega, mjpegb, sgi, planarrgb, macpaint, gif, photocd, qdgx, avrjpeg, opendmljpeg, bmp, winraw, vector, qd, h261, h263, dvntsc, dvpal, dvprontsc, dvpropal, flc, targa, png, tiff, componentvideosigned, componentvideounsigned, cmyk, microsoft, sorenson, indeo4, argb64, rgb48, alphagrey32, grey16, mpegyuv420, yuv420, sorensonyuv9 and mpeg4. The available codec quality settings are lossless, max, min, low, normal, or high.Note that minimum quality is, in many cases, the codec's default quality. Use "low" quality for consistent results.

jit objects.name: jit.phys.point2point

jit objects.name: jit.phys.picker
jit objects.digest: Constraint picking in a physics world
jit objects.description: The jit.phys.picker object responds to mouse clicks and drags in the destination by creating a constraint on jit.phys.body objects intersecting with the mouse. Multi-touch picking is facilitated by the touch message.

methods.name: touch
methods.digest: Create or update a multi-touch picking point.
methods.description: Update the multi-touch point at index (or create if doesn't exist). The constraint is enabled if down is 1, and the position is set from screen-x and screen-y.

attributes.name: body
attributes.description: The name of the jit.phys.body currently intersecting with the mouse.

attributes.name: dynamics
attributes.description: Enable/disable dynamic constraint picking intersecting bodies (default = 1).

attributes.name: enable
attributes.description: Enable the picker contraint and ray-testing in the physics simulation (default = 1).

attributes.name: filterclass
attributes.digest: Name of this object's collision filter-class.
attributes.description: Set the name of this object's collision filter-class (default = default). Other objects most specify the filterclass name in their filters list to enable collisions with this object. Maximum allowed unique names is 10.

attributes.name: filters
attributes.digest: List of filterclass names this object collides with
attributes.description: Specify a list of filterclass names to enable collisions with (default = all). Possible values include all and default. Additional values include any user-specified filterclass names (maximum allowed = 10).

attributes.name: hover
attributes.description: Enable/disable mouse hovering allowing for picking without the mouse button down (default = 0).

attributes.name: local_position
attributes.description: The local-space constraint position on the picked body (default = 0 0 0).

attributes.name: output_positions
attributes.description: Enable/disable the output of local and world position values when an object is selected(default = 0). When enabled the local position on the clicked object, and the world-space position of the constraint are output following the object name and mouse-state.

attributes.name: pickmode
attributes.description: Determines how the constraint is applied to the intersecting body (default = surface).

attributes.name: position
attributes.description: The current constraint picking position (default = 0 0 0).

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Set the constraint strength (default = 0.2). Determines what proportion of the joint error will be fixed each simulation step. Values between 0.1 and 0.8 are recommended.

attributes.name: stretch
attributes.description: Set the constraint stretch (default = 0.0). Setting to a positive value allows forces acting on rigid bodies to violate the constraint by an amount proportional to the stretch value.

attributes.name: ui_priority
attributes.description: UI priority value (default = -800). When multiple UI objects are listening to the same window, ui_priority determines the order objects receive input. Lower values test first.

attributes.name: worldname

jit objects.description: jit.la.determinant calculates the determinant of a given input matrix, and send the result out the leftmost outlet. The input matrices must be 1-plane or 2-plane matrices of the type float32 or float64. If a 2-plane matrix is used, it is assumed that the data is from the set of complex numbers and the output product is a list of 2 floating point values. jit objects.name: jit.lcd
jit objects.description: The jit.lcd object is a wrapper for many QuickDraw commands.

methods.name: ascii
methods.description: Writes the ASCII character specified by the character argument at the current pen location using the current font and textmode, then moves the pen position to the right of that character. Numbers that exceed the 0-255 range are restricted to that range with a modulus operation.

methods.name: brgb
methods.description: Sets the current background color. All values should be in the range 0-255.

methods.name: clearpicts
methods.digest: Delete all of the object's named pictures.
methods.description: The word clearpicts, followed by a symbol, deletes all of an lcd object's named pictures from memory so that they can no longer be drawn. To remove the images from the lcd object's display, the command should be followed by a clear message.

methods.name: clipoval
methods.digest: Clip drawing commands to an oval
methods.description: Clips drawing commands to the oval specified by left top right bottom The arguments are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

methods.name: clippoly
methods.digest: Clip drawing commands to the polygon
methods.description: Clips drawing commands to the polygon specified by the up to 254 x/y-pairs arguments. These integer pairs are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

methods.name: cliprect
methods.digest: Clip drawing commands to a specified rectanglar area
methods.description: Clips drawing commands to the rectangle specified by left, top, right, and bottom arguments. These integer arguments are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

methods.name: cliproundrect
methods.digest: Clip drawing commands to a rounded rectangle
methods.description: Clips drawing commands to the rounded rectangle specified by left, top, right, bottom, horizontal-roundness, and vertical-roundness arguments. These integer arguments are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

methods.name: color
methods.description: Sets the current pen color to the value specified by the color-index argument.

methods.name: deletepict
methods.description: The word deletepict, followed by a symbol, deletes the named the picture from memory so that it can no longer be drawn. To remove the image from the lcd object's display, the command should be followed by a clear message.

methods.name: drawpict
methods.digest: Draw a named picture or matrix
methods.description: Draws the named picture or matrix. A destination rectangle into which the picture is scaled and drawn may optionally be specified by the x-offset, y-offset, width, and height integer arguments. A source rectangle that specifies the area of the picture to use in the operation may also be optionally specified by the src-x-offset, src-y-offset, src-width, and src-height integer arguments. The position of the destination and source rectangles are relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Unless otherwise specified, both rectangles are set to be the same size as the picture. All arguments are optional and default to zero. The current penmode will used as the transfer mode.

methods.name: font
methods.digest: Set the current font name and size
methods.description: Sets the current font name and size. Fonts can be specified by either their ID number or name. Font size is specified in points.

methods.name: framearc
methods.digest: Paint the outline of an arc
methods.description: Paints the outline of an arc. The left, top, right, and bottom arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of an oval across which the arc will be drawn, and the start-angle and arc-length arguments describe the position of the arc with respect to the oval. The location of the oval/arc is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. A color may also optionally be specified using a single number that selects a color from Max's color palette (similar to the color message), or by using three additional numbers that describe an RGB value (similar to the frgb message). The width of the line segment describing the arc is set using the pensize message to the jit.lcd object.

methods.name: frameoval
methods.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of an oval
methods.description: Draws the unfilled outline of an oval. The left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of the oval. The location of the oval is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the border may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the border of the oval is set using the pensize message to the jit.lcd object.

methods.name: framepoly
methods.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of a polygon arguments.
methods.description: Draws the unfilled outline of a polygon specified by up to 254 integer x/y-pair arguments. Each integer pair specifies a pixels relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. A polygon is closed by specifying an x/y pair having the same values as the first integer pair. The width of the border of the polygon is set using the pensize message to the jit.lcd object.

methods.name: framerect
methods.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of a rectangle
methods.description: Draws the unfilled outline of a rectangle specified by the left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments. The edge positions are specified as pixels relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the border may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the border of the rectangle is set using the pensize message to the jit.lcd object.

methods.name: frameroundrect
methods.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of a rounded rectangle
methods.description: Draws the unfilled outline of a rounded rectangle. The left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments describe the top and bottom extremities of the rectangle, and the The horizontal-roundness and vertical-roundness] integer arguments specify the amount of corner rounding in pixels. The location of the rounded rectangle is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the border may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the border of the rectangle is set using the pensize message to the jit.lcd object.

methods.name: frgb
methods.description: Sets the current foreground color. All arguments should be in the range 0-255.

methods.name: getpenloc
methods.digest: Get and output the current pen location
methods.description: Sends the x and y coordinates of the current pen location out the right outlet of the object as a list in the form penloc  x-offset  y-offset. The numbers represent local coordinates relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. The first number is the number of pixels to the right of that corner, and the second number is the number of pixels down from that corner.

methods.name: getpixel
methods.digest: Get and output the color of a specified pixel
methods.description: Sends the color of the pixel specified by the x and y offset arguments and the coordinates out the object's right outlet as a list in the form pixel  red  green  blue  x-offset  y-offset. The three color values should be in the range 0-255. The pixel location is specified relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. If a pixel is out of range, the getpixel message will output pixel 0 0 0 x y, where x and y are the out of range location specified.

methods.name: line
methods.digest: Draw a line from the current pen position to a relative point.
methods.description: Draws a line from the current pen position to the relative point specified by two integer x-offset and x-offset arguments. The endpoint of the line becomes the new pen position. Positive values for the x-offset and x-offset arguments draw the line to the right or down, and negative arguments draw up or to the left.

methods.name: linesegment
methods.description: Draws a line segment. The x-start, y-start, x-end, and y-end arguments specify the start and end points of the line segment. The location of the start and end points is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the line segment may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the line segment is set using the pensize message to the jit.lcd object.

methods.name: lineto
methods.digest: Draw a line from the current pen position to a specified point
methods.description: Draws a line from the current pen position to the relative point specified by two integer x-offset and x-offset arguments. Positive values for the x-offset and x-offset arguments draw the line to the right or down, and negative arguments draw up or to the left.

methods.name: move
methods.digest: Move the pen position relative to its current location
methods.description: Moves the pen position relative to its current location. The new location is specified by the two integer x-offset and x-offset arguments. Positive values for the x-offset and x-offset arguments move the pen position to the right or down, and negative arguments move it up or to the left.

methods.name: moveto
methods.description: Sets the pen position at which the next graphic instruction will be drawn. The new location is specified by the two integer x-offset and x-offset arguments that are relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area.

methods.name: noclip
methods.digest: Remove clipping area that may be in place
methods.description: Removes any clipping area that may be in place.

methods.name: oprgb
methods.digest: Set the opcode color used in some of the jit.lcd object's transfermodes
methods.description: Sets the current opcode color used in some of the jit.lcd object's transfermodes, such as "blend". All arguments should be in the range 0-255.

methods.name: paintarc
methods.description: Paints an arc. The left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of an oval across which the arc will be drawn, and the start-angle and arc-length arguments describe the position of the arc with respect to the oval. The location of the oval/arc is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the arc may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.

methods.name: paintoval
methods.description: Paints an oval. The left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of the oval. The location of the oval is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the oval may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.

methods.name: paintpoly
methods.description: Paints a polygon specified by up to 254 integer x/y-pair arguments. Each integer pair specifies a pixel relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. A polygon is closed by specifying an x/y pair having the same values as the first integer pair.

methods.name: paintrect
methods.description: Paints a rectangle specified by the left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments. The edge positions are specified as pixels relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the rectangle may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.

methods.name: paintroundrect
methods.description: Paints a rounded rectangle. The left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments describe the top and bottom extremities of the rectangle, and the The horizontal-roundness and vertical-roundness] integer arguments specify the amount of corner rounding in pixels. The location of the rounded rectangle is relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the rectangle may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.

methods.name: penmode
methods.digest: Set the transfer mode for drawing operations
methods.description: Sets the transfer mode for subsequent drawing operations. The transfer mode is set using an integer argument in the range 0-39. Since JUCE does not support pen modes, the only available penmode is 32 (Blend). All other penmodes are ignored.

methods.name: pensize
methods.digest: Set the pen size to be used in drawing operations
methods.description: Sets the pen size to be used in subsequent drawing operations. The pen size is set with two integer arguments, though the second argument is not supported due to differences in QuickDraw emulation.

methods.name: readpict
methods.digest: Read a picture file from disk into RAM.
methods.description: Reads a picture file specified by the symbol pict-name from disk into RAM. This named picture can then be drawn in lcd with the drawpict and tilepict messages.

methods.name: reset
methods.digest: Erase the contents of the display area and reset the object to its default values
methods.description: Erases the contents of the jit.lcd object's display area and resets the object to its default values. This message is equivalent to this series of messages to the jit.lcd object:clearpensize 1penmode 0frgb 0 0 0 (black)brgb 255 255 255 (white)

methods.name: scrollrect
methods.digest: Move or "scroll" a rectangular area to a specified location
methods.description: Moves or "scrolls" a rectangle defined by the left, top, right, and bottom integer arguments in the direction specified by the x-offset and y-offset integer arguments. the first four arguments in the direction specified by the fifth and sixth ints within the jit.lcd object's display area.

methods.name: setpixel
methods.digest: Set a pixel to a specified RGB value
methods.description: Sets the pixel located at the coordinates specified by the x-offset and y-offset coordinates to the RGB value specified by the red, green, and blue arguments. The RGB values should be integers in the range 0-255. The pixel location is specified relative to the top left corner of the jit.lcd object's display area.

methods.name: textface
methods.description: Sets the font style(s) to be used when rendering text. Font styles may be specified individually with a single symbol argument, or as a list. Valid font styles are normal, bold, italic, underline, outline, shadow, condense, and extend;

methods.name: textmode
methods.description: Sets the text rendering mode using an integer argument in the range 0-39. Supported textmodes are:0 = Copy1 = Or2 = Xor3 = Bic4 = NotCopy5 = NotOr6 = NotXor7 = NotBic32 = Blend33 = AddPin34 = AddOver35 = SubPin36 = Transparent37 = AddMax38 = SubOver39 = AddMinFor more information on the effects of each rendering mode, refer to the QuickDraw documentation in Inside Macintosh.

methods.name: tilepict
methods.digest: Fill a rectangle by tiling a picture
methods.description: Fills a rectangle by tiling a picture. The name of a jit.matrix object can be used in place of the name of a PICT file, provided that the named jit.matrix object is a 4 plane char data matrix.Four optional integers can be used to specify a destination rectangle in which the picture is tiled and four integers that specify the area of the picture to use in the operation can be added. Destination and source rectangles are specified by their left, top, width, and height values in pixels. The destination and source rectangles are specified relative to the top left corner of the matrix. The order in which the orientation is applied is first rotate about x axis rot-x, then rotate about y axis rot-y, and finally rotate about z axis rot-z.

jit objects.name: jit.la.diagproduct
jit objects.digest: Calculate the product across the main diagonal
jit objects.description: jit.la.diagproduct calculates the product across the main diagonal of a given input matrix, and send the result out the leftmost outlet. The input matrices must be 1-plane or 2-plane matrices of the type float32 or float64. If a 2-plane matrix is used, it is assumed that the data is from the set of complex numbers and the output product is a list of 2 floating point values. The first element is the real component and the second element is the imaginary component.

jit objects.name: jit.altern
jit objects.description: Overlays a color screen onto incoming matrices. The original matrix values are revealed through "gaps" in the screen.

attributes.name: bgcolor

attributes.name: colwidth
attributes.description: The width of the vertical band "gaps" in the screen. (default = 1)

attributes.name: ignore_zero
attributes.description: Alpha channel mode (default = 0 (include alpha channel))0 = Luminance calculation includes the alpha channel1 = Plane 0 is ignored and the luminance threshold calculation uses the RGB value

attributes.name: rowheight

attributes.name: thresh
attributes.description: The luminance threshold as an average of plane values (default = 0.) Input matrix values above this threshold are displayed as a grid of rectangular "gaps" between the overlaid horizontal and vertical screen stripes. Values below the threshold are displayed using the color specified by the bgcolor attribute.

attributes.name: xinterval

attributes.name: yinterval

attributes.name: line_length

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Defines how the rendered text is drawn (default = 2d).

attributes.name: plane
attributes.description: The plane of a multi-plane char input matrix which will be interpreted as text. (default = 0)

attributes.name: precision

jit objects.name: jit.tiffany

methods.name: xy

jit objects.digest: Place a light source in a 3D scene
jit objects.description: Contains the properties needed to define a light source in OpenGL. These include light type (directional, point and spot), light color, attenuation, and spot angle and falloff. In addition a position (for point and spot) and orientation (for directional and spot) can be defined for a virtual light in 3D space.

methods.name: sendoutput
methods.digest: Send the shadow output texture a message
methods.description: Send the shadow output texture a message

attributes.name: ambient
attributes.description: The color and opacity of the ambient light component in the form red green blue opacity (default = 0. 0. 0. 1. (opaque black)) All values should be in the range 0.-1.

attributes.name: atten_const
attributes.description: The constant factor in the attenuation formula: 1.0 means never attenuate, 0.0 is complete attenuation. The attenuation parameters determine how the light source diminishes with distance for point and spot  type lights.

attributes.name: atten_linear
attributes.description: The linear factor in the attenuation formula: 1 means attenuate evenly over the distance. The attenuation parameters determine how the light source diminishes with distance for point and spot  type lights.

attributes.name: atten_quad
attributes.description: The quadratic factor in the attenuation formula: adds a curvature to the attenuation formula. The attenuation parameters determine how the light source diminishes with distance for point and spot  type lights.

attributes.description: The color and opacity of the diffuse light component in the form red green blue opacity (default = 1. 1. 1. 1. (opaque white)) All values should be in the range 0.-1.

attributes.name: shadowblur
attributes.description: Shadow blur amount (default = 0.2). Indicates the width of a gaussian blur performed on the shadow output texture.

attributes.name: shadowquality
attributes.description: Shadow texture quality (default = med). Setting this value affects the dim and type of the internal jit.gl.texture shadow target.

attributes.name: shadowrange
attributes.description: Shadow range value (default = 50.0). For directional lights, this represents the the maximum distance a shadow-caster can be from shadow-receiver. For spot/point lights the maximum range a light will affect other objects. Setting this as low as possible in the scene generally gives better shadow results.

attributes.name: shadowtexoutname

attributes.name: specular

jit objects.name: jit.change
jit objects.description: Calculates the number of cells in which the current matrix differs from the previously received matrix, and based on this difference either passes the matrix or not.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Mode of operation (default = 0 (more differing cells))0 = pass new frames having MORE differing cells than the number specified by the thresh value1 = pass new frames having FEWER differing cells than the number specified by the thresh value

attributes.name: report
attributes.digest: Report if a matrix was passed
attributes.description: Report whether a matrix was passed (default = 0)0 = do not report whether a matrix was passed1 = report whether a matrix was passedWith report set to on (1), jit.change will behave a bit like Max's == object. If jit.change determines that the matrix input has not changed (within the parameters set with the mode and thresh attributes), it will send the message report 1 from its rightmost outlet. If the matrix input has changed, jit.change will send the message report 0.

attributes.name: thresh
attributes.description: The difference threshold (default = 0)The threshold specifies the number to cells above or below which a new "changed" frame will be output. This object uses cells not planes; if you have a 4-plane matrix and a threshold value of 3, one matrix cell with a different values from the previously passed frame will NOT trigger a new frame -- If you have a single matrix cell with 4 values (one per plane) which are different from the previously passed frame, it will not trigger a new frame.With the mode set to 0, a threshold of 0 means that even 1 different matrix cell between 2 frames will cause that frame to be output. Higher values refer explicitly to the matrix cell count required to cause output (5000 means it will take 5000 different matrix cells to cause the matrix to be output). Setting a negative threshold will pass all frames.
