jit objects.name: jit.avc
jit objects.description: Communicates with FireWire VTR devices, such as digital cameras and DV decks, using the 1394 AV/C protocol. Use it to control the transport of these devices with messages.

methods.name: close
methods.description: Closes the AV/C connection. The connection is closed automatically if the object is deleted, or the patch containing the object is closed.

methods.name: custom
methods.digest: Send a custom string of data
methods.description: Sends a custom string of data to the DV device. Messages are usually sent as a sequence of hexadecimal numbers. Accepted messages are documented by the1394 Trade Association. The relevant specification is the "AV/C Tape Recorder/Player Subunit".

methods.name: fastwind
methods.description: Fast rewinds the transport.

methods.name: ff
methods.description: Fast forwards the transport.

methods.name: getdevice
methods.description: Sends the name of the currently active device out the right outlet of the object in the form device  active-device.

methods.name: gettime
methods.description: Sends the name of the currently active device out the right outlet of the object in the form time  DVdevicemedia-time.

methods.name: gettransport
methods.description: The gettransport message will report the precise state of the transport of the VTR device to which it is connected out the right outlet of the jit.avc object.

methods.name: open
methods.description: Opens an AV/C connection to a compatible device if one can be found.

methods.name: pause
methods.description: Pauses the transport playback.

methods.name: play
methods.description: Sets playback at normal speed. The following optional arguments are permitted:pause: Pause in playback.reverse: Playback at normal speed in reverse.revpause: Pause in reverse playback.nextframe: Playback the next sequential frame or field.prevframe: Playback the previous sequential frame or field.sf: Playback at the slowest forward special effect speed (sf = slowest, sf6 = slow, sf1 = fastest)sf6: Playback at slow forward special effect speedsf5: Playback at slow forward special effect speedsf4: Playback at slow forward special effect speedsf3: Playback at slow forward special effect speedsf2: Playback at slow forward special effect speedsf1: Playback at fastest slow forward special effect speedsr: Playback at the slowest reverse special effect speed (sr = slowest, sr6 = slow, sr1 = fastest)sr6: Playback at slow reverse special effect speedsr5: Playback at slow reverse special effect speedsr4: Playback at slow reverse special effect speedsr3: Playback at slow reverse special effect speedsr2: Playback at slow reverse special effect speedsr1: Playback at fastest slow reverse special effect speedff: Playback at the fastest fast forward special effect speed (ff = fastest, ff6 = fast, ff1 = slowest)ff6: Playback at fast forward special effect speedff5: Playback at fast forward special effect speedff4: Playback at fast forward special effect speedff3: Playback at fast forward special effect speedff2: Playback at fast forward special effect speedff1: Playback at slowest fast forward special effect speedfr: Playback at the fastest fast reverse special effect speed. (fr = fastest, fr6 = fast, fr1 = slowest)fr6: Playback at fast reverse special effect speedfr5: Playback at fast reverse special effect speedfr4: Playback at fast reverse special effect speedfr3: Playback at fast reverse special effect speedfr2: Playback at fast reverse special effect speedfr1: Playback at slowest fast reverse special effect speed

methods.name: record
methods.digest: Set the DV device to record
methods.description: Sets the DV device to record. The following optional arguments are permitted:recpause: Pause while recording all signal(s)insertvideo: Replace the video signal with a new signal, but leave any other signals on the medium intactinsertaudio: Replace the audio signal with a new signal, but leave any other signals on the medium intactinsertav: Replace the audio and video signals with new signals, but leave any other signals on the medium intactinsertsubcode: Replace the subcode signal with a new signal, but leave any other signals on the medium intactinsertvideopause: Pause recording signals, and set the recording mode record insertvideo insertaudiopause: Pause recording signals, and set the recording mode record insertaudio insertavpause: Pause recording signals, and establish the recording mode record insertav insertsubcodepause: Pause recording signals, and set the recording mode record insertsubcode

methods.name: recpause
methods.description: Pauses while recording all signal(s).

methods.name: rewind
methods.description: Rewinds the transport.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Halts the transport.

methods.name: time
methods.description: Causes the attached DV device to seek for the specified time on any loaded media. Time is specified by four integer arguments that specify hours, minutes, seconds and frames. Many devices do not support this function.

jit objects.name: jit.dx.grab
jit objects.description: Digitizes video from any DirectX-compatible video digitizer, and decompresses the signal into a Jitter matrix. It also offers a grab-to-disk mode. Although numerous parameters for control are offered, not all features are supported by all digitizers.

methods.name: settings
methods.description: Opens the standard video digitizer settings dialog box.

methods.name: snd_settings
methods.description: Opens the standard sound digitizer settings dialog box.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Stops grabbing to disk.

methods.name: defaults
methods.description: Restores digitizer image control defaults.

methods.name: exportimage
methods.digest: Export the current frame as an image file
methods.description: Export the current frame as an image file with the name specified by the first argument. The second argument sets the file type (default = png). Available file types are png, tiff, and jpeg.You can use the Max Preferences to specify a default image resolution for png image types.

methods.name: open
methods.description: Opens a sequence grab component. A component must be explicitly opened before the jit.dx.grab object will began digitizing.

methods.name: close
methods.description: Closes an open sequence grab component. The component is automatically closed when the object is freed.

methods.name: write
methods.description: Starts grabbing to disk. If no filename argument is supplied, a file dialog box will open.The default FPS is 30. frames/sec.

methods.name: getvdevlist
methods.description: Reports the list of available video digitizers from the object's right outlet, preceded by the word vdevlist.

methods.name: getinputlist
methods.description: Reports the list of available inputs to the video digitizer from the object's right outlet, preceded by the word inputlist. Note that the digitizer must be open in order for this method to function.

methods.name: getsnddevlist
methods.description: Reports the list of available sound digitizers from the object's right outlet, preceded by the word snddevlist.

methods.name: getsndinputlist
methods.description: Reports the list of available inputs for the current sound digitizer from the object's right outlet, preceded by the word sndinputlist. Note that the digitizer must be open in order for this method to function.

methods.name: getformatlist
methods.description: Reports the list of available digitizer formats from the object's right outlet, preceded by the word formatlist. Note that the digitizer must be open in order for this method to function.

attributes.name: backlight
attributes.description: The video digitizer backlight compensation setting (default = digitizer-specific)0 = off1 = on

attributes.name: bitrate
attributes.description: The sound digitizer bit depth (default = digitizer-specific)8 = digitize sound at 8-bit resolution16 = digitize sound at 16-bit resolution

attributes.name: brightness
attributes.description: The video digitizer brightness level (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: channels
attributes.description: The sound channel selection (default = digitizer-specific)1 = digitize sound in mono2 = digitize sound in stereo

attributes.name: colorenable
attributes.description: The video digitizer colorenable setting (default = digitizer-specific)0 = off1 = on

attributes.name: colormode
attributes.description: The output matrix's color encoding (default = argb)argb = ARGB (alpha, red, green, blue) colormodeuyvy = UYVY (YUV 4:2:2 packed) colormode

attributes.name: contrast
attributes.description: The video digitizer contrast level (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: dropreport
attributes.description: Dropped frames reporting flag (default = 0 (disabled))When this flag is set, the message dropped will be sent from the rightmost outlet of the jit.dx.grab object, followed by the number of dropped frames, whenever frame-dropping is detected.

attributes.name: dstrect
attributes.description: The portion of the output matrix used for decompressing media to the internal matrix. (default = 0 0 (matrix width) (matrix height))The proportions of the rectangle are expressed in the form left top right bottom. All values are relative to the top left corner of the viewing area of the output matrix.

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: The video digitizer format selection (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: gain
attributes.description: The video digitizer gain (default = digitizer-specific)Note that the jit.qt.grab object has an attribute called gain which controls audio, rather than video gain.

attributes.name: gamma
attributes.description: The video digitizer gamma (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: hue
attributes.description: The video digitizer hue adjustment (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: input
attributes.description: The current video digitizer input (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: interp
attributes.description: Image interpolation flag (default = 0)

attributes.name: resolution
attributes.description: Preferred capture resolution for the digitizer (default = digitizer-specific)If a resolution is specified, an attempt is made to configure the digitizer to capture at that resolution.

attributes.name: samplerate
attributes.description: Sound digitizer sample rate (default = digitizer-specific)44100 = 44.1 kHz48000 = 48.0 kHz(other rates may be available, but are digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: saturation
attributes.description: Video digitizer saturation level (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: sharpness
attributes.description: Video digitizer sharpness level (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: snddevice
attributes.description: The current sound digitizer (default = 0)

attributes.name: srcrect
attributes.description: Source rect from digitizer frame (default = 0 0 (matrix width) (matrix height))

attributes.name: unique
attributes.description: Unique frame filter flag (default = 0 (disabled))When the flag is set, only new frames from the digitizer are output when the object receives a bang. If no new frame has been received from the digitizer, the jit.dx.grab object will not respond to the bang.

attributes.name: usedstrect
attributes.description: Destination rect flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the dstrect attributes are used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix.

attributes.name: usesrcrect
attributes.description: Source rect flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the srcrect attributes are used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix.

attributes.name: vdevice
attributes.description: The current video digitizer (default = 0)

attributes.name: whitebalance
attributes.description: The video digitizer white balance (color temperature) (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: write_audio
attributes.description: Audio track write flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, an audio track is written when grabbing images to disk.

attributes.name: write_video
attributes.description: Video track write flag (default = 1) When the flag is set, a video track is written when grabbing images to disk.

jit objects.name: jit.peek~
jit objects.digest: Read matrix data as an audio signal
jit objects.description: jit.peek~ reads the value of one plane of a matrix cell at the position specified by the signal inputs. This value is output as a signal. The object arguments are [matrix_name]  [dim_inputcount]  [plane].

arguments.name: matrix_name
arguments.description: The named matrix to access (default = none)

arguments.name: dim_inputcount
arguments.description: The number of dimensions in the matrix (default = 2)

arguments.name: plane
arguments.description: The plane in a cell whose value is output (default = 0)

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Set the dimensional location of the data to be read
methods.description: All inlets: Signal values arriving in these inlets specify the dimensional location of the data to be stored for the plane specified. A signal inlet is provided for each dimension specified by the dim_inputcount argument (i.e., jit.peek~ bigcube 3 has 3 inlets -- one for each of the 3 dimensions of the matrix).

attributes.name: interp
attributes.description: Interpolation flag (default = 0)

attributes.name: matrix_name
attributes.description: The named matrix to access (default = none)

attributes.name: normalize
attributes.description: Normalizated input coordinates flag (default = 0)

attributes.name: plane
attributes.description: The plane in a cell whose value is output (default = 0)

jit objects.name: jit.gl.model
jit objects.digest: Read and draw various 3D model formats
jit objects.description: jit.gl.model Reads and draws a variety of 3D model formats, such as OBJ, Collada, and Blender. Only tessellated polygons are drawn, and surfaces that are not tessellated are converted before drawing. Certain model formats, such as Collada, support skinned animation.

methods.name: (drag)
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: animenable
methods.description: Enable a model animation. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index to enable. Otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: animloop
methods.description: Enable/disable looping on an animation. Looping on animations is enabled by default. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index to enable. Otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: animlooppoints
methods.description: Set the loop points of an animation, if looping is currently enabled on that animation. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index to enable. Otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: animrate
methods.description: Set an animation's rate. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index, otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: animreset
methods.description: Reset the state of an animation. Time is set to 0., rate to 1., weight to 1., and the loop points are set to the beginning and end of the animation. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index to enable. Otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: animtime
methods.description: Jump to a specific time, in seconds, of an animation. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index, otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: animweight
methods.description: Set an animation's weight which determines how much influence the animation has on the affected mesh. If two arguments are provided, the first is the animation index, otherwise the current animation is used.

methods.name: copynodestoclipboard
methods.digest: Copy all nodes to the clipboard
methods.description: Copy all nodes in the model as jit.anim.node objects, to the clipboard. When the nodes are pasted in the patch, they will control the internal nodes of the model. Make sure the name attribute is set before using this feature.

methods.name: dispose
methods.digest: Unload the model file and free all resources
methods.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: getanim_dict
methods.description: Send a description of the animation at anim-index as a dictionary out the dumpout.

methods.name: getanimnames
methods.description: Sends a list of the scenes named animations out the dumpout. Some model files don't support named animations, and therefore the names will not be sent, even though animations are present.

methods.name: getbonenames
methods.description: Sends a list of the bones currently loaded in the model, if any, out the dumpout.

methods.name: getmaterial_dict
methods.description: Send a description of the drawgroup material as a dictionary out the dumpout. If no argument, use the current drawgroup attribute.

methods.name: getnodenames
methods.description: Sends a list of the scene nodes currently loaded in the model out the dumpout.

methods.name: gettexnames
methods.description: Sends a list of all the textures currently loaded in the model out the dumpout.

methods.name: nodeanimenable
methods.description: Toggle the animation of the named node. If disabled, model animations will have no effect on that node.

methods.name: nodebind
methods.digest: Bind a node to a jit.anim.node
methods.description: Takes two args, the name of the node in the model to bind, and the name of an jit.anim.node object to bind to.

methods.name: nodereset
methods.description: Resets the named node in the model to it's initial spatial transform state.

methods.name: nodesetinitial
methods.description: Sets the named nodes initial transform state to it's current transform.

methods.name: read
methods.digest: Load a model file from disk
methods.description: Loads an model file from disk. The read message will attempt to find the model file in the Max search path and load it. If no file name is specified, a file dialog box is presented.

methods.name: sendmaterial
methods.description: Send the internal material for drawgroup a message. See jit.gl.material for possible messages and attributes.

methods.name: sendtexture
methods.digest: Send a named texture a message
methods.description: Send the internal named texture a message. See jit.gl.texture for possible messages and attributes.

methods.name: texgroup
methods.digest: Apply a named texture to a mesh group
methods.description: The texgroup message is used to apply a named texture to a specific mesh within the model. The model's mesh-groups are specified in its model file. The texture applied to a group will override any textures which have been applied to the object using the texture attribute, and textures loaded from the model file.

attributes.name: animblendmode
attributes.description: Determine how multiple enabled animations will be blended (default = 0 - Average).

attributes.name: drawgroup
attributes.description: If non-zero, draw only one mesh. If zero, draw all mesh groups in the model (default = 0).

attributes.name: drawskeleton
attributes.description: If enabled draw a wireframe representation of the bones in the model (default = 0).

attributes.name: file
attributes.description: Load a model file

attributes.name: find_instances
attributes.description: Mesh instance removal on import (default = 1). An optional post-processing step when importing the model file. Instanced meshes are removed by referencing one parent.

attributes.name: fix_normals
attributes.description: Fix normals on import (default = 0). An optional post-processing step when importing the model file. Tries to fix normal vectors that are facing inwards.

attributes.name: gen_normals
attributes.description: Generate normals on import (default = 1). An optional post-processing step when importing the model file.

attributes.name: gen_tangents
attributes.description: Generate tangents on import (default = 1). An optional post-processing step when importing the model file. Calculates tangents and bitangents if possible.

attributes.name: hasbones
attributes.description: Indicates whether the loaded model has bone nodes.

attributes.name: material_mode
attributes.description: Mode for applying built-in material properties of a model. (default = 1 - Diffuse)

attributes.name: nodeaxes
attributes.description: If non-zero, draw a RGB axes at the location of all the nodes in the model.

attributes.name: normalize
attributes.description: Normalize model coordinates flag (default = 1). When enabled, the model is scaled to the range (-1.,1.) for the x, y, and z axes.

attributes.name: numanimations
attributes.description: Indicates the number of animations in the model.

attributes.name: numgroups
attributes.description: Indicates the number of mesh groups. A mesh group consists of vertex data and material data.

attributes.name: optimize
attributes.digest: Optimize vertices and nodes on import
attributes.description: Optimize vertices and nodes on import (default = 1). An optional post-processing step when importing the model file. Identical vertices are jointed to optimize indexing, small meshes are joined if possible, and Nodes with no data assigned are collapsed and joined.

attributes.name: smoothing_angle
attributes.description: Specifies the edge angle above which to smooth vertex normals (default = 89.)

attributes.name: verbose
attributes.description: Verbose mode flag (default = 0). If enabled, messages useful for debugging are printed to the Max Console.

jit objects.name: jit.movie
jit objects.description: Use the jit.movie for working with movie files.

methods.name: asyncread
methods.digest: Read a movie from a disk file asynchronously
methods.description: Asynchronously reads a movie from a disk file, if possible. If no argument is present a file selection dialog will be presented to choose a file. Any argument is assumed to be a local file name. At this time, asynchronous reading is not supported for URL-based movies

methods.name: cancelframedump
methods.description: Stops the frame dump process. See framedump.

methods.name: frame
methods.digest: Jump to a frame number (fast method)
methods.description: Jump to a frame number (fast method). See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify with this message.

methods.name: frame_true
methods.digest: Jump to a frame number (slower, more accurate method)
methods.description: Jump to a frame number (slower, more accurate method). See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify with this message.

methods.name: framedump
methods.description: Commences a framedump, in which the movie will start from a frame specified by start-frame (the default is 1) and automatically output frames in sequence (no bang or outputmatrix message is necessary) up to the frame specified by end-frame, skipping frame-skip frames between each frame. The default values are 1 for the start frame, and the total framecount of the movie for the end frame. The default frame-skip value is 1.During operation, the message framedump current_frame  is sent out the right outlet after each frame has been output. When finished, the message framedump done is output.

methods.name: jump
methods.digest: Jump to a relative movie frame (fast method)
methods.description: Jump to a relative movie frame (fast method). See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify with this message.

methods.name: jump_true
methods.digest: Jump to a relative movie frame (slower, more accurate method)
methods.description: Jump to a relative movie frame (slower, more accurate method). See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify with this message.

methods.name: read
methods.digest: Read a movie from a disk file/URL/clipboard
methods.description: Reads a movie from a disk file, URL or the clipboard. If no argument is present a file selection dialog will be presented to choose a file. If the argument is parseable as a URL, the object will attempt to load a movie from that location. Otherwise, an argument is assumed to be a local file name.If autostart is enabled, the movie will begin playing at once.

methods.name: start
methods.description: Starts movie playback at the current rate from the current time value specified by time.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Stops movie playback. rate is unaffected).

attributes.name: adapt
attributes.digest: Adapt output matrix dimensions to movie size flag

attributes.name: automatic
attributes.description: Enable automatic matrix output when bound to jit.world.

attributes.name: autostart
attributes.description: Autoplay on movie open flag (default = 1)

attributes.name: colormode
attributes.description: The output matrix's color encoding.

attributes.name: drawto
attributes.description: A render context name, used when output_texture is enabled.

attributes.name: dstrect
attributes.digest: The portion of the output matrix written to by the input frame
attributes.description: The portion of the output matrix used for decompressing media to the internal matrix (default = 0 0 (matrix width) (matrix height))The bounds of the rectangle are expressed in the form left top right bottom. All values are relative to the top-left corner of the viewing area of the output matrix.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.description: The duration of the movie.

attributes.name: engine
attributes.description: Video engine backend. This argument can only be set in the max box. If not specified, it is determined by the Video Engine Max preference. As of this writing, possible values include avf (Mac only), qt and viddll.

attributes.name: fps
attributes.description: The approximate calculation of the movie's internal FPS rate.

attributes.name: framecount
attributes.digest: Number of frames in the movie

attributes.name: framereport
attributes.description: Frame reporting flag (default = 0). When enabled, the message framecalc will be sent from the rightmost outlet of the jit.movie object as each frame is processed, followed by the number of milliseconds spent doing so.

attributes.name: loop
attributes.description: Looping mode (default = 1 (start to end))

attributes.name: loopend
attributes.description: The movie loop point end. Time is specified as time values.

attributes.name: looppoints
attributes.description: The movie loop points. Time is specified as time values.

attributes.name: looppoints_ms
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: looppoints_secs
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: loopreport
attributes.description: Loop notification flag (default = 0). When enabled, the jit.movie object will send the message loopnotify when the playing movie passes the loop point. In palindrome looping mode, the message will be sent at both the beginning and the end of the movie.

attributes.name: loopstart
attributes.description: The movie loop point start. Time is specified as time values.

attributes.name: milliseconds
attributes.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: moviefile
attributes.digest: Load a movie file from disk
attributes.description: Load a movie file from disk

attributes.name: moviename
attributes.description: Identifies the file name of a movie (Note: setting this attribute does not load a movie file).

attributes.name: moviepath
attributes.digest: Fully specified path on disk for the movie
attributes.description: The movie's fully-specified path on disk, if the movie has a disk-file (Note: setting this attribute does not load a movie file).

attributes.name: output_texture
attributes.description: Enable OpenGL texture output (default = 0). When enabled an OpenGL texture is output instead of a Jitter matrix. The object's drawto attribute must be set to a valid gl context. An RGBA texture is output using the movie's native dimensions. When enabled, the following attributes have no effect:adaptcolormodedimdstrectsrcrectusedstrectusesrcrect

attributes.name: position
attributes.description: Current playback position, normalized between 0. and 1. See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify when setting this attribute.

attributes.name: rate
attributes.description: Set playback speed for a movie. (1.0 = original speed, 0.5 = half-speed, etc).

attributes.name: seamless_loopcount
attributes.description: Number of instances to add to the seamless loop composition (default = 32). Seamless mode looping enables an avf only feature where the entire file is added seamless_loopcount number of times to a virtual media composition. When enabled, looping media should exhibit less of a playback stutter when the playhead returns to the start of the file. This mode only allows forward playback looping of the entire file (looppoints are ignored), and is geared more towards temporal compression codec playback, such as h264. Increasing this value adds more instances to the composition, but may impact load time and memory usage.

attributes.name: seconds
attributes.description: The movie duration in seconds.

attributes.name: srcrect
attributes.digest: The portion of the input matrix used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix
attributes.description: The portion of the movie to decompress into a matrix (default = 0 0 (movie width) (movie height)). The bounds of the rectangle are expressed in the form left top right bottom. All values are relative to the top-left corner of the viewing area of the movie.

attributes.name: texture_name
attributes.description: Output texture name, when output_texture is enabled.

attributes.name: time
attributes.description: The current time in the movie. Time is specified as time values. See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify when setting this attribute.

attributes.name: time_ms
attributes.description: Current playback time in milliseconds. See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify when setting this attribute.

attributes.name: time_secs
attributes.description: Current playback time in seconds. See the above Discussion for information on using seeknotify when setting this attribute.

attributes.name: timescale
attributes.description: The timescale for the movie (default = 600, but movie-dependent)

attributes.name: unique
attributes.description: Unique frame filter flag (default = 0 (disabled)). When the flag is set, only new frames from the movie are output when the object receives a bang. If no new frame has been decompressed, the jit.movie object will not respond to the bang.

attributes.name: usedstrect
attributes.description: Destination rect flag (default = 0). When the flag is set, the dstrect attributes are used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix.

attributes.name: usesrcrect
attributes.description: Source rect flag (default = 0). When the flag is set, the srcrect attributes are used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix.

jit objects.name: jit.thin
jit objects.description: The jit.thin object removes redundant dimensions of size 1.

jit objects.name: jit.phys.hinge
jit objects.digest: A hinge constraint in a physics world
jit objects.description: The jit.phys.hinge object restricts two additional angular degrees of freedom so an attached jit.phys.body object can only rotate around the hinge axis. This can be useful to represent doors or wheels rotating around one axis. Limits and Motor forces can be specified for the hinge. If only a single body is bound, it is constrained to a point in world space.

methods.name: reset
methods.digest: Return attached objects to original position and remove forces
methods.description: Removes any current forces and returns the attached objects to their original position.

attributes.name: bias
attributes.digest: Degree of strictness for position error correction
attributes.description: Magnitude of the limit's position correction (default = 0.3). This attribute sets how strictly the position error is corrected. For most cases, the value should not be greater than 1.

attributes.name: body1
attributes.description: The name of the first jit.phys.body to constrain.

attributes.name: body2
attributes.description: The name of the second jit.phys.body to constrain.

attributes.name: collisions
attributes.description: Enables collisions between attached bodies (default = 0.).

attributes.name: enable
attributes.description: Enable this constraint in the physics simulation (default = 1).

attributes.name: hingeangle
attributes.description: The angle, in degrees, between constrained bodies around the hinge axis (default = 0).

attributes.name: lowerlimit
attributes.description: The lower limit, in degrees, of allowed rotation around the hinge axis (default = 1). If lowerlimit is greater than upper limit, no limits are applied to the constraint.

attributes.name: motorstrength
attributes.description: The maximum motor impulse (default 1.).

attributes.name: motortarget
attributes.description: Angle around hinge axis, in degrees, the motor is targeting (default = 0).

attributes.name: motorvelocity
attributes.description: Enables motor and specifies velocity desired in degrees per second (default = 0).

attributes.name: position1
attributes.digest: Pivot point of body1 as a 3D vector
attributes.description: The pivot point of body1 as a 3D vector relative to the body1 center of mass (default = 0 0 0).

attributes.name: position2
attributes.digest: Pivot point of body2 as a 3D vector
attributes.description: The pivot point of body2 as a 3D vector relative to the body2 center of mass (default = 0 0 0). If body2 is blank, this is the worldspace position of the constraint.

attributes.name: adjust
attributes.description: Flag to enable or disable adjusting the HDR image data through ILM's proposed display mapping pipeline (default = 0). When enabled, the exposure, defog, kneehigh, kneelow, and normalize attributes can be used to control the following display mapping process:1. Compensate for fogging by subtracting defog from the raw pixel values.2. Multiply the defogged pixel values by 2(exposure + 2.47393).3. Values, which are now 1.0, are called "middle gray." If defog and exposure are both set to 0.0, then middle gray corresponds to a raw pixel value of 0.18. In step 6, middle gray values will be mapped to an intensity 3.5 f-stops below the display's maximum intensity.4. Apply a knee function. The knee function has two parameters, kneeLow and kneeHigh. Pixel values below 2kneeLow are not changed by the knee function. Pixel values above kneeLow are lowered according to a logarithmic curve, such that the value 2kneeHigh is mapped to 23.5 (in step 6, this value will be mapped to the display's maximum intensity).5. Gamma-correct the pixel values.6. Scale the values such that middle gray pixels are mapped to 84.66 (or 3.5 f-stops below the display's maximum intensity).7. If converting to 8 bit unsigned integer values (char), clamp the values to [0, 255].

attributes.name: channels

attributes.description: The list of channel names to use. When reading an OpenEXR file into a jit.matrix object, these channels will be mapped to sequential planes. If a channel does not exist it will be filled with zeros. When writing a jit.matrix object, the names listed in this list will be used to name each plane as they are stored in the OpenEXR file. (default = null)

attributes.description: Value subtracted from pixel values to compensate for fogging due to stray light in the recording device (default = 0.0).

attributes.name: exposure

attributes.name: kneelow

attributes.description: Pixel values between kneehigh and kneelow set the white level of the displayed image, determining which value is mapped to the maximum intensity of the monitor (default = 0.0).

jit objects.name: Jitter Matrix Operators
jit objects.digest: Messages and attributes common to Jitter matrix operators
jit objects.description: Since the matrix is Jitter's focus, it is not surprising that the majority of Jitter objects fall in this category of Matrix Operators. Every Matrix operator has some number of matrix inputs and some number of matrix outputs. Matrix inputs are referred to by the names "in", "in2", "in3", etc., from left to right, and matrix outputs are referred to by the names "out", "out2", "out3", etc., from left to right--i.e. the names are appended by the input/output number except for the first (leftmost) input and first (leftmost) output which are simply named "in" and "out". We will refer to the input or output name names as the "I/O-name".Matrix inputs and outputs typically each have their own matrices internally where information is kept. This is necessary because Jitter is an asynchronous framework (i.e. all the matrices don't arrive at all inputs at the same time). Various aspects of matrix inputs and outputs can be set using the command [I/O-name] combined with one of the following suffixes: "_dim" which will set the dimensions of the specified I/O matrix, "_type" which will set the type of the specified matrix, "_planecount" which will set the plane of the specified matrix, or "_name" which will set the name of the specified matrix. There is one special case which does not have an internal matrix and this is the first input "in". This is the case since this special input actually triggers the calculation of the matrix operator, so it doesn't need to be cached until a calulation takes place, unlike the other inputs. Therefore there is no mechanism to set the dim, planecount, type, or name of "in".Matrix operators accept what we'll refer to as "matrix args"--i.e. [planecount (int)] [ type (symbol)] [dim (int list)]. if these arguments are present, the adapt attribute will be turned off, otherwise it will be turned on. If adapt mode is turned on, each time a matrix is received in the first input, there will also be the equivalent of setting the dim, planecount, and type attributes to that of the input matrix. If the other inputs and outputs are linked to these attributes, this will affect their linked attributes as well. See the "MOP" table to determine which inputs and outputs will be linked to which attributes when adapt mode is turned on. For the leftmost input this is not applicable, and hence all columns are labelled "n/a".The jit.matrix object is a named matrix which may be used to matrix data storage and retrieval, resampling, and matrix type and planecount conversion operations.

jit objects.name: jit.la.inverse
jit objects.digest: Calculate the inverse of a matrix
jit objects.description: jit.la.inverse calculates the inverse with respect to multiplication of a given input matrix. The input matrices must be 1-plane or 2-plane matrices of the type float32 or float64. If a 2-plane matrix is used, it is assumed that the data is from the set of complex numbers.

attributes.name: thresh
attributes.description: The threshold value beneath which the absolute value of the result of internal calculations are considered to be equal to zero (default = 0.000000001)

jit objects.name: jit.alphablend
jit objects.digest: Blend two images with an alpha channel image
jit objects.description: Accesses the alpha channel (plane 0) of the input matrix in the left inlet as a per-cell crossfade value, and crossfades between the input matrices in the left and right inlets. In mode 0, a low value means more of the right input matrix, while a high value means more of the left input matrix. In mode 1, a low value means more of the left input matrix, while a high value means more of the right input matrix.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Crossfade mode (default = 0 (left to right))0 = crossfade right to left1 = crossfade left to right

jit objects.name: jit.poke~

jit objects.description: jit.poke~ writes the value specified by the leftmost signal input into one plane of a matrix cell at the position specified by the signal inputs (following the leftmost input). The object arguments are [matrix_name]  [dim_inputcount]  [plane].

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: Signal values arriving in this inlet will be stored at the dimensional locations specified by the signal inputs to the remaining inlets of the jit.poke~ object. The number of dimensional inlets will vary, depending on the value of the [dim_inputcount] argument.In other inlets: Signal values arriving in this inlet specify the dimensional location of the data to be stored for the plane specified. A signal inlet is provided for each dimension specified by the [dim_inputcount] attribute (i.e., jit.poke~ bigcube 3 has 4 inlets -- one for input data, and one for each of the 3 dimensions of the matrix).

jit objects.name: jit.grab

jit objects.description: Use the jit.grab object to digitize video from any video digitizer and decompress the signal into a Jitter matrix or GL texture.

methods.name: int
methods.description: Opens and closes the digitizer. See the open and close messages for more info.

methods.name: close

methods.description: Closes an open sequence grab component. The component is automatically closed when the object is freed.

methods.name: exportimage

Available file types are png, tiff, and jpeg.You can use the Max Preferences to specify a default image resolution for png image types.

methods.name: getformatlist

methods.name: getframeratelist

methods.name: getinputlist

methods.name: getvdevlist

methods.name: open

attributes.name: adapt

attributes.description: Adapt output matrix dimensions to native device dimensions. Enabled by default if no dim specified.

attributes.name: automatic

attributes.name: colormode

attributes.name: drawto

attributes.name: dstrect

attributes.description: The portion of the output matrix used for decompressing media to the internal matrix. (default = 0 0 (matrix width) (matrix height))The proportions of the rectangle are expressed in the form left top right bottom. All values are relative to the top left corner of the viewing area of the output matrix.

attributes.name: engine
attributes.description: Video engine backend. This argument can only be set in the max box. If not specified, it is determined by the Video Engine Max preference. As of this writing, possible values include avf (Mac only), qt, and viddll.

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: The video digitizer format selection (default = digitizer-specific). For a list of supported formats, send the message getformatlist.

attributes.name: framerate
attributes.description: The video digitizer frame rate (default = digitizer-specific).The digitizer has to be closed and re-opened before changes to framerate take effect.

attributes.name: framereport
attributes.description: Frame reporting flag (default = 0)When enabled, the message framecalc will be sent from the rightmost outlet of the jit.grab object as each frame is processed, followed by the number of milliseconds spent doing so.

attributes.name: input
attributes.description: The current video digitizer input (default = digitizer-specific)

attributes.name: interp
attributes.description: Image interpolation flag (default = 0)

attributes.name: output_texture
attributes.description: Enable OpenGL texture output (default = 0). When enabled an OpenGL texture is output instead of a Jitter matrix. The object's drawto attribute must be set to a valid gl context. An RGBA texture is output using the movie's native dimensions. When enabled, the following attributes have no effect:adapt colormode dim dstrect srcrect usedstrect usesrcrect

attributes.name: srcrect
attributes.description: The portion of the capture matrix to copy to the internal matrix. (default = 0 0 1 1)The proportions of the rectangle are expressed in the form left top right bottom. All values are in pixels and relative to the top left corner of the incoming matrix.

attributes.name: texture_name
attributes.description: Output texture name, when output_texture is enabled.

attributes.name: unique
attributes.description: Unique frame filter flag (default = 0 (disabled))When the flag is set, only new frames from the digitizer are output when the object receives a bang. If no new frame has been received from the digitizer, the jit.grab object will not respond to the bang.

attributes.name: usedstrect
attributes.description: Destination rect flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the dstrect attributes are used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix.

attributes.name: usesrcrect
attributes.description: Source rect flag (default = 0) When the flag is set, the srcrect attributes are used when copying an input matrix to the internal matrix.

attributes.name: vdevice
attributes.description: The current video digitizer (default = 0)

arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: bang
methods.digest: Pass a bang to the corresponding outlet
methods.description: Any bang is passed to the corresponding outlet.

methods.name: int

methods.name: list

methods.name: anything

methods.description: The clear message with no arguments initializes all inlets. Optional arguments specify by number the inlets to initialize. Inlet numbering starts from 0.When initialized, no output will occur for the inlet's corresponding outlet until new input is received in that inlet.

attributes.name: immediate
attributes.description: Processing mode (default = 0 (left inlet only))0 = output triggered by input to the left inlet only.1 = input to any inlet is sent out the outlet associated with it immediately.

jit objects.name: jit.catch~
jit objects.description: Transforms MSP signals into a stream of jitter matrices.

outletlist.digest: a matrix of floats representing the input signal(s)
a matrix of floats representing the input signal(s)

arguments.name: channels
arguments.description: The number of input signals. An inlet will be created for each channel and the output matrices will contain the data for each channel on a separate plane.

methods.name: bang
methods.description: Receiving a bang may trigger a matrix to be output, depending on the mode and the amount of signal data that has been received since the last bang.

methods.name: bufsize
methods.description: The word bufsize, followed by a floating-point number, sets the size of the buffer to be sampled.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Capture and convert an audio signal
methods.description: Signal data received in any inlet of a jit.catch~ object will be converted to a stream of Jitter matrices and sent out the object's outlet.

attributes.name: downsample
attributes.description: A downsampling factor (default=1). If downsampling value is set to n, each group of n successive samples are averaged.

attributes.name: framesize
attributes.description: In some modes, the width of the output matrix. (default=320)

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Four different modes are possible: in mode 0, all data since the last output is output in a one-dimensional matrix. In mode 1 the amount of buffered data that fits into a multiple of the framesize is output in two dimensions; data not output will be saved for the next time. In these first two modes, every sample collected should be output once and only once. In mode 2 a framesize of the most recent data is output. Mode 3 causes jit.catch~ to behave like an oscilloscope, triggering on channel trigchan when the signal crosses triglevel in the direction trigdir. If the threshold has not been passed for the duration of the entire internal data buffer (100 ms), jit.catch~ reverts temporarily to mode 2 behavior and outputs the most recent data until the threshold is crossed again.

attributes.name: trigdir
attributes.description: The direction to use to identify crosses in the trigger point: 0 is upwards, and 1 is downwards. (default=0)

attributes.name: trigchan
attributes.digest: Set the channel for trigger points
attributes.description: In mode 3, the channel to use for trigger points (default=0)

attributes.name: trigthresh
attributes.description: The signal level at which to trigger a redraw in mode 3 (default=0.0)

m4l objects.name: live.grid
m4l objects.digest: A UI grid of steps, with constraints and directions
m4l objects.description: live.grid is a user interfaces object designed for use with the chucker~ object. It provides a display grid of steps, constraints for transposition, and playback direction for use in controlling the chucker~ object.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Set, display, and output the current step
methods.description: Sets, displays and outputs the current step. The list sent out the left outlet of the live.grid object takes the form step(s)  direction (optional, depending on the visibility of the directions panel). When the live.grid object is in Matrix Mode and there is no value selected in the column, a 0 is sent as the step value.

methods.name: list
methods.digest: Function depends on the direction or matrixmode attributes
methods.description: When the direction attribute is set to 0, a list of 2 values sets the step index and value.When the direction attribute is set to 1, a list of 3 values sets the step index, value and direction.When the matrixmode attribute is set to 1, a list of 3 values sets the object's behavior: x, y, and state (0/1). An optional fourth value can be used to set direction (-1/0/1).

methods.name: clear
methods.digest: Deselect all currently set rows and columns
methods.description: The clear message is only used when the matrixmode attribute is enabled, and will deselect all currently set rows and columns.

methods.name: constraint
methods.digest: Set the constraint for a step
methods.description: Sets the constraint for a specific step. For instance, the message constraint 3 0 0 1 1 sets the constraints of the third step (column numbering starts at 1) to 0 0 1 1.

methods.name: directions
methods.description: Sets the grid directions, used to indicate the direction of playback of a step:-1: Backward0: Stop1: Forward

methods.name: down
methods.description: Decreases (lowers) the current values of all the steps by one. New step values are sent out the second outlet.Note: The current constraints, if any, are also taken into account when altering current step values; the resulting shift might be "rounded" to the closest step.

methods.name: freeze
methods.description: Set the index to 0 to hide the overlay used to indicate frozen values. Any index greater than zero sets and displays the frozen step.

methods.name: getcell
methods.digest: Report the value of a specified cell
methods.description: The word cell, followed by a pair of numbers that specifies the x and y indices of a cell in the live.grid display, will send a list consisting of the word cell, a number pair that specifies the x and y indices, and the value of the cell (column numbering starts at 1).

methods.name: getcolumn
methods.digest: Report the values for a specified column
methods.description: The word getcolumn, followed by a number that specifies a column in the live.grid display, will send a list consisting of the word column, a number that specifies the column index, and a list of the current column values out the fourth (dumpout) outlet (column numbering starts at 1).

methods.name: getconstraint
methods.digest: Report the constraint values for a specified column
methods.description: The word getconstraint, followed by a number that specifies a column in the live.grid display, will send a list consisting of the column number followed by a list indicating the constrain state of each cell in the column, from bottom to top (column numbering starts at 1). Constraints are indicated as follows:0: Constraint1: No constraint

methods.name: getdirections
methods.digest: Report the direction for a specified column
methods.description: The word getdirections, followed by a number that specifies a column in the live.grid display, will send a list consisting of the column number followed by the direction out the fourth (dumpout) outlet (column numbering starts at 1). The direction is indicated as follows:-1: Backward0: Stop1: Forward

methods.name: getrow
methods.digest: Report the values for a specified row
methods.description: The word getrow, followed by a number that specifies a row in the live.grid display, will send a list consisting of the word row, a number that specifies the row index, and a list of the current row values out the fourth (dumpout) outlet (row numbering starts at 1).

methods.name: init
methods.digest: Restore and output the initial values
methods.description: Restores and outputs the initial values.

methods.name: left
methods.description: Rotate the values of all steps to the left. New steps values are sent out the second outlet.Note: The current constraints, if any, are also taken into account when altering current step values; the resulting shift might be "rounded" to the closest step.

methods.name: linkdump
methods.digest: Synchronize a live.grid object to another
methods.description: When the link attribute is set to 1, the linkdump message sends all messages required to synchronize one live.grid object to another live.grid object out the object's right outlet.

methods.name: random
methods.digest: Generate new step values or step constraints
methods.description: The word random generates new step values or step constraints, depending on the current mode. An optional second argument can be used to select a portion of the UI object to randomize:steps: Randomize the steps valuesconstraint: Randomize constraints and make sure that the steps values are correct with respect to the new constraints griddirections: Randomize directions if the direction attribute is set to 1.

methods.name: reset
methods.digest: Set the default values or clear constraints
methods.description: The word reset sets the default values or clears the constraints, depending on the current mode. An optional second argument can be used to select a portion of the UI object to reset:steps: Reset the steps values (Note: since the reset may interact with the current constraints, a given step value may not be completely reset)constraint: Clear all constraintsdirections: Set all the directions to forward if the direction attribute is set to 1.

methods.name: right
methods.description: Rotate the values of all the steps to the right. New steps values are sent out the second outlet.Note: The current constraints, if any, are also taken into account when altering current step values; the resulting shift might be "rounded" to the closest step.

methods.name: set
methods.digest: Set and display an output step without causing output
methods.description: Sets and displays the current output step without causing output.

methods.name: setcell
methods.digest: Set the value of the specified cell
methods.description: The word setcell, followed by a pair of numbers that specifies the x and y indices of a cell in the live.grid display and a number value, will set the value of the specified cell (column numbering starts at 1).

methods.name: steps
methods.digest: Set the values of all the steps at once
methods.description: Sets the values of all the steps at once. Value numbering starts at 1.

methods.name: up
methods.description: Increases (raises) the values of all steps. New steps values are sent out the second outlet.Note: The current constraints, if any, are also taken into account when altering current step values; the resulting shift might be "rounded" to the closest step.

attributes.name: bordercolor
attributes.description: Sets the border color of the live.grid object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: bordercolor2

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Toggles the display of the directions arrows.

attributes.name: direction_height

attributes.name: directioncolor

attributes.name: displayamount

attributes.name: hbgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the highlighted background color of the live.grid object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: link

m4l objects.name: chucker~
m4l objects.digest: Segment audio and reorder it on looped playback
m4l objects.description: chucker~ takes a specified amount of audio data, stores the data in an internal buffer, divides the buffered data into equal sections, and allows the sections to be reordered on playback.

inletlist.description: The right inlet of the object accepts a signal input in the range 0. - 1.0 (typically from the right outlet of a groove~ object) to control the playback of the object's buffered contents.

outletlist.digest: signal: Out left outlet: The segmented and reordered playback of the left channel of the chucker~ object's buffered contents.

outletlist.description: signal: Out middle outlet: The segmented and reordered playback of the right channel of the chucker~ object's buffered contents.
signal: Out right outlet: The current step number in the playback cycle is sent out the right outlet as a signal value.Note: This is the step number, not the index of the segment being played back.

arguments.name: buffer-size-in-ms
arguments.description: An optional integer argument can be used to set the number of milliseconds to allocate for the recorded sound. (e.g. an argument of 8000 will allocate enough memory for a stereo output of 8 seconds)Note: The actual allocation will be larger than what is specified by the argument, since the chucker~ object supports two buffers and provides for double-buffering.

methods.name: directions
methods.description: The word directions, followed by a 1 or 2 to indicate left or right channel and a list of integer values whose length is equal to the number of steps, sets the direction of playback for the sections. Playback direction is specified as follows:1: forward (the default)0: mute-1: reverse

methods.name: fademode
methods.description: Sets the fade method for segment smoothing. Modes include:0: Classic (same as Max 5)1: Pre-fade (fades use buffered audio, fade executes prior to segment transition)2: Post-fade (fades use buffered audio, fade executes after segment transition)

methods.name: freeze
methods.digest: Loop the current buffer segment on playback
methods.description: The message freeze 1 causes the current buffer segment to loop on playback. Sending the message freeze 0 resumes normal playback.

methods.name: nstep
methods.digest: Set the number of buffer segments
methods.description: The word nsteps, followed by an integer in the range 1 - 64, sets the number of equal portions into which the chucker~ object's internal buffer is segmented for playback.

methods.name: signal
methods.description: In left inlet: Left channel audio input.In middle inlet: Right channel audio input.In right inlet: An audio signal in the range 0. - 1.0 provides the audio sync input. This task is typically done using a phasor~ object's output as input.

methods.name: smooth
methods.digest: Set a crossfade amount between segments
methods.description: The word smooth, followed by a floating point number in the range 0. - 1.0, sets an amount of smoothing (crossfading) between the individual segments being reordered for playback.

methods.name: steps
methods.digest: Set the playback order for the sections
methods.description: The word steps, followed by a 1 or 2 to indicate left or right channel and a list of integer values whose range is between 1 and the number of steps and whose length is equal to the number of steps, sets the order of playback for the sections.e.g. the message steps 1 4 3 2 1, steps 2 1 2 3 4, when sent to a chucker~ object whose number of steps is set to 4, will play the four left channel segments in reverse order, and the right channel in regular order. order

The button's color (set using the circlecolor and circleoncolor attributes found in the object Inspector)
methods.description: To drop a file, click on the name of an audio file or its icon in the Live application's file browser, drag it onto the live.drop object's display area, and release the mouse button.When the mouse is positioned over the live.drop object, a round button will appear in the lower right-hand portion of the object's display. methods.name: set

methods.description: The word set, followed by a list that specifies a filepath, sets a filepath to be reported by the the live.drop when it is initialized. The set message allows you to store a filepath as reported by the object in the parameter and display and output the path as if a file had been manually dropped on the object.

attributes.name: annotation_name

attributes.description: When enabled (default), the live.drop object will attempt to decode non-PCM-audio files dropped on it from Live's file browser (for instance, .mp3, .mp4, .m4v, .mov, .flac, etc.). Decoded files will be cached to a temporary directory on the computer's hard drive. In this case, the filename and path passed out of the object's outlets will refer to the temporary decoded file, not to the original. This feature is limited to file types which Live can decode.You might wish to disable decodemode if you are using the live.drop object to read, for instance, movie files for use in jit.movie or if you otherwise need the original file data, rather than extracted audio from the dragged file.

attributes.name: legend

m4l objects.name: live.thisdevice
m4l objects.digest: Send a bang automatically when a Max Device is loaded, report device state
m4l objects.description: live.thisdevice reports three pieces of information about your Max Device. A bang message is automatically sent from the left outlet when the Max Device is opened and completely initialized, or when the containing patcher is part of another file that is opened. Additionally, a bang will be reported every time a new preset is loaded or the device is saved (and thus reloaded within the Live application). A 1 or 0 will be sent from the middle outlet when the Device is enabled or disabled, respectively. A 1 or 0 will be sent from the right outlet when preview mode for the Device is enabled or disabled, respectively. Used within Max, live.thisdevice functions essentially like the loadbang object. The middle and right outlets are inactive in this case.

m4l objects.name: live.modulate~
m4l objects.digest: Modulate Ableton Live and Max for Live Parameters
m4l objects.description: The live.modulate~ object enables you to modulate the value of Live parameters in realtime using signal objects. To understand more about Live's parameters, look up the DeviceParameter Object Class in the Live Object Model.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Send a value to the selected Live Parameter
methods.description: An integer number value received in the left inlet will be applied to the selected Live parameter (DeviceParameter Object), if any, at the beginning of the next audio buffer, or at the end of a pending ramp (see smoothing).

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Send a decimal value to the selected Live Parameter
methods.description: A floating point number value received in the left inlet will be applied to the selected Live parameter (DeviceParameter Object), if any, at the beginning of the next audio buffer, or at the end of a pending ramp (see smoothing).

methods.name: list
methods.description: Start a ramp with a list of two floats, similar to the line~ object. Sending in “1 500” means that the value 1 will be reached in 500 ms, starting at the current value. New ramps will always override the current ramp, so if you want to cut short a ramp, send another value.

methods.name: getid
methods.description: The mapped object's id is sent from the outlet, preceded by the word id. If there is no mapped object, id 0 will be sent.

methods.name: id
methods.digest: Set the Live object using it's id nn
methods.description: In right inlet: Sets the selected Live object. The message has no effect if the id is not a parameter (DeviceParameter Object).

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Send signal values to the selected Live Parameter
methods.description: Signal input values received in the left inlet will be applied to the selected parameter (DeviceParameter Object), if any, in realtime.

attributes.name: depth
attributes.description: The live.modulate~ object has an input range of -1 to 1 which maps onto the full range of the modulated parameter.You can control the depth of the modulation with the depth attribute. In other words, you can constrain the modulation to a smaller amount than the full range, expressed as a depth amount between 0 and 1.

attributes.name: smoothing
attributes.description: Set the ramp time that is used for each incoming event. This also performs an automatic downsampling of any signal you send in. For example, a smoothing value of 1 ms will downsample the signal to 1 ms and send ramp events which output a linear approximation of the initial signal. This attribute defaults to 1 ms.

m4l objects.name: ddg.mono
m4l objects.digest: Monophonic Synth Controller for Virtual Synths
m4l objects.description: ddg.mono provides MIDI message handling for virtual monophonic synths in Max. It implements last/high/low note priority and legato/retrigger phrasing.

arguments.name: note priority
arguments.description: An optional integer argument in the range 0 - 2 can be used to specify note priority. The mode settings are:mode 0 (retrigger): Retrigger on each keypress (default).mode 1 (legato): When a note is held, new notes ignore velocity.mode 2 (laststep): Send a noteoff message on last note only.

methods.name: int
methods.description: In first inlet: The number is treated as a pitch value for a MIDI note-on message. Output of the received number and its corresponding velocity value is dependent on the mode attribute and the triggering modes (set using the legato or retrig messages).In second inlet: The number is stored as a velocity to be paired with pitch numbers received in the left inlet.

methods.name: clear
methods.description: The clear message will send a note-off message to stop any notes which are currently playing.

methods.name: in1
methods.digest: Store as a velocity to pair with pitch values
methods.description: In right inlet: The number is stored as a velocity to be paired with pitch numbers received in the left inlet.

methods.name: laststep
methods.digest: Send a note-off for the last note played
methods.description: The laststep message will cause the ddg.mono object to send a note-off message for the last note played.

methods.name: legato
methods.digest: Send output only when a new note is played
methods.description: The legato message will cause the ddg.mono object to send its output only when a new note is played.

methods.name: retrig
methods.digest: Send output on each key press (retrigger)
methods.description: The retrig message will cause the ddg.mono object to send its output on each key press (i.e., retriggering previously played notes).

attributes.name: legatomode
attributes.description: Sets the legato mode.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Sets the note priority mode.

m4l objects.name: midiselect
m4l objects.digest: Select and interpret raw MIDI data
m4l objects.description: midiselect receives raw MIDI bytes and separates the input stream. MIDI data to be selected for output is set using object attributes. There is a separate data outlet associated with each MIDI data selection attribute. Any input data which is unselected will be sent out the object's eighth outlet.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: bang
methods.description: Clears the midiselect object's memory of any partial MIDI messages received up to that point.

methods.name: int
methods.description: Numbers received in the inlet (usually from a seq or midiin object) are treated as bytes of a MIDI message. The status byte and the filtering attributes determine the outlet which will be used to output the data bytes.

methods.name: float
methods.description: Floating-point numbers received in the inlet are converted to integer values and treated as bytes of a MIDI message. The status byte and the filtering attributes determine the outlet which will be used to output the data bytes.

attributes.name: bend
attributes.description: When then bend attribute is set to 1, Pitch Bend information is sent out the 6th outlet, otherwise the Pitch Bend is sent out the 8th outlet as raw MIDI Data.

attributes.name: ch
attributes.description: The ch attribute allows you to specify which MIDI input channels will be selected. While you can choose input from all channels by instantiating the midiselect object the the argument @ch all, you can also select specific channels (e.g., the argument @ch 1 3 5 will only select MIDI information on the first, third and fifth channels).

attributes.name: ctl
attributes.description: The ctl attribute allows you to specify which MIDI controller messages will be selected. By default, no controlers are selected. You can select specific controlers to be filtered (e.g., the argument @ctl 7 9 64 will select the controler 7 (Volume), 9 (Pan), 64 (Sustain Pedal)). To select all controllers, use the argument @ctl all. To select no controllers (the default), use @ctl none.

attributes.name: hires
attributes.description: An integer in the range 0 - 2 sets the range used for pitch bend messages by the midiparse object.

attributes.name: note
attributes.description: The note attribute allows you to specify which MIDI note messages will be selected. By default, no notes are selected. You can select specific notes to be filtered (e.g., @note 60 64 67 will select the C4, E4, G4 notes). To select all notes, use the argument @note all. To select no notes (the default), use @note none.

attributes.name: pgm
attributes.description: When then pgm attribute is set to 1, Program Change information is sent out the 4th outlet. Otherwise, the Program Change is sent out the 8th outlet as raw MIDI Data.

attributes.name: poly
attributes.description: The poly attribute allows you to specify which MIDI poly pressure will be selected. By default, no poly pressure is selected. You can select specific notes to be filtered (e.g., @poly 60 64 67 will select the C4, E4, G4 notes). To select all the notes, use the argument @poly all. To select no notes (the default) use @poly none.

attributes.name: touch
attributes.description: When then touch attribute is set to 1, After touch data is sent out the 5th outlet. Otherwise, the Aftertouch is sent out the 8th outlet as raw MIDI Data.

m4l objects.name: live.observer
m4l objects.digest: Monitor changes in Live objects
m4l objects.description: live.observer    is used to listen to changes in the values of properties of Live    objects. This object works in conjunction with the     live.path     object, which sends            id       nn         messages into the right inlet of     live.observer     .              After an object id and property is specified, its value is sent out the    left outlet. From this moment on, the value is sent on each change of the    property ('notification') as well as in response to bang messages.              The left outlet is reserved for value messages, all other output is sent to    the right outlet.              Not all properties can be observed, please consult the      Live Object Model      to see which can. Also, it is not possible to modify the live set from a    notification, i.e. while you are receiving a value message spontaneously    sent by a     live.observer     's outlet.              Besides properties, it is also possible to observer children of Live    objects. Their values are object ids or lists of them.        Note: The Live API runs in the main thread in Live, and that all messages to and from the API are automatically deferred.

arguments.name: property

methods.description: Arguments:                           child                 the name of a child list of the current object                          Operation:                  Selects the child list to be observed. Outputs the id list (or nothing)        to the left outlet if the selected Live object has such a list child.                          Remark:                  Not all child lists can be observed.                                               Outlet            Output            Example                                left                                           id                 nn                 ... id                 mm                                                    id 4 id 5

methods.description: Operation:                  Sends the name of the selected property (or child resp. list-child) out        the right outlet.
