m4l objects.name: live.step
m4l objects.digest: Step Sequencer UI object
m4l objects.description: live.step displays multiple sequences which have multiple steps composed of pitch, velocity, and duration. Two additional steps (Extra 1 and Extra 2) are available for user-defined display.

outletlist.digest: Step Values (Index Pitch, Velocity, Duration, Extra1, Extra2)

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: bang
methods.description: If the target_seq attribute is set to zero, a bang message will send the values associated with the current step of all sequences out the object's left outlet. If the target_seq attribute is set to a value greater than zero, a bang message will send the values associated with the current step of the currently specified sequence out the object's left outlet.

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Set the current step for all sequences
methods.description: If the target_seq attribute is set to zero, an integer sets the current step of all sequences to the corresponding integer (index numbering starts at 1). If the target_seq attribute is set to a value greater than zero, an integer sets the current step of the currently specified sequence. The values associated with the current step are sent out the object's left outlet.

methods.name: active
methods.description: If the target_seq attribute is set to zero, the message active 0 deactivates all sequences. The word active, followed by any non-zero value, will activate all sequences.If the target_seq attribute is set to a value greater than zero, the message active 0 deactivates the specified sequence. The word active, followed by any non-zero value, will activate the specified sequence.

methods.name: copy
methods.digest: Copy all or a part of a sequence
methods.description: The word copy will copy the entire sequence. One or two optional integer arguments may be used to specify starting and ending indices (index numbering starts at 1). For example, copy 2 will copy the sequence starting at index 2, while copy 2 5 will copy starting at index 2 and ending at index 5.

methods.name: dictionary
methods.description: Replaces the current sequence or all sequences of live.step by the content of a named dictionary.  If multiple sequences are present in the dictionary, every sequences is replaced.

methods.name: direction
methods.digest: Set the playback direction for sequences
methods.description: The word direction followed by an integer in the range 0-4, sets the playback direction for sequence playback. The playback options are:0: forward1: backward2: back and forth3: Rotate4: randomIf the target_seq attribute is set to zero, the integer argument sets the direction of all sequences when live.step object's playback is controlled using the time message.If the target_seq attribute is set to a value greater than zero, an integer sets the direction of the specified sequence when live.step object's playback is controlled using the time message.

methods.name: doedit
methods.digest: Move or rotate stored sequence data
methods.description: The word doedit, followed by a number in the range 0-4, provides a simple means to move or rotate the parameters stored in the live.step object. The modes specified by the number arguments are:0: transpose the pitch upward.1: transpose the pitch downward.2: Rotate the steps to the left.3: Rotate the steps to the right4: Randomize steps depending on the mode attribute. For instance, if the mode is set to velocity, doedit 4 will only randomize the velocity.For more advanced editing features, use the up, down, left, right, random, scramble, and sort messages.

methods.name: down
methods.digest: Decreases the values of a sequence based on target_seq and mode attributes
methods.description: The word down will decreases the values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the down message will only decrease the velocity of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).An optional argument may be used with the down message to specify the parameters to be decreased without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: decrease all parameterspitch: transpose pitches downwardvelocity: decrease velocitiesduration: decrease durationsextra1: decrease values for the user-definable Extra 1 parameterextra2: decrease values for the user-definable Extra 2 parameter

methods.name: dump
methods.description: Sends the values (pitch, velocity, duration, extra1, extra2) of all steps of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's right outlet.

methods.name: dump_to_dict
methods.description: Sends out a dictionary of the current sequence or all sequences (if target_seq is set to 0), via the dump outlet.

methods.name: duration
methods.digest: Set duration values for the current sequence
methods.description: The word duration, followed by an integer that specifies a starting index into a sequence (index numbering starts with 1) and a list of values (in ticks), will set the duration values for the current sequence specified by the target_seq attribute.

methods.name: extra1
methods.digest: Set extra1 values for the current sequence
methods.description: The word extra1, followed by an integer that specifies a starting index into a sequence (index numbering starts with 1) and a list of values, will set the extra1 values for the current sequence specified by the target_seq attribute.

methods.name: extra2
methods.digest: Set extra2 values for the current sequence
methods.description: The word extra2, followed by an integer that specifies a starting index into a sequence (index numbering starts with 1) and a list of values, will set the extra2 values for the current sequence specified by the target_seq attribute.

methods.name: fetch
methods.digest: Report parameter values for a step in the sequence
methods.description: The word fetch, followed by a symbol that specifies a step parameter (pitch, velocity, duration, extra1, or extra2) and an integer that specifies a step number, will send a list out of the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form <parameter-name> <step-number> <value>.

methods.name: fold
methods.description: The word fold, followed by a 0 or 1, toggles the folded display mode. When folding is enabled, the live.step object only displays those pitches which are present in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute rather than all possible pitches. Fold mode displays only the pitches specific to each individual sequence.Note: Sequence editing messages such as up, down, and random use the list of pitches displayed in fold state when performing operations (i.e., the random message will only choose randomly from among the pitches displayed on fold mode. These operations are also dependent on the target sequence, as well). for all sequences.

methods.name: fold_pitch
methods.digest: Set pitches to be displayed in fold mode
methods.description: The word fold_pitch, followed by an integer or list of integers that specify MIDI note numbers, sets the pitches to be displayed by the live.step object in fold mode. As with the fold message, the fold_pitch message sets pitches to be displayed in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute.

methods.name: getactive
methods.digest: Report the active state of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getactive will send the active state of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word active.

methods.name: getcurrentstep
methods.digest: Report the current step of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getcurrentstep will send the current step of the sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a number preceded by the word currentstep. When working with multiple sequences, the getcurrentstep message will report the current step of the targeted sequence (specified by the target_seq attribute).

methods.name: getdirection
methods.digest: Report the direction state of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getdirection will send the direction state of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word direction.

methods.name: getduration
methods.digest: Report all duration values in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getduration will send a list of all the duration values in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word duration.

methods.name: getextra1
methods.digest: Report all extra1 values in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getextra1 will send a list of all the extra1 values in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word extra1.

methods.name: getextra2
methods.digest: Report all extra2 values in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getextra2 will send a list of all the extra2 values in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word extra2.

methods.name: getinterval
methods.digest: Report the interval of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getinterval will send the interval of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word interval.

methods.name: getloop
methods.digest: Report the loop points in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getloop will send the loop points of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word loop.

methods.name: getmodelist
methods.description: The message getmodelist will send the list of the display modes out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word modelist.

methods.name: getnstep
methods.digest: Report the number of steps in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getnstep will send the number of steps in the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word nstep.

methods.name: getpitch
methods.digest: Report all pitch values in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getpitch will send a list of all the pitch values in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word pitch.

methods.name: getstep
methods.digest: Report all parameter values for a sequence step
methods.description: The message getstep will send a list of the values (pitch, velocity, duration, extra1, extra2) of the specified index of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word step.

methods.name: getvelocity
methods.digest: Report all velocity values in the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getvelocity will send a list of all the velocity values in the sequence specified by the target_seq attribute out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word velocity.

methods.name: getzoom
methods.digest: Report the zoom pitch values of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The message getzoom will send the zoom pitch values of the currently specified sequence out the live.step object's fourth (dumpout) outlet in the form of a list preceded by the word zoom.

methods.name: init
methods.digest: Restore and output the initial values entered when Initial Enabled is checked in the live.step object's Inspector
methods.description: Restores and outputs the initial values entered when Initial Enabled is checked in the live.step object's Inspector.

methods.name: interval
methods.digest: Set the interval of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: Sets the interval of the currently specified sequence.

methods.name: left
methods.digest: Left-shift the sequence values based on the target_seq and mode attributes
methods.description: The word left will rotate (left-shift) the values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the left message will only rotate the velocity of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).An optional argument may be used with the left message to specify the parameters to be rotated without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: Rotate all parameters to the leftpitch: Rotate all pitches to the leftvelocity: Rotate all velocities to the leftduration: Rotate all durations to the leftextra1: Rotate all user-definable Extra 1 parameters to the leftextra2: Rotate all user-definable Extra 2 parameters to the left

methods.name: loop
methods.digest: Set loop points for the currently specified sequence
methods.description: The word loop, followed by two numbers that specify starting and ending indices, sets the loop points of the currently specified sequence.

methods.name: (mouse)
methods.description: Whenever the live.step object is edited using the mouse, the message changed followed by a number in the range 0-2 will be sent out the object's dumpout outlet. The number specifies what portion of the live.step display has been modified, as follows:0: The pitch, velocity, duration, extra1, or extra2 settings have been modified.1: The looping portion of the UI has been modified.2: Edits have been made in the ruler area of the UI.

methods.name: next
methods.digest: Report the values for the next step in the sequences
methods.description: The next message will send the values associated with the next step of all sequences out the object's left outlet. If the target_seq attribute is set to a value greater than zero, a next message will send the values associated with the next step of the currently specified sequence out the object's left outlet.

methods.name: nstep
methods.digest: Set the number of steps in the target sequence
methods.description: Sets the number of steps in the target sequence.

methods.name: paste
methods.description: When the paste message is received without argument, all parameters are pasted at the same location as they were copied. An optional argument to specify parameter type (pitch, velocity, duration, extra1, extra2) can be used to paste only specific items. An additional option number argument specifies the starting index where the copied steps will be pasted (index numbering starts at 1).

methods.name: pitch
methods.digest: Set pitch values for the current sequence
methods.description: The word pitch, followed by an integer that specifies a starting index into a sequence (index numbering starts with 1) and a list of values, will set the pitch values for the current sequence specified by the target_seq attribute.

methods.name: random
methods.description: The word random will randomize the values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the random message will only scramble the velocity of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).An optional argument may be used with the random message to specify the parameters to be scrambled without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: Randomize all parameterspitch: Randomize all pitchesvelocity: Randomize all velocitiesduration: Randomize all durationsextra1: Randomize all values for the user-definable Extra 1 parameterextra2: Randomize all values for the user-definable Extra 2 parameter

methods.name: reset
methods.description: The reset message allows you to deactivate the current step. It is equivalent to setting the current step to 0.

methods.name: right
methods.digest: Right-shift the sequence values based on the target_seq and mode attributes
methods.description: The word right will rotate (right-shift) the values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the left message will only rotate the velocity of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).An optional argument may be used with the right message to specify the parameters to be rotated without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: Rotate all parameters to the rightpitch: Rotate all pitches to the rightvelocity: Rotate all velocities to the rightduration: Rotate all durations to the rightextra1: Rotate all values for the user-definable Extra 1 parameter to the rightextra2: Rotate all values for the user-definable Extra 2 parameter to the right

methods.name: scramble
methods.digest: Randomize the order of sequence values based on target_seq and mode attributes
methods.description: The word scramble will randomize the order of the values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the left message will only scramble the velocity of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).An optional argument may be used with the scramble message to specify the parameters to be scrambled without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: Randomize the order of all parameterspitch: Randomize the order of all pitchesvelocity: Randomize the order of all velocitiesduration: Randomize the order of all durationsextra1: Randomize the order of all user-definable Extra 1 parametersextra2: Randomize the order of all user-definable Extra 2 parametersIf you are not using mode all, and that you pass 1 as argument, scramble will keep your steps synchronized. For instance, the scramble pitch 1 message will reorder the pitches, but the other parameters will follow.

methods.name: set
methods.digest: Set the current step of all the sequences
methods.description: If the target_seq attribute is set to zero, the word set, followed by an integer sets the current step of all the sequences to the corresponding integer (index numbering starts at 1).If the target_seq attribute is set to a value greater than zero, the word set, followed by an integer sets the current step of the currently specified sequence.

methods.name: setall
methods.digest: Set a value for all layers in the current sequence
methods.description: The word setall, followed by a number, will assign that value to every layer in the currently targeted sequence when the the live.step object is in display mode. An optional first argument specifying a specific layer (i.e. setall velocity 85) can be used to set all values in a specify layer. When the editlooponly attribute is set to 1, the setall message will only be applied to indices inside the loop selection.

methods.name: settimeshift
methods.digest: Move to a sequence step relative to the current step
methods.description: The word settimeshift, followed by a positive or negative number that specifies an offset, will move to the relative position from the current step in the sequence and first that step (e.g., sending the message settimeshift -1 when the current step number is 3 will cause the content of step 2 to fire.

methods.name: sort
methods.digest: Sort step values of a sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes
methods.description: The word sort will sort the step values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the sort message will only sort the velocity values of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).Optional arguments may be used with the sort message to specify behavior, synchronization, and direction of sortint. The can be used to set the parameters to be sorted without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: Sort the order of all parameterspitch: Sort the order of the pitchesvelocity: Sort the order of the velocitiesduration: Sort the order of the durationsextra1: Sort the order of all user-definable Extra 1 parametersextra2: Sort the order of all user-definable Extra 2 parametersThe first integer argument specifies whether or not to keep the step values synchronized - it only works if the mode attribute is not set to all. For instance, the message sort pitch 1 will reorder the steps based on the pitch, but the velocity, duration and user-definable extra1 and extra2 values associated to the pitch will be maintained. An optional second integer argument can be used to set the sorting order:1: Ascending (the default) -1: Descending.

methods.name: step
methods.digest: Set the values for a sequence step
methods.description: The word step, followed by a list of four integers, sets the values of a specific step. The required arguments are:the index (index numbering starts at 1)the MIDI note number (0-127)the note velocity (0-127)the duration (30, 60, 120, 240, 480, 960, 1920, 3840 ticks)

methods.name: time
methods.digest: Specify the timing position in the sequence.
methods.description: The word time, followed by a list of 6 numbers, defines the timing position in the sequence. The required arguments are bar, beat, unit, resolution-in-ppq, time-signature-numerator, and time-signature-denominator. The live.step object does not have an internal clock, so you need to send the time message often if you want to use it to drive the live.step object.

methods.name: up
methods.digest: Increase values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes
methods.description: The word up will increase the values of the sequence based on the target_seq and mode attributes. For instance, if the mode attribute is set to velocity, the up message will only increase the velocity of the currently specified sequence (or all the sequences if the target_seq attribute is set to zero).An optional argument may be used with the up message to specify the parameters to be increased without having to use the mode attribute. The optional arguments are:all: Increase all parameterspitch: Transpose pitches upwardvelocity: Increase velocitiesduration: Increase durationsextra1: Increase the value of all user-definable Extra 1 parametersextra2: Increase the value of all user-definable Extra 2 parameters

methods.name: velocity
methods.digest: Set velocity values for the current sequence
methods.description: The word velocity, followed by an integer that specifies a starting index into a sequence (index numbering starts with 1) and a list of values, will set the velocity values for the current sequence specified by the target_seq attribute.

methods.name: zoom
methods.digest: Sets the the upper and lower displayed range of the currently specified sequence
methods.description: Sets the the upper and lower displayed range of the currently specified sequence.

methods.name: zoom_fit
methods.digest: Set the pitch display ranges based on low/high note values
methods.description: The word zoom_fit will cause the currently displayed pitch range of the live.step object to adjust so that the highest and lowest note values become the upper and lower limits of the display.

methods.name: zoom_in
methods.digest: Decrease the displayed pitch range by 7 steps
methods.description: The word zoom_in will cause the current pitch range of the live.step object display to decrease by a factor of a fifth (7 steps) at the top and bottom, resulting in a "zoom in" effect.

methods.name: zoom_out
methods.digest: Increase the displayed pitch range by 7 steps
methods.description: The word zoom_out will cause the current pitch range of the live.step object display to increase by a factor of a fifth (7 steps) at the top and bottom, resulting in a "zoom out" effect.

attributes.name: annotation_name
attributes.description: The string that is prepended to annotations. This shows up in the Info pane in Live, and the clue window in Max.

attributes.name: autoscroll
attributes.description: When set to 1, this attribute lets you expand the scrolling dragging the cursor to the edge of the display or to drag a selected pitch beyond the range of the current visual display.

attributes.name: bgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the background color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: bgcolor2
attributes.description: Sets the second background color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: bgrulercolor
attributes.description: Sets the ruler background color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: bgunitcolor
attributes.description: Sets the unit background color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: blackkeycolor
attributes.description: Sets the color for the upper (black) keys in RGBA format.

attributes.name: bordercolor
attributes.description: Sets the border color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: display_seq
attributes.description: Sets the sequence to be displayed (index numbering starts at 1).

attributes.name: duration_active
attributes.description: Activates display of the duration layer

attributes.name: editlooponly
attributes.description: When the editlooponly attribute is set to 1, the edit messages (up, down, left, right, random, scramble, sort) are only applied to indices inside the loop selection.

attributes.name: extra1_active
attributes.description: Activates display of the user-definable extra1 layer

attributes.name: extra1_max
attributes.description: Sets the maximum value for the user-definable extra1 layer.

attributes.name: extra1_min
attributes.description: Sets the minimum value for the user-definable extra1 layer

attributes.name: extra1_signed
attributes.description: Displays the user-definable extra1 layer as Signed.

attributes.name: extra2_active
attributes.description: Activates display of the user-definable extra2 layer

attributes.name: extra2_max
attributes.description: Sets the maximum value for the user-definable extra2 layer

attributes.name: extra2_min
attributes.description: Sets the minimum value for the user-definable extra2 layer

attributes.name: extra2_signed
attributes.description: Displays the user-definable extra2 layer as Signed.

attributes.name: extra_thickness
attributes.description: Sets the thickness of the vertical bars displayed in the extra1 layer. Values should be in the range of 0. (invisible) to 1.0 (full width).

attributes.name: hbgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the highlight background color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: loopbordercolor
attributes.description: Sets the loop border color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: loopruler
attributes.description: Toggles the display of the loop ruler.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: An integer or symbol can be used to set the information display mode of the live.step object.

attributes.name: nseq
attributes.description: Defines the number of sequences.

attributes.name: pitch_active
attributes.description: Activates display of the pitch layer

attributes.name: stepcolor
attributes.description: Sets the step color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: stepcolor2
attributes.description: Sets the second step color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: target_seq
attributes.description: Defines the sequence to be edited (index numbering starts at 1).

attributes.name: textcolor
attributes.description: Sets the text color of the live.step object in RGBA format.

attributes.name: unitruler
attributes.description: Toggles the display of the unit ruler.

attributes.name: usestepcolor2
attributes.description: Toggles the use of a second step color in the display

attributes.name: velocity_active
attributes.description: Activates display of the Velocity layer

attributes.name: whitekeycolor
attributes.description: Sets the color for the lower level (white) keys in RGBA format.

m4l objects.name: live.meter~
m4l objects.digest: Live-style visual peak level indicator
m4l objects.description: live.meter~ is a simple mono Live-style signal level meter that can be attached to any signal whose level is between -1 and 1 (other signals should be scaled first).

outletlist.description: Peak Value For Each Metering Interval

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: int
methods.description: Converted to float.

methods.name: float
methods.description: When no signal is connected to the live.meter~ object's inlet, a float number will set the meter to react as though a signal with equal amplitude peak-value has been passed to its input. Corresponding LEDs will light up and the peak-level value will be passed out the outlet (0.0 will show silence, 0.0 through 1.0 will light up to any but the overload LED, and anything above 1.0 will light all LEDs including overload).

methods.name: db
methods.description: The word db, followed by a floating point number that specficies a deciBel value, will set the live.meter~ object to react as though a signal with that dB peak-value has been passed to its input. Corresponding LEDs will light up and the value will be passed out the outlet.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Display peak amplitude of the signal
methods.description: The peak amplitude of the incoming signal is displayed by the on-screen level meter.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: Enables (1) or disables (0) the meter display.

attributes.name: bgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the background color in RGBA format.

attributes.name: clip_size
attributes.description: Sets the clipping range for the display. The options are Normal or Extended.

attributes.name: coldcolor
attributes.description: Sets the Cold signal color in RGBA format.

attributes.name: display_range
attributes.description: Sets the display range of the meter in dB.

attributes.name: hotcolor
attributes.description: Sets the Warning signal color in RGBA format.

attributes.name: inactivecoldcolor
attributes.description: Sets the Cold signal (inactive) color in RGBA format.

attributes.name: inactivewarmcolor
attributes.description: Sets the Warm signal (inactive) color in RGBA format.

attributes.name: interval
attributes.digest: Sets the maximum update-time interval, in milliseconds, of the live.meter~ display.
attributes.description: Sets the maximum update-time interval, in milliseconds, of the live.meter~ display. The minimum update-interval is 10 milliseconds, the maximum is 2 seconds, and the default is 50 milliseconds. This message also sets the rate at which meter~ sends out the peak value received in that time interval. Thethreshold_dborthreshold_linearattributes are used to limit the refresh and the output, depending on the setting of themodeattribute.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Sets the display and output mode of the live.meter~ object.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Sets the orientation of the meter display. The options are Horizontal or Vertical

attributes.name: overloadcolor
attributes.description: Sets the Overload signal color in RGBA format.

attributes.name: threshold_db
attributes.description: When the live.meter~ object'smodeattribute is set to 0, this attribute sets the refresh threshold in deciBels. If the signal peak delta is greater than the threshold value, the object will be redrawn and the value sent out the outlet.

attributes.name: threshold_linear
attributes.description: When the live.meter~ object'smodeattribute is set to 1, this attribute sets the refresh threshold in deciBels. If the signal peak delta is greater than the threshold value, the object will be redrawn and the value sent out the outlet.

attributes.name: warmcolor
attributes.description: Sets the Warm signal color in RGBA format.

m4l objects.name: live.remote~
m4l objects.digest: Realtime control of parameters in Ableton Live and Max for Live.
m4l objects.description: Thelive.remote~ object allows you to remotely control parameters in Ableton Live and Max for Live in realtime.  To understand more about Live's parameters, look up the DeviceParameter Object Class in the Live Object Model .

methods.name: float
methods.digest: Send a decimal value to the selected Live Parameter
methods.description: A floating point number value received in the left inlet will beapplied to the selected Live parameter (DeviceParameter Object), if any, at the beginning of the next audio buffer, or at the end of a pending ramp (see smoothing).

methods.name: int
methods.digest: Send a value to the selected Live Parameter
methods.description: An integer number value received in the left inlet will be applied tothe selected Live parameter (DeviceParameter Object), if any, at the beginning of the next audio buffer, or at the end of a pending ramp (see smoothing).

methods.name: list
methods.description: Start a ramp with a list of two floats, similar to the line~ object. Sending in “1 500” means that the value 1 will be reached in 500 ms, starting at the current value. New ramps will always override the current ramp, so if you want to cut short a ramp, send another value.

methods.name: signal
methods.digest: Send signal values to the selected Live Parameter
methods.description: Signal input values received in the left inlet will be applied to theselected parameter (DeviceParameter Object), if any, in realtime.

methods.name: id
methods.digest: Set the Live object using it's id nn
methods.description: In right inlet: Sets the selected object. The message hasno effect if the id is not a parameter (DeviceParameter Object).

methods.name: getid
methods.description: The mapped object's id is sent from the outlet, preceded by the word id. If there is no mapped object, id 0 will be sent.

attributes.name: smoothing
attributes.description: Set the ramp time that is used for each incoming event. This also performs a temporal downsampling of any signal you send in. For example, a smoothing value of 1 ms will sample the incoming signal every 1 ms and send ramp events which output a linear approximation of the signal. This attribute defaults to 1 ms.

attributes.name: normalized
attributes.digest: Automatically scale the input values to the parameter range
attributes.description: Toggles thelive.remote~object's normalized mode, which automatically scales the input values to the target parameter range. When the normalized attribute is set to 1, sending a signal or values in the range 0 to 1 to live.remote~ will automatically scale the values to the range of the receiving parameter. If the normalized attribute is set to 0, automatic scaling is disabled. You will need to provide values between the minimum and maximum of the parameter in order to control it.

m4l objects.name: live.colors
m4l objects.digest: Get the colors of the active Ableton Live Theme via a Max for Live device.
m4l objects.description: Get the dynamic colors from the active Ableton Live application color theme and use these color names to ensure compatibility between various Max objects and Ableton Live themes. These colors adapt dynamically to the active Live theme, eliminating the need to change RGBA values, since each color name is a token that references specific colors across Live themes.In Max 8.2 or later, you can change a Max object's color by setting dynamic colors using the color picker in the Max object's inspector window, instead of using live.colors.

outletlist.digest: Color in RGBA Format (float numbers from 0. to 1.)
Bang when the Live colors change

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: anything
methods.digest: The dynamic color name in Live
methods.description: Sends the color for Color Name from the live.colors object's left outlet in RGBA format (float numbers from 0. to 1.).

methods.name: everything
methods.digest: Report all current color RGBA values as a series of messages.
methods.description: Sends all the available colors out the outlet as a series of messages. Each message consists of the color id followed by four floating-point values that describe the color scheme color in RGBA format (float numbers from 0. to 1.).

m4l objects.name: paraminspector
m4l objects.digest: TEXT_HERE
m4l objects.description: TEXT_HERE

attributes.name: _parameter_order
attributes.description: Sets the order of recall of this parameter. Lower numbers are recalled        first. The order of recall of parameters with the same order number is        undefined.

attributes.name: _parameter_path
attributes.description: This feature is debug-build only, so you will never see this message.        If you insist, this is the moniker path to the parameter object from the        top-level of the patcher hierarchy.

attributes.name: _parameter_linknames
attributes.digest: Link Parameter Name to Scripting Name
attributes.description: When checked, the Scripting Name is linked to the Long Name attribute.

attributes.name: _parameter_longname
attributes.description: The long name of the parameter. This name must be unique per patcher        hierarchy.

attributes.name: _parameter_shortname
attributes.description: The short name of the parameter. This name is used for display in the        user interface.

attributes.name: _parameter_scriptname
attributes.description: The scripting name of the object. This name must be unique per patcher.

attributes.name: _parameter_type
attributes.description: The type of the parameter. In general, this will be Int (0-255), Float        (32-bit float), Enum (enumerated list of values) or Blob (list). Some        parameters do not support certain parameter types, in which case those        types will be unavailable in the drop-down menu.

attributes.name: _parameter_range
attributes.description: The range of the parameter (for Int and Float types), or the members of        the enumerated list (for Enum types). Range is unsupported for Blob        parameters.

attributes.name: _parameter_modmode
attributes.description: The clip modulation mode of the parameter. Available modes depend on the        parameter's type. Clip modulation is unsupported for Enum and Blob parameter        types.

attributes.name: _parameter_modrange
attributes.description: The clip modulation range of the parameter, if modulation is enabled.

attributes.name: _parameter_initial_enable
attributes.description: If enabled, the parameter will be set to an initial value (as specified        in the Initial Value column) when the patcher or device is loaded. Turn        this on (or off, and then on again) to store the current value of the        parameter as the initial value.

attributes.name: _parameter_initial
attributes.description: The parameter's initial value, if the Initial Value Enabled checkbox is        enabled.

attributes.name: _parameter_units
attributes.description: The string to use when displaying the parameter's value, if "Unit        Style" is set to 'Custom'. Simple symbols or sprintf-style strings may        be used.

attributes.name: _parameter_unitstyle
attributes.description: Parameters have a number of built-in display styles for their data.        Choose between them from the drop-down menu.

attributes.name: _parameter_exponent
attributes.description: When set to a value other than 1., the parameter's input and output        values will be exponentially scaled according to the factor entered in        this column.

attributes.name: _parameter_steps
attributes.description: The number of steps available between the minimum and maximum values of        a parameter. For instance, if the parameter has a range from 0.-64.,        with Steps set to 4, the user can only set the parameter to 0, 21.33,        42.66 and 64.

attributes.name: _parameter_units
attributes.description: The string to use when displaying the parameter's value, if "Unit        Style" is set to 'Custom'. Simple symbols or sprintf-style strings may        be used.

attributes.name: _parameter_lval
attributes.description: For Int, Float and Enum types, the linear value (without exponential        scaling) of the parameter.

attributes.name: _parameter_mval
attributes.description: The parameter's value.

attributes.name: _parameter_invisible
attributes.description: For automatable parameters (Int, Float, Enum), 'Stored Only' disables        automation, although parameter values are stored in presets. 'Hidden'        causes the parameter's value to be ignored when storing and recalling        data. m4l objects.name: live.banks
m4l objects.digest: Manage Max for Live Device banks for Push controllers.
m4l objects.description: Create, edit and delete Max for Live Device parameter banks, as displayed on Ableton's Push controllers. Banks are saved with the device, but can be modified in real-time to cause updates on the Push display. For instance, you might want to reveal or hide particular parameters within a bank depending on device state.

arguments.name: OBJARG_NAME
arguments.description: TEXT_HERE

methods.name: (mouse)
methods.digest: Double-click to open the Parameter Banks window.
methods.description: Double-click to open the Parameter Banks window. Only available in the editor, this feature is disabled inside of Live.

methods.name: delete
methods.description: Delete a parameter bank. Deleting a bank will decrement the index of the banks with higher indices.

methods.name: edit
methods.description: Edit a parameter bank, specified by bank_id (0-indexed). To change the bank name, pass a new name as bank_name, or pass - (minus) to use the existing name. The optional list of parameters should be a list of index/name pairs in the form parameter_index  parameter_name. For instance, edit 0 newname 0 foo 2 bar 4 - 5 bap would change the name of bank 0 to newname and modify parameter slot 0 to use the parameter foo, slot 2 to use the parameter bar, eliminate the parameter in slot 4, and assign slot 5 to the parameter named bap.

methods.name: getcount
methods.digest: Report the current number of banks.
methods.description: Sends the count message from the outlet, followed by the number of banks.

methods.name: getname
methods.digest: Report the name of a bank.
methods.description: Sends the name message from the outlet, followed by the index (int) and name (symbol) of the specified bank.

methods.name: getparameters
methods.digest: Report the parameters in a bank.
methods.description: Sends the parameters message from the outlet, followed by the index (int) of and a list of parameter names (symbol) in the specified bank.

methods.name: new
methods.description: Create a bank at the index specified by bank_id (0-indexed). If a bank already exists at that index, the new bank will be inserted at the specified index and all higher-indexed banks will have their indices incremented. The bank requires a name, specified by bank_name. The list of parameters should be a list of up to 8 symbols, specifying the parameter name for bank slots 0-7. A - (minus) can be used to indicate that a slot should have no parameter associated with it. Note: when creating banks, it is possible to specify indices higher than the bank count. That is, one could start with an empty set of banks and create bank 3 first. In that case, dummy banks will be created in slots 0, 1 and 2. Dummy banks are displayed with grey text in the Parameter Banks window. Editing a dummy bank will cause it to become a 'real' bank. Creating a new bank at the index occupied by a dummy bank will replace the dummy bank in-place, rather than performing an insert.

methods.name: (mouse)

methods.name: set
methods.description: Switches the live.toggle on or off without sending anything out the outlet. The word set, followed by any non-zero number, sets toggle to on; set 0 sets it to off.

attributes.name: active

attributes.name: appearance

attributes.name: bordercolor

m4l objects.name: live.path
m4l objects.digest: Navigate to objects in the Live application
m4l objects.description: live.path is used to navigate to Live objects on which the live.object, live.observer and live.remote~ objects operate. The navigation is purely path-based and is independent of the objects currently present in Live (navigating to a nonexistent path will result in the message id 0 being sent out the left and middle outputs rather than an error message).Note: The Live API runs in the main thread in Live, and that all messages to and from the API are automatically deferred.

arguments.name: initial path
arguments.description: Specify an initial path as argument to live.path, without any quotes.
